title: 'Take Up Thy Cross', the Savior Said
author: Charles W. Everest

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"Take up thy cross," the Savior said,
"If thou wouldst My disciple be;
Deny thyself, the world forsake,
And humbly follow after Me."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Take up thy cross, let not its weight Fill
thy weak spirit with alarm;
His strength shall bear thy spirit up,
And brace thy heart and nerve thine arm.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Take up thy cross, nor heed the shame,
Nor let thy foolish pride rebel;
Thy Lord for thee the cross endured,
And saved thy soul from death and hell.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Take up thy cross then in His strength,
And calmly sin's wild deluge brave,
'Twill guide thee to a better home,
It points to glory o'er the grave.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Take up thy cross and follow Christ,
Nor think til death to lay it down;
For only those who bear the cross May hope
to wear the glorious crown.

title: 'Tis Midnight and On Olive's Brow
author: William Bingham Tappan
source: 'St. Cross' John Bacchus Dykes, 1861. Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Tis midnight, and on Olive's brow The star
is dimmed that lately shone; 'Tis midnight,
in the garden now The suff'ring Savior prays
alone.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis midnight, and from all removed Immanuel
wrestles, lone, with fears;
E'en the disciple whom He loved Heeds not
his Master's grief and tears.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis midnight, from the heav'nly plains Are
borne the songs that angels know;
Unheard by mortals are the strains That
sweetly soothe the Savior's woe.

title: 'Twas On That Dark, That Doleful Night
author: Isaac Watts
source: 'St. Cross' John Bacchus Dykes, 1861. Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Twas on that dark, that doleful night When
pow'rs of earth and hell arose Against the
Son of God's delight, And friends betrayed
Him to His foes:

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before the mournful scene began,
He took the bread, and blessed, and brake:
What love through all His actions ran!
What wondrous words of grace He spake!

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
For us His flesh with nails was torn,
He bore the scourge, He felt the thorn;
And justice poured up on His head Its heavy
vengeance in our stead.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
For us His vital blood was spilt,
To buy the pardon of our guilt, When,
for black crimes of biggest size,
He gave His soul a sacrifice.

title: A Child of The King
author: Harriet E. Buell

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Father is rich in houses and lands,
He holdeth the wealth of the world in His
hands! Of rubies and diamonds of silver and
gold His coffers are full,He has riches
untold.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I'm a child of the King,
a child of the King: With Jesus my Savior
I'm a child of the King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Father's own Son, the Savior of men,
Once wander'd o'er earth as the poorest of
men, But now He is reigning forever on high,
And will give me a home in heaven by and by.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I once was an outcast stranger on earth,
A sinner by choice, and an alien by birth!
But I've been adopted,
my name's written down,An heir to a mansion,
a robe, and a crown.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A tent or a cottage, why should I care?
They're building a palace for me over there!
Tho' exiled from home, yet,
still I may sing: All glory to God,
I'm the child of a King.

title: A Great and Mighty Wonder
author: Germanus of Constantinople (634-734).  Translated by John Mason Neale
source: 'Es Ist Ein Ros Entsprungen (Rhythmic)' German from Köln, 1599.  Setting: Michael Praetorius, 1609

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A great and mighty wonder,
a full and holy cure: The virgin bears the
Infant with virgin honor pure!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Repeat the hymn again:
"To God on high be glory And peace on earth
to men!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Word becomes incarnate and yet remains
on high, And cherubim sing anthems to
shepherds from the sky.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While thus they sing your Monarch,
those bright angelic bands, Rejoice,
ye vales and mountains, ye oceans,
clap your hands.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Since all He comes to ransom,
by all be He adored, The Infant born in
Bethl'em, the Savior and the Lord.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And idol forms shall perish,
and error shall decay,
And Christ shall wield His scepter,
our Lord and God for aye.

title: A Lamb Goes Uncomplaining Forth
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'An Wasserflüssen Babylon' Wolfgang Dachstein, 1525.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A Lamb goes uncomplaining forth,
The guilt of all men bearing;
And laden with the sins of earth,
None else the burden sharing!
Goes patient on, grow weak and faint,
To slaughter led with out complaint,
That spotless life to offer;
Bears shame and stripes,
and wounds and death, Anguish and mocker y,
and saith, "Willing all this I suffer."

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This Lamb is Christ, the soul's great
Friend, The Lamb of God, our Savior;
Him God the Father chose to send To gain for
us His favor. "Go forth,
My Son," the Father saith,
"And free men from the fear of death,
From guilt and condemnation.
The wrath and stripes are hard to bear,
But by Thy Passion men shall share The fruit
of Thy salvation."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"Yea, Father, yea, most willingly I'll bear
what Thou commandest; My will conforms to
Thy decree, I do what Thou demandest." O
wondrous Love, what hast Thou done!
The Father offers up His Son! The Son,
content, descendeth! O Love,
how strong Thou art to save!
Thou beddest Him with in the grave Whose
word the mountains rendeth.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, all my life I'll cleave to Thee,
Thy love fore'er beholding, Thee ever,
as Thou ever me, With loving arms enfolding.
Yea, Thou shalt be my Beaconlight,
To guide me safe through death's dark night.
And cheer my heart in sorrow;
Henceforth my self and all that's mine To
Thee, my Savior, I consign,
From whom all things I borrow.

title: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Ein Feste Burg (Isorhythmic)' Martin Luther, 1529.  Setting: "Common Service Book" (ULCA), 1917, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
A mighty fortress is our God,
a bulwark never failing; Our helper He,
amid the flood of mortal ills prevailing:
For still our ancient foe doth seek to work
us woe; His craft and pow'r are great, and,
armed with cruel hate,
On earth is not his equal.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Did we in our own strength confide,
our striving would be losing;
Were not the right Man on our side,
the Man of God's own choosing:
Dost ask who that may be? Christ Jesus,
it is He; Lord Sabaoth, His name,
from age to age the same,
And He must win the battle.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And though this world, with devils filled,
should threaten to undo us,
We will not fear, for God hath willed His
truth to triumph through us:
The Prince of Darkness grim,
we tremble not for him;
His rage we can endure, for lo,
his doom is sure, One little word shall fell
him.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
That word above all earthly pow'rs,
no thanks to them, abideth;
The Spirit and the gifts are ours through
Him who with us sideth:
Let goods and kindred go,
this mortal life also;
The body they may kill:
God's truth abideth still,
His kingdom is forever.

title: Abide With Me
author: Henry F. Lyte

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Abide with me; fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord with me abide.
When other helpers fail and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But as Thou dwell'st with Thy disciples,
Lord, Familiar, condes cending, patient,
free. Come not to sojourn,
but abide with me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come not in terrors, as the King of kings,
But kind and good, with healing in Thy
wings, Tears for all woes,
a heart for every plea? Come,
Friend of sinners, and thus bide with me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though re bellious and perverse
meanwhile, Thou hast not left me,
oft as I left Thee, On to the close, O Lord,
abide with me.

title: Abide, O Dearest Jesus
author: Joshua Stegmann
source: 'Christus der ist mein Leben' Melchior Vulpius, 1609

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Abide, O dearest Jesus,
Among us with Thy grace,
That Satan may not harm us,
Nor we to sin give place.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Abide, O dear Redeemer,
Among us with Thy Word,
And thus now and hereafter True peace and
joy afford.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Abide with heav'nly brightness Among us,
precious Light; Thy truth direct,
and keep us From error's gloomy night.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Abide with richest blessings Among us,
bounteous Lord; Let us in grace and wisdom
Grow daily through Thy Word.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Abide with Thy protection Among us, Lord,
our Strength, Lest world and Satan fell us
And overcome at length.

title: All Creatures of Our God and King
author: Francis of Assisi circa
source: 'Lasst Uns Erfreuen' from Geistliche Kirchengesäng, Köln, 1623. Setting: Ralph Vaughan Williams, 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All creatures of our God and King Lift up
your voice and with us sing, Alleluia!
Alleluia! Thou burning sun with golden beam,
Thou silver moon with softer gleam!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
O praise Him! O praise Him! Alleluia!
Alleluia! Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou rushing wind that art so strong Ye
clouds that sail in Heaven along,
O praise Him! Alleluia! Thou rising moon,
in praise rejoice, Ye lights of evening,
find a voice!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou flowing water, pure and clear,
Make music for thy Lord to hear,
O praise Him! Alleluia!
Thou fire so masterful and bright,
That givest man both warmth and light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Dear mother earth, who day by day Unfoldest
blessings on our way, O praise Him!
Alleluia! The flowers and fruits that in
thee grow, Let them His glory also show.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And all ye men of tender heart,
Forgiving others, take your part, O sing ye!
Alleluia! Ye who long pain and sorrow bear,
Praise God and on Him cast your care!

title: All Depends On Our Possessing
author: unknown circa
source: 'Alles ist an Gottes Segen' Johann Balthasar König, 1738.  Setting: "Chorale Book for England", 1863, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All depends on our possessing God's abundant
grace and blessing, Though all earthly
wealth depart. He who trusts with faith
unshaken In His God is not forsaken And e'er
keeps a dauntless heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He who hitherto hath fed me And to many joys
hath led me, Is and ever shall be mine.
He who did so gently school me,
He who still doth guide and rule me,
Will remain my Help divine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Many spend their lives in fretting Over
trifles and in getting Things that have no
solid ground. I shall strive to win a
treasure That will bring me lasting pleasure
And that now is seldom found.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When with sorrow I am stricken,
Hope my heart anew will quicken,
All my longing shall be stilled.
To His lovingkindness tender Soul and body I
surrender; For in Him alone I build.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Well He knows what best to grant me;
All the longing hopes that haunt me,
Joy and sorrow, have their day.
I shall doubt His wisdom never,
As God wills, so be it ever,
I to Him commit my way.

title: All Glory, Laud, and Honor
author: Theodulf of Orleans, circa 820. Translated by John Mason Neale
source: 'Valet Will Ich Dir Geben' or 'St. Theodulph' Melchior Teschner, 1615

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou art the King of Israel,
Thou David's royal Son,
Who in the Lord's Name comest,
The King and Blessed One.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
All glory, laud and honor, To Thee,
Redeemer, King, To Whom the lips of children
Made sweet hosannas ring.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The company of angels Are praising Thee on
High, And mortal men and all things Created
make reply.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The people of the Hebrews With palms before
Thee went; Our prayer and praise and anthems
Before Thee we present.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To Thee, before Thy passion,
They sang their hymns of praise; To Thee,
now high exalted, Our melody we raise.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou didst accept their praises;
Accept the prayers we bring,
Who in all good delightest,
Thou good and gracious King.

title: All Hail The Power Of Jesus' Name
author: Edward Perronet

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All hail the pow'r of Jesus' Name!
Let angels prostrate fall;
Bring forth the royal diadem,
and crown Him Lord of all.
Bring forth the royal diadem,
and crown Him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let highborn seraphs tune the lyre,
and as they tune it, fall Before His face
Who tunes their choir,
and crown Him Lord of all.
Before His face Who tunes their choir,
and crown Him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Crown Him, ye morning stars of light,
who fixed this floating ball;
Now hail the strength of Israel's might,
and crown Him Lord of all.
Now hail the strength of Israel's might,
and crown Him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Crown Him, ye martyrs of your God,
who from His altar call;
Extol the Stem of Jesse's Rod,
and crown Him Lord of all.
Extol the Stem of Jesse's Rod,
and crown Him Lord of all.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ye seed of Israel's chosen race,
ye ransomed from the fall,
Hail Him Who saves you by His grace,
and crown Him Lord of all.
Hail Him Who saves you by His grace,
and crown Him Lord of all.

title: All My Heart This Night Rejoices
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Ebeling' or 'Bonn' or 'Warum Sollt Ich' or 'All My Heart This Night' Johann Georg Ebeling, 1666

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All my heart this night rejoices, As I hear,
Far and near, Sweetest angel voices;
"Christ is born," their choirs are singing,
Till the air Ev'rywhere Now with joy is
ringing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For it dawns,the promised morrow Of His
birth Who the earth Rescues from her sorrow.
God to wear our form de scendeth,
Of His grace To our race Here His Son He
lendeth:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yea, so truly for us careth,
That His Son All we've done As our off'ring
beareth; As our Lamb who, dying for us,
Bears our load, And to God Doth in peace
restore us.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hark! a voice from yonder manger,
Soft and sweet, Doth entreat,
"Flee from woe and danger; Brethren come,
from all doth grieve you You are freed,
All you need I will surely give you."

sections.label: Verse 5

title: All Praise to Jesus' Hallowed Name
author: verse 1, ancient German.  verses 2-7, Martin Luther
source: 'Gelobet Seist Du' ancient German found in Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All praise to Jesus' hallowed Name Who of
virgin pure became True man for us!
The angels sing As the glad news to earth
they bring. Hallelujah!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Th'Eternal Father's only Son For a manger
leaves His throne Disguised in our poor
flesh and blood See now the everlasting
Good.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He whom the world could not inwrap Yonder
lies in Mary's lap; He is become an infant
small, Who by His might upholdeth all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Th'Eternal Light, come down from heav'n,
Hath to us new sunshine giv'n;
It shineth in the midst of night,
And maketh us the sons of light.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Father's Son, God everblest,
In the world be came a guest;
He leads us from this vale of tears,
And makes us in his kingdom heirs.

title: All Praise To Thee, My God, This Night
author: Thomas Ken, circa
source: 'Tallis` Canon' Thomas Tallis, circa 1567.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All praise to Thee, my God, this night,
For all the blessings of the light! Keep me,
O keep me, King of kings,
Beneath Thine own almighty wings.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Forgive me, Lord, for Thy dear Son,
The ill that I this day have done,
That with the world, myself, and Thee, I,
ere I sleep, at peace may be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Teach me to live, that I may dread The grave
as little as my bed. Teach me to die,
that so I may Rise glorious at the judgment
day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O may my soul on Thee repose,
And with sweet sleep mine eyelids close,
Sleep that may me more vig'rous make To
serve my God when I awake.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When in the night I sleepless lie,
My soul with heav'nly thoughts supply;
Let no ill dreams disturb my rest,
No pow'rs of darkness me molest.

title: All Who Believe and Are Baptized
author: Thomas Hansen Kingo
source: 'Es ist das Heil uns Kommen Her' German circa 1400 from Etlich Christlich Lider, Wittenberg, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
All who believe and are baptized shall see
the Lord's salvation; baptized into the
death of Christ, they are a new creation.
through Christ's redemption they shall stand
among the glorious heav'nly band of every
tribe and nation.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With one accord, O God, we pray:
grant us thy Holy Spirit;
look thou on our infirmity through Jesus'
blood and merit. Grant us to grow in grace
each day that by this sacra ment we may
eternal life inherit.

title: Alleluia, Alleluia! Hearts to Heaven and Voices Raise
author: Christopher Wordsworth
source: 'Ode to Joy' Ludwig van Beethoven; Adapted by Edward Hodges, 1824

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Alleluia, alleluia! Hearts to Heav'n and
voices raise: Sing to God a hymn of
gladness, sing to God a hymn of praise. He,
who on the cross a Victim,
for the world's salvation bled,
Jesus Christ, the King of glory,
now is risen from the dead.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now the iron bars are broken,
Christ from death to life is born,
Glorious life, and life immortal,
on the holy Easter morn.
Christ has triumphed, and we conquer by His
mighty enterprise: We with Him to life
eternal by His resurrection rise.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Christ is risen, Christ,
the first fruits of the holy harvest field,
Which will all its full abundance at His
second coming yield: Then the golden ears of
harvest will their heads before Him wave,
Ripened by His glorious sunshine from the
furrows of the grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Christ is risen, we are risen!
Shed upon us heav'nly grace,
Rain and dew and gleams of glory from the
brightness of Thy face; That we,
with our hearts in Heaven,
here on earth may fruitful be,
And by angel hands be gathered, and be ever,
Lord, with Thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Alleluia, alleluia! Glory be to God on high;
Alleluia! to the Savior who has gained the
victory; Alleluia! to the Spirit,
fount of love and sanctity: Alleluia,
alleluia! to the Triune Majesty.

title: Alleluia, Sing To Jesus!
author: William Chatterton Dix
source: 'HyFrydol' Rowland H. Prichard, 1830.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Alleluia! sing to Jesus! His the scepter,
His the throne. Alleluia! His the triumph,
His the victory alone. Hark!
the songs of peaceful Zion thunder like a
mighty flood. Jesus out of every nation has
redeemed us by His blood.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Alleluia! not as orphans are we left in
sorrow now; Alleluia! He is near us,
faith believes, nor questions how;
Though the cloud from sight received Him
when the forty days were o'er Shall our
hearts forget His promise,
"I am with you evermore"?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Alleluia! bread of angels,
Thou on earth our food, our stay; Alleluia!
here the sinful flee to Thee from day to
day: Intercessor, Friend of sinners,
Earth's Redeemer, plead for me,
Where the songs of all the sinless sweep
across the crystal sea.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Alleluia! King eternal,
Thee the Lord of lords we own; Alleluia!
born of Mary, Earth Thy footstool,
Heaven Thy throne: Thou within the veil hast
entered, robed in flesh our great High
Priest; Thou on earth both priest and victim
in the Eucharistic feast.

title: Almighty God Your Word Is Cast
author: John Cawood

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Almighty God, Your Word is cast Like seed
into the ground; Now let the dew of Heav'n
descend, And righteous fruits abound.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let not the foe of Christ and man This holy
seed remove, But give it root in ev'ry heart
To bring forth fruits of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let not the world's deceitful cares The
rising plant destroy. But let it yield a
hundredfold The fruits of peace and joy.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nor let Your Word so kindly sent To raise us
to Your throne Return to You,
and sadly tell That we reject Your Son.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Oft as the precious seed is sown,
Your quick'ning grace bestow,
That all whose souls the truth receive,
Its saving power may know.

title: Amazing Grace
author: John Newton
source: 'New Britain' James P. Carrell and David L. Clayton, 1831.  Setting: Edwin Othello Excell, 1900

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Amazing grace! How sweet the sound That
saved a wretch like me! I once was lost,
but now am found; Was blind, but now I see.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear,
And grace my fears relieved;
How precious did that grace appear The hour
I first believed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Through many dangers, toils and snares,
I have already come; 'Tis grace hath brought
me safe thus far, And grace will lead me
home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The Lord has promised good to me,
His Word my hope secures;
He will my Shield and Portion be,
As long as life endures.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yea, when this flesh and heart shall fail,
And mortal life shall cease,
I shall possess, with in the veil,
A life of joy and peace.

title: And Can It Be
author: Charles Wesley
source: 'Fillmore' Jeremiah Ingalls (1764-1828).  Setting: "The Methodist Hymnal", 1905

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
And can it be that I should gain An interest
in the Savior's blood? Died He for me,
who caused His pain? For me,
who Him to death pursued? Amazing love!
How can it be, That Thou, my God,
shouldst die for me?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis mystery all: th'Immortal dies:
Who can explore His strange design?
In vain the firstborn seraph tries To sound
the depths of love divine. 'Tis mercy all!
Let earth adore, Let angel minds inquire no
more.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He left His Father's throne above So free,
so infi nite His grace?
Emptied Himself of all but love,
And bled for Adam's helpless race:
'Tis mercy all, immense and free,
For O my God, it found out me!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Angel Voices, Ever Singing
author: Francis Pott

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Angel voices, ever singing,
round Thy throne of light, Angel harps,
forever ringing, rest not day or night;
Thousands only live to bless Thee,
and confess Thee Lord of might.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou Who art beyond the farthest mortal eye
can scan, Can it be that Thou regardest
songs of sinful man? Can we feel that Thou
art near us and wilt hear us? Yea, we can.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, we know Thy love rejoices o'er each
work of Thine; Thou didst ears and hands and
voices for Thy praise combine;
Craftsman's art and music's measure for Thy
pleasure didst design.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here, great God, today we offer of Thine own
to Thee; And for Thine acceptance proffer,
all unworthily, Hearts and minds,
and hands and voices, in our choicest
melody.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Honor, glory, might and merit,
Thine shall ever be, Father, Son,
and Holy Spirit, blessed Trinity;
Of the best that Thou hast given Earth and
Heaven render Thee.

title: Angels From the Realms of Glory
author: James Montgomery
source: 'Regent Square' Henry Smart, 1867.  Setting: "Psalms and Hymns for Divine Worship", 1867

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Angels from the realms of glory,
Wing your flight o'er all the earth;
Ye who sang creation's story Now proclaim
Messiah's birth.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Come and worship, come and worship,
Worship Christ, the newborn King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shepherds, in the field abiding,
Watching o'er your flocks by night,
God with us is now residing;
Yonder shines the infant light:

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Saints, before the altar bending,
Watching long in hope and fear;
Suddenly the Lord, descending,
In His temple shall appear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sinners, wrung with true repentance,
Doomed for guilt to endless pains,
Justice now revokes the sentence,
Mercy calls you; break your chains.

title: Angels We Have Heard On High
author: French Carol; Translated by James Chadwick
source: 'Gloria' French carol melody.  Setting: Edward (or Edwin) S. Barnes, before 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Angels we have heard on high Sweetly singing
o'er the plains, And the mountains in reply
Echoing their joyous strains.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Gloria, in excelsis Deo! Gloria,
in excelsis Deo!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shepherds, why this jubilee?
Why your joyous strains prolong?
What the gladsome tidings be Which inspire
your heav'nly song?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come to Bethlehem and see Christ Whose birth
the angels sing; Come, adore on bended knee,
Christ the Lord, the newborn King.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
See Him in a manger laid,
Whom the choirs of angels praise; Mary,
Joseph, lend your aid,
While our hearts in love we raise.

title: As With Gladness Men of Old
author: William Chatterton Dix
source: 'Dix' or 'Treuer Heiland, Wir Sind Heir' Conrad Kocher, 1838. Abridged by William Henry Monk, 1861

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
As with gladness, men of old Did the guiding
star behold As with joy they hailed its
light Leading onward, beaming bright So,
most glorious Lord, may we Evermore be led
to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As with joyful steps they sped To that lowly
manger bed There to bend the knee before Him
whom Heav'n and earth adore;
So may we with willing feet Ever seek Thy
mercy seat.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
As they offered gifts most rare At that
manger rude and bare; So may we with holy
joy, Pure and free from sin's alloy,
All our costliest treasures bring, Christ,
to Thee, our heav'nly King.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Holy Jesus, ev'ry day Keep us in the narrow
way; And, when earthly things are past,
Bring our ransomed souls at last Where they
need no star to guide,
Where no clouds Thy glory hide.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In the heav'nly country bright,
Need they no created light; Thou its Light,
its Joy, its Crown, Thou its Sun which goes
not down; There forever may we sing
Alleluias to our King!

title: Ascribe To the Lord Honor
author: Bola Omodun Ilori
source: 'Iyin Oluwa' traditional Yoruba tune

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ascribe to the Lord, honor,
And glory due His Name Worship in His
holiness, Worthy is His pow'r and fame.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Lord of glory thunders O'er great and
mighty seas; His voice is so majestic,
It breaks cedar to pieces.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His voice like a mighty flash,
Shakes the desert of Kadesh,
It makes bare the thick forest No other
voice is its match.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The Lord sits upon His throne,
That's set upon the flood.
He gives strength to His people,
Who put their trust in His word.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Ascribe to the Lord, honor,
And glory due His Name,
Worship Him in holiness Worthy is His might
and fame.

title: At The Lamb's High Feast
author: Latin, circa 6th Century. Translated by Robert Campbell
source: 'Sonne der Gerechtigkeit' Czech, Kirchengeseng, 1566.  Setting: Brian J. Dumont, 31 Dec 2009

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
At the Lamb's high feast we sing,
Praise to our victorious King,
Who has washed us in the tide Flowing from
his piercèd side; Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Praise we Him, whose love divine Gives His
sacred blood for wine,
Gives His body for the feast,
Christ the Victim, Christ the Priest.
Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Where the Paschal blood is poured,
Death's dark angel sheathes his sword;
Israel's hosts triumphant go Through the
wave that drowns the foe. Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Praise we Christ, whose blood was shed,
Paschal Victim, Paschal Bread;
With sincerity and love Eat we Manna from
above. Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Author of All Life
author: Brian J. Dumont, 12 Oct
source: 'Beach Spring' Benjamin F. White, 1844.  Setting: "The Sacred Harp", 1860, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Author of all Life, our Father,
breathe into our hearts again.
Stir our deadness, heal our weakness,
crush our evil thoughts so vain.
Life Creator, life Redeemer, life Imparter,
Source of Truth, Teach us now to love each
other, Teach us Lord to love like You.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hearts so hard, we hate each other,
those in need we treat with scorn... Old,
unwise, or not my color, Palsied limbs,
or not yet born. Life Creator,
life Redeemer, life Imparter, Three in One,
Teach us Lord to see Your Image,
Teach us now to see the Son.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Christ now grants us life eternal,
to know You the one true God,
He the Way to see the Father,
He the One who felt the rod. Life Creator,
life Redeemer, life Imparter,
Life conferred! Let us sing of Your
atonement, Let all people hear Your Word!

title: Awake My Soul, An Offering Bring
author: Brian L. Penney
source: 'Melismata 22' Thomas Ravenscroft, 1611 (#22 from "Melismata").  Setting: Brian L. Penney, 2009

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake my soul, an off'ring bring to Jesus
our exalted King; Sing to Him Who reigns
above in carnate fount of grace and love;
Sing to Him Who reigns above incarnate fount
of grace and love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4

title: Awake, My Heart, With Gladness
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Auf, Auf, Mein Herz mit Freuden' Johann Crüger, 1648. Setting: "Mehrstimmiges ChoralBuch", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, my heart, with gladness,
See what today is done;
How after gloom and sadness,
Comes forth the glorious Sun.
My Savior there was laid Where our bed must
be made When to the realms of light Our
spirit wings its flight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They in the grave did sink Him,
The foe held jubilee; Before he can bethink
him, Lo! Christ again is free.
And "Victory" He cries,
And waving tow'rds the skies His banner,
while the field Is by the Hero held!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Upon the grave is standing The Hero looking
round; The foe, no more withstanding,
His weapons on the ground Throws down,
his hellish pow'r To Christ must he give
o'er, And to the Victor's bands Must yield
his feet and hands.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
A sight it is to gladden;
And fill the heart with glee,
No more affright or sadden Shall aught,
or take from me My trust or fortitude,
Or any precious good The Savior bought for
me In sov'reign love and free.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Hell and its prince, the devil,
Of all their pow'rs are shorn;
Now I am safe from evil,
And sin I laugh to scorn.
Grim Death with all his might Cannot my soul
affright; He is a pow'rless form,
Howe'er he rage and storm.

title: Awake, My Soul, And With The Sun
author: Thomas Ken

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Awake, my soul, and with the sun Thy daily
stage of duty run; Shake off dull sloth,
and joyful rise, To pay thy morning
sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy precious time misspent, redeem,
Each present day thy last esteem,
Improve thy talent with due care;
For the great day thyself prepare.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By influence of Light divine Let thy own
light to others shine.
Reflect all Heaven's propitious ways In
ardent love, and cheerful praise.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Wake, and lift up thyself, my heart,
And with the angels bear thy part,
Who all night long unwearied sing High
praise to the eternal King.

title: Away In A Manger
author: stanzas 1,2 anonymous published Philadelphia
source: 'Mueller' James R. Murray, 1887.  Setting: "Hymnal for American Youth", 1919

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Away in a manger, no crib for a bed,
The little Lord Jesus laid down His sweet
head. The stars in the sky looked down where
He lay, The little Lord Jesus,
asleep on the hay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The cattle are lowing, the Baby awakes,
But little Lord Jesus, no crying He makes;
I love Thee, Lord Jesus,
look down from the sky And stay by my cradle
til morning is nigh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Be near me, Lord Jesus,
I ask Thee to stay Close by me for ever,
and love me, I pray; Bless all the dear
children in Thy tender care,
And fit us for Heaven to live with Thee
there.

title: Baptized Into Thy Name Most Holy
author: Johann Jakob Rambach
source: 'O Dass Ich Tausend Zungen Hätte (Dretzel)' Kornelius Heinrich Dretzel, 1731

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Baptized into Thy Name most holy, O Father,
Son, and Holy Ghost, I claim a place,
though weak and lowly, Among Thy seed,
Thy chosen host. Buried with Christ and dead
to sin, Thy Spirit now shall live within.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
And I have vowed to fear and love Thee And
to obey Thee, Lord, alone;
I felt Thy Holy Spirit move me,
I dared to pledge myself Thine own,
Renouncing sin to keep the faith And war
with evil unto death.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My faithful God, Thou failest never,
Thy cov'nant surely will abide; Oh,
cast me not away forever Should I transgress
it on my side! But if I fall hide not Thy
face, Restore Thy child, Lord, by Thy Grace.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yes, all I am and love most dearly,
To Thee I offer now the whole;
O let me make my vows sincerely,
Take full possession of my soul!
Let naught within me, naught I own,
Serve any will save Thine alone.

title: Be Still My Soul
author: Katharina A. von Schlegel
source: 'Finlandia' Jean Sibelius, 1899.  Setting: from Jean Sibelius, 1900

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Be still, my soul: the Lord is on thy side.
Bear patiently the cross of grief or pain.
Leave to thy God to order and provide;
In every change, He faithful will remain.
Be still, my soul: thy best,
thy heav'nly Friend Through thorny ways
leads to a joyful end.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Be still, my soul: thy God doth undertake To
guide the fu ture, as He has the past.
Thy hope, thy confidence let nothing shake;
All now mysterious shall be bright at last.
Be still, my soul: the waves and winds still
know His voice Who ruled them while He dwelt
below.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Be still, my soul: when dearest friends
depart, And all is dark ened in the vale of
tears, Then shalt thou better know His love,
His heart, Who comes to soothe thy sorrow
and thy fears. Be still, my soul:
thy Je sus can repay From His own fullness
all He takes away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Be still, my soul: the hour is hast'ning on
When we shall be forever with the Lord.
When disappointment, grief and fear are
gone, Sorrow forgot, love's purest joys
restored. Be still, my soul:
when change and tears are past All safe and
blessèd we shall meet at last.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Be still, my soul: begin the song of praise
On earth, believ ing, to Thy Lord on high;
Acknowledge Him in all thy words and ways,
So shall He view thee with a well pleased
eye. Be still, my soul:
the Sun of life divine Through passing
clouds shall but more brightly shine.

title: Be Thou My Vision
author: Attr. Dallan Forgaill, 8th Century.  Translated by Mary Byrne
source: 'Slane' Traditional Irish.  Setting: Mark Hamilton Dewey, 2007

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Be Thou my Vision, O Lord of my heart;
Naught be all else to me,
save that Thou art. Thou my best Thought,
by day or by night, Waking or sleeping,
Thy presence my light.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Be Thou my battle Shield,
Sword for the fight; Be Thou my Dignity,
Thou my Delight; Thou my soul's Shelter,
Thou my high Tower: Raise Thou me
heav'nward, O Pow'r of my pow'r.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Riches I heed not, nor man's empty praise,
Thou mine Inheritance, now and always:
Thou and Thou only, be first in my heart,
High King of Heaven, my Treasure Thou art.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
High King of Heaven, my victory won,
May I reach Heav'ns joys,
O bright Heaven's Sun!
Heart of my own heart, whatever befall,
Still be my Vision, O Ruler of all.

title: Beautiful Savior
author: German Jesuits, published
source: 'Crusader`s Hymn' Silesian folk song, 1842.  Setting: Richard S. Willis, 1850

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Beautiful Savior, King of Creation Son of
God and Son of Man! Truly I'd love Thee,
truly I'd serve Thee, Light of my soul,
my joy, my crown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fair are the meadows, Fair are the
woodlands, Robed in the flow'rs of blooming
spring; Jesus is fairer, Jesus is purer,
He makes our sorr'wing spirit sing.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fair is the sunshine, Fair is the moonlight,
Bright the sparkling stars on high;
Jesus shines brighter,
Jesus shines purer Than all the angels in
the sky.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Beautiful Savior, Lord of the nations,
Son of God and Son of Man! Glory and honor,
Praise, adoration Now and forevermore be
Thine!

title: Behold, A Host, Arrayed in White
author: Hans Adolf Brorson, circa
source: 'Den Store Hvide Flok' or 'Great White Host' traditional Norwegian, 17th cent.  Setting: Edvard Grieg, 1907

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Behold a host, arrayed in white,
Like thousand snow clad mountains bright,
With palms they stand.
Who is this band Before the throne of light?
Lo, these are they of glorious fame Who from
the great affliction came And in the flood
of Jesus' blood Are cleansed from guilt and
blame. Now gathered in the holy place Their
voices they in worship raise,
Their anthems swell where God doth dwell,
Mid angels song of praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Despised and scorned, they sojourned here;
But now, how glorious they appear!
Those martyrs stand a priestly band,
God's throne forever near. So oft,
in troubled days gone by,
In anguish they would weep and sigh.
At home above the God of Love For aye their
tears shall dry. They now enjoy their
Sabbath rest, The paschal banquet of the
blest; The Lamb, their Lord,
at festal board Himself is Host and Guest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then hail, ye mighty legions, yea, All hail!
Now safe and blest for aye,
And praise the Lord, who with His Word
Sustained you on the way.
Ye did the joys of earth disdain,
Ye toiled and sowed in tears and pain.
Farewell, now bring your sheaves and sing
Salvation's glad refrain.
Swing high your palms, lift up your song,
Yea, make it myriad voices strong.
Eternally shall praise to Thee, God,
and the Lamb belong.

title: Beneath The Cross Of Jesus
author: Elizabeth C. Clephane
source: 'St. Christopher' Frederick C. Maker, 1881.  Setting: "Bristol Tune-Book", 1891

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Beneath the cross of Jesus I fain would take
my stand, The shadow of a mighty rock within
a weary land; A home within the wilderness,
a rest upon the way, From the burning of the
noontide heat, and the burden of the day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O safe and happy shelter,
O refuge tried and sweet,
O trysting place where Heaven's love and
Heaven's justice meet!
As to the holy patriarch that wondrous dream
was giv'n, So seems my Savior's cross to me,
a ladder up to heav'n.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There lies beneath its shadow but on the
further side The darkness of an awful grave
that gapes both deep and wide And there
between us stands the cross two arms
outstretched to save A watchman set to guard
the way from that eternal grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Upon that cross of Jesus mine eye at times
can see The very dying form of One Who
suffered there for me;
And from my stricken heart with tears two
wonders I confess; The wonders of redeeming
love and my unworthiness.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I take, O cross, thy shadow for my abiding
place; I ask no other sunshine than the
sunshine of His face; Content to let the
world go by to know no gain or loss,
My sinful self my only shame,
my glory all the cross.

title: Blessed Assurance
author: Fanny Crosby
source: 'Blessed Assurance' or 'Assurance' Phoebe P. Knapp, 1873

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blessèd assurance, Jesus is mine!
O what a foretaste of glory divine!
Heir of salvation, purchase of God,
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior, all the day long;
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Savior, all the day long.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Perfect submission, perfect delight,
Visions of rapture now burst on my sight;
Angels descending bring from above Echoes of
mercy, whispers of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Perfect submission, all is at rest I in my
Savior am happy and blest,
Watching and waiting, looking above,
Filled with His goodness, lost in His love.

title: Blessed Jesus at Thy Word
author: verses 1-3, Tobias Clausnitzer
source: 'Liebster Jesu wir Sind Hier' Johann Rudolph Ahle, 1664.  Setting: Fridrich Layriz, 1854

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blessed Jesus, at Thy Word We are gathered
all to hear Thee; Let our hearts and souls
be stirred Now to seek and love and fear
Thee, By Thy teachings sweet and holy,
Drawn from earth to love Thee solely.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost,
Praise to Thee and adoration!
Grant that we Thy Word may trust And obtain
true consolation, While we here below must
wander, Till we sing Thy praises yonder.

title: Blest Be The Tie That Binds
author: John Fawcett
source: 'Boylston' Lowell Mason, 1832

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blest be the tie that binds Our hearts in
Christian love; The fellowship of kindred
minds Is like to that above.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before our Father's throne We pour our
ardent prayers; Our fears, our hopes,
our aims are one Our comforts and our cares.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We share each other's woes,
Our mutual burdens bear;
And often for each other flows The
sympathizing tear.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When we asunder part, It gives us inward
pain; But we shall still be joined in heart,
And hope to meet again.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
This glorious hope revives Our courage by
the way; While each in expectation lives,
And longs to see the day.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, alt
source: 'Fillmore' Jeremiah Ingalls (1764-1828).  Setting: "The Methodist Hymnal", 1905

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Blind Bartimaeus at the gates Of Jericho in
darkness waits: He hears the crowd;
he hears a breath say "It is Christ of
Nazareth!" And calls in tones of agony,
"O Jesus, Jesus pity me!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The thronging multitudes in-crease "Blind
Bartimaeus, hold thy peace!" But still,
above the noisy crowd,
The blind man's cry is shrill and loud:
Until they say, "He calleth thee; Courage!
arise! He calleth thee!"

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then saith the Christ,
as silent stands The crowd,
"What wilt thou at My hands?" And he
replies, "O give me light! Rabbi,
restore the blind man's sight." And Jesus an
swers, "Go thy way, Thy faith,
thy faith hath savèd thee."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Ye that hath eyes and cannot see,
In darkness and in misery,
Recall those mighty voices three "O Jesus,
Jesus pity me!" "Courage! arise!
He calleth thee!" "Thy faith,
thy faith hath savèd thee."

title: Bonus Carol: Good King Wenceslas
author: John Mason Neale
source: 'Tempus Adest Floridum' 13th Century spring carol; first published in the Swedish Piae Cantones, 1582

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Good King Wenceslas looked out on the Feast
of Stephen, When the snow lay round about,
deep and crisp and even.
Brightly shone the moon that night,
though the frost was cruel,
When a poor man came in sight,
gath'ring winter fuel.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Hither, page, and stand by me,
if thou knows't it, telling, Yonder peasant,
who is he? Where and what his dwelling?"
"Sire, he lives a good league hence,
underneath the mountain,
Right against the forest fence,
by Saint Agnes' fountain."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"Bring me flesh and bring me wine,
bring me pine logs hither,
Thou and I will see him dine,
when we bear them thither." Page and
monarch, forth they went,
forth they went together,
Through the cold wind's wild lament and the
bitter weather.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Sire, the night is darker now,
and the wind blows stronger, Fails my heart,
I know not how; I can go no longer." "Mark
my footsteps, my good page,
tread thou in them boldly,
Thou shalt find the winter's rage freeze thy
blood less coldly."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In his master's steps he trod,
where the snow lay dinted;
Heat was in the very sod which the saint had
printed. Therefore, Christian men, be sure,
wealth or rank possessing,
Ye who now will bless the poor shall
yourselves find blessing.

title: Breathe on Me, Breath of God
author: Edwin Hatch
source: 'Aylesbury' or 'Wirksworth' found in John Chetham's Psalmody, 1718

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Breathe on me, breath of God,
Fill me with life anew,
That I may love what Thou dost love,
And do what Thou wouldst do.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Breathe on me, breath of God,
Until my heart is pure,
Until with Thee I will one will,
To do and to endure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Breathe on me, breath of God,
So shall I never die, But live with Thee the
perfect life Of Thine eternity.

title: Built on the Rock
author: Nikolai F. S. Grundtvig
source: 'Kirken Den Er Et Gammelt Hus' Ludvig M. Lindeman, 1840.  Setting: "The Lutheran Hymnary", 1913

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Built on the Rock the church doth stand,
Even when steeples are fall ing;
Crumbled have spires in every land,
Bells still are chiming and calling;
Calling the young and old to rest,
But above all the soul distressed,
Longing for rest everlasting.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Surely in temples made with hands, God,
the Most High, is not dwell ing;
High above earth His temple stands,
All earthly temples excelling;
Yet He whom heav'ns cannot contain Chose to
abide on earth with men,
Built in our bodies His temple.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We are God's house of living stones,
Built for His own habita tion;
He through baptismal grace us owns,
Heirs of His wondrous salvation;
Were we but two His Name to tell,
Yet He would deign with us to dwell,
With all His grace and His favor.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now we may gather with our King;
Ev'n in the lowliest dwell ing:
Praises to Him we there may bring,
His wondrous mercy foretelling;
Jesus His grace to us accords,
Spirit and life are all His words,
His truth doth hallow the temple.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Still we our earthly temples rear,
That we may herald His prais es;
They are the homes where He draws near And
little children embraces,
Beautiful things in them are said,
God there with us His cov'nant made,
Making us heirs of His kingdom.

title: By Grace I'm Saved
author: Christian L. Scheidt
source: 'O Dass Ich Tansend Zungen' Johann Balthasar König, 1738

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
By grace I'm savedgrace free and boundless!
My heart, believ'st thou this or not?
Why tremblest thou with terror groundless?
Has ever God a falsehood taught?
His Word is truethen this must be:
By grace there is a crown for thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By grace! our works are all rejected,
All claims of merit pass for naught;
The mighty Savior, long expected,
To us this blissful truth has brought,
That He by death redeems our race,
And we are saved alone by grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By grace! mark well this phrase's meaning,
When sin rolls sorrows o'er thy breast,
When Satan threats with pride o'erweening,
When troubled conscience sighs for rest:
What reason ne'er can comprehend It pleases
God by grace to send.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By grace His Son, on earth appearing,
Vouchsafed beneath thy woe to bend;
Hadst thou, damnation justly fearing,
Done aught to render Him thy friend?
Was't not that He thy welfare sought,
And but by grace deliv'rance wrought?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
By grace! this ground of our salvation As
long as God is true endures:
What saints have penned by inspiration,
What God to our poor soul secures,
What all our faith must rest upon, Is grace,
free grace through His dear Son.

title: Christ Arose
author: Robert Lowry

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Low in the grave He lay Jesus my Savior!
Waiting the coming dayJesus my Lord!
Up from the grave He arose,
With a mighty triumph o'er His

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
He arose! foes; He arose a Victor from the
dark domain, And He lives forever with His
He arose! saints to reign. He arose!
He arose! Hallelujah! Christ arose!
He arose! He arose!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Vainly they watch His bedJesus my Savior!
Vainly they seal the deadJesus my Lord!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Death cannot keep his preyJesus my Savior!
He tore the bars awayJesus my Lord!

title: Christ Jesus Lay In Death's Strong Bands
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Christ lag in Tobes Banden' or 'Torgau' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christ Jesus lay in death's strong bands,
For our offenses given;
But now at God's right hand He stands,
And brings us life from Heaven.
Wherefore let us joyful be,
And sing to God right thankfully Loud songs
of Alleluia! Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No son of man could conquer Death,
Such mischief sin had wrought us,
For innocence dwelt not on earth,
And therefore Death had brought us Into
thralldom from of old And ever grew more
strong and bold And kept us in his bondage.
Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But Jesus Christ, God's only Son,
To our low state de scended,
The cause of Death He has undone,
His power forever ended,
Ruined all his right and claim And left him
nothing but the name, His sting is lost
forever. Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It was a strange and dreadful strife When
life and death con tended;
The victory remained with life;
The reign of death was ended.
Stripped of power, no more it reigns,
An empty form a lone remains Death's sting
is lost forever! Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Here the true Paschal Lamb we see,
Whom God so freely gave us;
He died on the accursed tree So strong His
love! to save us. See,
His blood doth mark our door;
Faith points to it, Death passes o'er,
And Satan cannot harm us. Alleluia!

title: Christ My King On High
author: Jay C. Wingard
source: 'Christ My King on High' Jay C. Wingard, 2011

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, my sin, it grieves me so.
How I long for my Lord to come.
Bless my God who clothes me bright,
wraps me pure in heav'n's Great Light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Spotless Lamb made sin for me. God,
Great Judge, just always be.
Sealed on high with Christ's Great Pledge
never more shall death I dread.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One with Him, I stand secure,
Safe in Triune hands I'm sure.
Christ's great merits giv'n to me.
I now hear Him say, "Whom I'm pleased."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Long to see the skies burn bright,
heaven's hosts all clothed in white.
See the King, His vic'try won. Come,
pure Bride behold the Son.

title: Christ Returneth
author: H. L. Turner

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It may be at morn, when the day is awaking,
When sunlight through darkness and shadow is
breaking That Jesus will come in the
fullness of glory To receive from the world
"His own."

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
O Lord Jesus, how long,
how long Ere we shout the glad song,
Christ re turneth! Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
Amen. Hallelujah! Amen.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It may be at midday, it may be at twilight,
It may be, per chance,
that the blackness of midnight Will burst
into light in the blaze of His glory,
When Jesus receives "His own."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While hosts cry Hosanna,
from heaven descending,
With glorified saints and the angels
attending, With grace on His brow,
like a halo of glory, Will Jesus receive
"His own."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, joy! oh, delight! should we go without
dying, No sickness, no sadness,
no dread and no crying.
Caught up through the clouds with our Lord
into glory, When Jesus receives "His own."

title: Christ The Lord Is Risen Today (Lyra)
author: Stanzas 1-7, Charles Wesley
source: 'Llanfair' Robert Williams, 1817.  Setting: John Roberts, 1837

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Christ, the Lord, is risen today, Alleluia!
Sons of men and angels say, Alleluia!
Raise your joys and triumphs high, Alleluia!
Sing, ye heavens, and earth, reply,
Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Love's redeeming work is done, Alleluia!
Fought the fight, the battle won, Alleluia!
Lo! the Sun's eclipse is o'er, Alleluia! Lo!
He sets in blood no more, Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Vain the stone, the watch, the seal,
Alleluia! Christ hath burst the gates of
hell, Alleluia! Death in vain forbids His
rise, Alleluia! Christ hath opened paradise,
Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lives again our glorious King, Alleluia!
Where, O death, is now thy sting? Alleluia!
Once He died our souls to save, Alleluia!
Where thy victory, O grave? Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Soar we now where Christ hath led, Alleluia!
Following our exalted Head, Alleluia!
Made like Him, like Him we rise, Alleluia!
Ours the cross, the grave, the skies,
Alleluia!

title: Come Down, O Love Divine
author: Bianco of Siena d
source: 'Down Ampney' Ralph Vaughan Williams, 1906.  Setting: Ralph Vaughan Williams, 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come down, O love divine,
seek Thou this soul of mine,
And visit it with Thine own ardor glowing.
O Comforter, draw near,
within my heart appear, And kindle it,
Thy holy flame bestowing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O let it freely burn, til earthly passions
turn To dust and ashes in its heat
consuming; And let Thy glorious light shine
ever on my sight, And clothe me round,
the while my path illuming.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let holy charity mine outward vesture be,
And lowliness become mine inner clothing;
True lowliness of heart,
which takes the humbler part,
And o'er its own shortcomings weeps with
loathing.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And so the yearning strong,
with which the soul will long,
Shall far outpass the pow'r of human
telling; For none can guess its grace,
till he become the place Wherein the Holy
Spirit makes His dwelling.

title: Come Holy Spirit, Lord Our God
author: v. 1 ancient Latin.  v.2-3 Martin Luther
source: 'Komm Heiliger Geist, Herre Gott' ancient Latin found in Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Holy Spirit, Lord our God,
And pour Thy gifts of grace abroad;
Thy faithful people fill with blessing,
Love's fire their hearts possessing. O Lord,
Thou by Thy heav'nly Light Dost gather and
in faith unite Through all the world a holy
nation To sing to Thee with exultation,

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text: Hallelujah! Hallelujah!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, holiest Light! O Rock adored!
Give us Thy light, Thy living Word,
To God Himself our spirits leading,
With Him as children pleading. From error,
Lord, our souls defend,
That they on Christ a lone attend;
In Him with faith unfeigned a biding,
In Him with all their might confiding.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O holiest Fire! O Source of rest!
Grant that with joy and hope possest,
And in Thy service kept for ever,
Naught us from Thee may sever. Lord,
may Thy pow'r prepare each heart;
To our weak nature strength impart,
Onward to press, our foes de fying, To Thee,
through living and through dying.

title: Come Thou Fount Of Every Blessing
author: Robert Robinson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Thou Fount of every blessing,
Tune my heart to sing Thy grace;
Streams of mercy, never ceasing,
Call for songs of loudest praise.
Teach me some melodious sonnet,
Sung by flaming tongues above.
Praise the mount! I'm fixed upon it,
Mount of Thy redeeming love.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus sought me when a stranger,
Wand'ring from the fold of God; He,
to rescue me from danger,
Interposed His precious blood;
How His kindness yet pursues me Mortal
tongue can never tell, Clothed in flesh,
till death shall loose me I cannot proclaim
it well.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O to grace how great a debtor Daily I'm
constrained to be! Let Thy goodness,
like a fetter, Bind my wand'ring heart to
Thee. Prone to wander, Lord, I feel it,
Prone to leave the God I love;
Here's my heart, O take and seal it,
Seal it for Thy courts above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O that day when freed from sinning,
I shall see Thy lovely face;
Clothèd then in blood washed linen How I'll
sing Thy sovereign grace; Come, my Lord,
no longer tarry, Take my ransomed soul away;
Send thine angels now to carry Me to realms
of endless day.

title: Come, God Creator, Holy Ghost
author: variously ascribed to Ambrose, Gregory the Great, Charlemagne, or Rhabanus Maurus
source: 'Komm, Gott Schoepfer Heiliger Geist' ancient Latin found in Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, God Creator, Holy Ghost,
And visit Thou these souls of men;
Fill them with graces, as Thou dost,
Thy creatures make pure again.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For Comforter Thy name we call.
Sweet gift of God most high above,
A holy unction to us all O Fount of life,
Fire of love.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou with Thy wondrous sev'nfold gifts The
finger art of God's right hand;
The Father's Word Thou sendest swift On
tongues of fire to each land.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Drive far from us our wily foe;
Grant us Thy blesséd peace within,
That in Thy footsteps we may go,
And shun the dark ways of sin.

title: Come, Thou Long-Expected Jesus
author: Charles Wesley
source: 'Jefferson'  from "Southern Harmony", 1835, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, Thou long expected Jesus Born to set
Thy people free; From our fears and sins
release us, Let us find our rest in Thee.
Israel's Strength and Consolation,
Hope of all the earth Thou art;
Dear Desire of every nation,
Joy of every longing heart.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Born Thy people to de liver,
Born a child and yet a King,
Born to reign in us forever,
Now Thy gracious kingdom bring.
By Thine own eternal Spirit Rule in all our
hearts alone; By Thine all sufficient merit,
Raise us to Thy glorious throne.

title: Come, Ye Disconsolate
author: verses 1-2 Thomas Moore
source: 'Consolator (Webbe)' Samuel Webbe, 1792

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Joy of the desolate, light of the straying,
Hope of the penitent, fadeless and pure,
Here speaks the Comforter, tenderly saying,
"Earth has no sorrow that Heav'n cannot
cure."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here see the Bread of Life;
see waters flowing Forth from the throne of
God, pure from above; Come to the feast of
love; come, ever knowing Earth has no sorrow
but Heav'n can remove.

title: Come, Your Heart and Voices Raising
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Quem Pastores' German, 1410.  Setting: "The Lutheran Hymnary", 1913

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, your hearts and voices raising,
Christ the Lord with gladness praising;
Loudly sing His love amazing,
Worthy folk of Christendom.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sin and death may well be groaning,
Satan now may well be moaning; We,
our full sal vation owning,
Cast our every care away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See how God, for us providing,
Gave His Son and life abiding;
He our weary steps is guiding From earth's
woe to heav'nly joy.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Christ, from heav'n to us descending And in
love our race befriending,
In our need His help extending,
Saved us from the wily Foe.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Jacob's Star in all its splendor Beams with
comfort sweet and tender,
Forcing Satan to surrender,
Breaking all the pow'rs of hell.

title: Comfort, Comfort Ye My People
author: Johann Olearius (Oelschlaeger)
source: 'Freu dich sehr, o meine Seele' from Trente Quatre Pseaumes de David, Geneva, 1551

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Comfort, comfort ye My people,
Speak ye peace, thus saith our God;
Comfort those who sit in darkness,
Mourning 'neath their sorrow's load;
Speak ye to Jerusalem Of the peace that
waits for them; Tell her that her sins I
cover, And her warfare now is over.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For the herald's voice is crying In the
desert far and near, Bidding all men to
repentance, Since the kingdom now is here.
O that warning cry obey!
Now prepare for God a way!
Let the valleys rise to meet Him,
And the hills bow down to greet Him.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yea, her sins our God will pardon,
Blotting out each dark misdeed;
All that well deserved His anger He will no
more see nor heed. She has suffered many a
day, Now her griefs have passed away,
God will change her pining sadness Into ever
springing gladness.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Make ye straight what long was crooked,
Make the rougher places plain:
Let your hearts be true and humble,
As befits His holy reign,
For the glory of the Lord O'er the earth is
shed abroad, And all flesh shall see the
token That His Word is never broken.

title: Crown Him With Many Crowns
author: Verses 1, 4, 5, 6 & 9: Matthew Bridges, The Passion of Jesus
source: 'Diademata' George J. Elvey, 1868.  Setting: "Appendix to Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Crown Him with many crowns,
the Lamb upon His throne. Hark!
How the heav'nly anthem drowns all music but
its own. Awake, my soul,
and sing of Him who died for thee,
And hail Him as thy matchless King through
all eternity.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Crown Him the virgin's Son,
the God incarnate born,
Whose arm those crimson trophies won which
now His brow adorn; Fruit of the mystic
rose, as of that rose the stem;
The root whence mercy ever flows,
the Babe of Bethlehem.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Crown Him the Son of God,
before the worlds began,
And ye who tread where He hath trod,
crown Him the Son of Man;
Who every grief hath known that wrings the
human breast, And takes and bears them for
His own, that all in Him may rest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Crown Him the Lord of life,
who triumphed o'er the grave,
And rose victorious in the strife for those
He came to save. His glories now we sing,
Who died, and rose on high,
Who died eternal life to bring,
and lives that death may die.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Crown Him the Lord of peace,
Whose pow'r a scepter sways From pole to
pole, that wars may cease,
and all be prayer and praise.
His reign shall know no end,
and round His pierced feet Fair flow'rs of
paradise extend their fragrance ever sweet.

title: Day of Wrath, O Day of Mourning
author: Thomas of Celano, 13th Century. Translated by William J. Irons
source: 'Dies Irae (Dykes)' John Bacchus Dykes, 1861.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Day of wrath, O day of mourning!
See fulfilled the prophet's warning,
Heav'n and earth in ashes burning. 2. Oh,
what fear man's bosom rendeth When from
Heav'n the Judge descendeth On whose
sentence all dependeth!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Wondrous sound the trumpet flingeth,
Through earth's sepul chers it ringeth,
All before the throne it bringeth. 4.
Death is struck and nature quaking;
All creation is awaking,
To its Judge an answer making.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lo, the book, exactly worded,
Wherein all hath been recorded;
Thence shall judgment be awarded. 6.
When the Judge His seat attaineth And each
hidden deed arraigneth,
Nothing unavenged remaineth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What shall I, frail man, be pleading?
Who for me be interceding When the just are
mercy needing? 8. King of majesty
tremendous, Who dost free sal vation send
us, Fount of pity, then befriend us.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Think, good Jesus, my salvation Caused Thy
wondrous incarnation; Leave me not to
reprobation! 10. Faint and weary Thou hast
sought me, On the cross of suff'ring bought
me; Shall such grace be vainly brought me?

title: Dear Christians, One and All Rejoice
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Es ist Gewisslich an der Zeit' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Dear Christians, one and all rejoice,
With exultation springing,
And with united heart and voice And holy
rapture singing, Proclaim the wonders God
hath done, How his right arm the vict'ry
won; Right dearly it hath cost him.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Fast bound in Satan's chains I lay.
Death brooded darkly o'er me;
Sin was my torment night and day,
Therein my mother bore me.
Deeper and deeper still I fell,
Life was become a living hell,
So firmly sin possessed me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My good works could avail me naught,
For they with sin were stainéd;
Freewill against God's judgment fought,
And dead to good remainéd.
Grief drove me to despair,
and I Had nothing left me but to die,
To hell I fast was sinking.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
God saw, in his eternal grace,
My sorrow out of measure;
He thought upon his tenderness To save was
his good pleasure. He turn'd to me a
Father's heartNot small the cost to heal my
smart He gave his best and dearest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He spake to his beloved Son:
'Tis time to take compassion; Then go,
bright jewel of my crown,
And bring to man salvation;
From sin and sorrow set him free,
Slay bitter death for him,
that he May live with thee forever.

title: Despair Not, O Heart
author: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius (348-413). Translated by O. T. Sanden
source: 'Iam Moesta' or 'Jam Moesta' or 'Despair Not O Heart' or 'Med Sorgen Og Klagen'

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Despair not, O heart, in thy sorrow,
But hope from God's promises borrow Beware
in thy sorrow, of sinning For death is of
life the beginning.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The body is shrouded in mourning;
The garlands, the casket adorning,
Are emblems of hope that be token, O Death,
that thy power is broken.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
When dawneth the glorious morrow,
This body that we view with sorrow,
A glorified form shall be given,
Restored to its spirit in heaven.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The seed that in springtime is planted,
Is hid in the ground, but if granted A
measure of sunshine and showers,
Will spring into fruitage and flowers;

title: Did You Think To Pray?
author: Mary A. Pepper Kidder
source: 'Stockbridge' or 'Did You Think To Pray' William Oscar Perkins, 1876

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ere you left your room this morning,
Did you think to pray?
In the name of Christ our Savior,
Did you sue for loving favor,
As a shield today? O how praying rests the
weary!

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
When you met with great temptation,
Did you think to pray?
By His dying love and merit,
Did you claim the Holy Spirit As your guide
and stay?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When your heart was filled with anger,
Did you think to pray?
Did you plead for grace, my brother,
That you might forgive another Who had
crossed your way?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When sore trials came upon you,
Did you think to pray?
When your soul was bowed in sorrow,
Balm of Gilead did you borrow At the gates
of day?

title: Every Morning Mercies New
author: Greville Phillimore
source: 'Kelso' or 'Every Morning' Edward J. Hopkins, 1872

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Ev'ry morning mercies new Fall as fresh as
morning dew; Ev'ry morning let us pay
Tribute with the early day: For Thy mercies,
Lord, are sure; Thy compassion doth endure.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Still the greatness of Thy love Daily doth
our sins remove; Daily,
far as east from west,
Lifts the burden from the breast;
Gives unbought to those who pray Strength to
stand in evil day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let our prayers each morn prevail,
That these gifts may never fail; And,
as we confess the sin And the tempter's
pow'r within, Feed us with the Bread of
Life, Fit us for our daily strife.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
As the morning light returns,
As the sun with splendor burns,
Teach us still to turn to Thee,
Ever blessed Trinity, With our hands our
hearts to raise, In unfailing prayer and
praise.

title: Faith of Our Fathers
author: Frederick W. Faber
source: 'St. Catherine' Henri F. Hemy (1818-1888).  Setting: James G. Walton, 1874

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Faith of our fathers, living still,
In spite of dungeon, fire and sword;
O how our hearts beat high with joy Whene'er
we hear that glorious Word!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Faith of our fathers, holy faith!
We will be true to thee till death.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Faith of our fathers, we will strive To win
all nations unto Thee;
And through the truth that comes from God,
We all shall then be truly free.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Faith of our fathers, we will love Both
friend and foe in all our strife;
And preach Thee, too, as love knows how By
kindly words and virtuous life.

title: Far, Far Away On Judea's Plains
author: John M. MacFarlane
source: 'Far, Far Away On Judea`s Plains' John M. MacFarlane, 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Far, far away on Judea's plains,
Shepherds of old heard the joyous strains:
Glory to God, glory to God,
Glory to God in the

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Glory to God Glory to God in the highest in
the Glory to God in the highest Glory to God
in the highest; Peace on earth,
good will to men; Peace on earth,
good will to men.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sweet are these strains of redeeming love,
Message of mercy from heaven above:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, with the angels we too would rejoice;
Help us to sing with the heart and voice:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hasten the time when, from every clime,
Men shall unite in the strains sublime:

title: Fear Not, O Little Flock
author: Attr. to King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden (
source: 'Kommt her zu mir, spricht Gottes Sohn' traditional German, 1490

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
As true as God's own word is true,
Not earth nor hell with all their crew
Against us shall prevail.
A jest and byword are they grown;
God is with us, we are His own,
Our vict'ry cannot fail.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Amen, Lord Jesus, grant our prayer!
Great Captain, now Thine arm make bare;
Fight for us once again.
So shall thy saints and martyrs raise A
mighty chorus to Thy praise,
World without end. Amen.

title: For All The Saints
author: William W. How
source: 'Sine Nomine' Ralph Vaughan Williams, 1906.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For all the saints, who from their labors
rest, Who Thee by faith before the world
confessed, Thy Name, O Jesus,
be forever blessed. 4. For the Evangelists,
by whose blest word, Like fourfold streams,
the garden of the Lord,
Is fair and fruitful, be Thy Name adored.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text: Alleluia, Alleluia! Alleluia, Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou wast their Rock, their Fortress and
their Might; Thou, Lord,
their Captain in the well fought fight;
Thou, in the darkness drear,
their one true Light. 5. For Martyrs,
who with rapture kindled eye,
Saw the bright crown descending from the
sky, And seeing, grasped it,
Thee we glorify.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For the Apostles' glorious company,
Who bearing forth the Cross o'er land and
sea, Shook all the mighty world,
we sing to Thee: 6. O blest communion,
fellowship di vine! We feebly struggle,
they in glory shine; All are one in Thee,
for all are Thine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The golden evening brightens in the west;
Soon, soon to faithful warriors comes their
rest; Sweet is the calm of paradise the
blessed. 7. O may Thy soldiers, faithful,
true and bold, Fight as the saints who nobly
fought of old, And win with them the
victor's crown of gold.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But lo! there breaks a yet more glorious
day; The saints triumphant rise in bright
array; The King of glory passes on His way.
8. And when the strife is fierce,
the warfare long, Steals on the ear the
distant triumph song, And hearts are brave,
again, and arms are strong.

title: For The Beauty Of The Earth
author: Folliot S. Pierpoint

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
For the beauty of the earth For the glory of
the skies, For the love which from our birth
Over and around us lies.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Lord of all, to Thee we raise,
This our hymn of grateful praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For the beauty of each hour,
Of the day and of the night, Hill and vale,
and tree and flow'r, Sun and moon,
and stars of light.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For the joy of ear and eye,
For the heart and mind's delight,
For the mystic harmony Linking sense to
sound and sight.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For the joy of human love, Brother, sister,
parent, child, Friends on earth and friends
above, For all gentle thoughts and mild.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
For Thy Church, that evermore Lifteth holy
hands above, Off'ring up on every shore Her
pure sacrifice of love.

title: From Heaven Above To Earth I Come
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Vom Himmel Hoch' traditional German from Schumann's Geistliche Lieder, Leipzig, 1539

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
From Heaven above to earth I come,
To bear good news to every home;
Glad tidings of great joy I bring,
Whereof I now will say and sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To you, this night, is born a Child Of Mary,
chosen mother mild; This tender Child of
lowly birth, Shall be the joy of all your
earth.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
'Tis Christ our God, Who far on high Had
heard your sad and bitter cry;
Himself will your Salvation be,
Himself from sin will make you free.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He brings those blessings long ago Prepared
by God for all below; That in His heavenly
kingdom blest You may with us forever rest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
These are the tokens ye shall mark,
The swaddling clothes and manger dark;
There shall ye find the young Child laid,
By Whom the heav'ns and earth were made.

title: From Nazareth
author: Margaret E. Sangster

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Comes any good from Nazareth?
The scornful challenge as of old Is flung on
many'a jeering breath From cloistered cells
and marts of gold.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Comes any good from Nazareth? Behold,
the mighty Nazarene, The Lord of life,
the Lord of death, Through warring ages
walks serene.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One touch upon His garment's fringe Still
heals the hurt of bitter years.
Before Him yet the demons cringe,
He gives the wine of joy for tears.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O city of the Carpenter,
Upon the hill slope old and gray,
The world among its pain and stir Turns
yearning eyes on thee today.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
For He who dwelt in Nazareth,
And wrought with toil of hand and brain,
Alone gives victor y to faith Until the day
He come again.

title: Gabriel's Message
author: Traditional Basque Carol; Paraphrased by Sabine Baring Gould, (
source: 'Gabriel`s Message' Traditional Basque Carol.  Setting: Edgar Pettman, 1922

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The angel Gabriel from heaven came,
his wings as drifted snow,
his eyes as flame; "All hail," said he,
"thou lowly maiden, Mary,

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text: most highly favored lady," Gloria!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"For know a blessed Mother thou shalt be,
all generations laud and honor thee,
thy Son shall be Emmanuel,
by seers foretold,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Then gentle Mary meekly bowed her head,
"To me be as it pleaseth God," she said,
"my soul shall laud and magnify His holy
Name."

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Of her, Emmanuel, the Christ was born in
Bethlehem, all on a Christmas morn,
and Christian folk throughout the world will
ever say

title: Gentle Mary Laid Her Child
author: Joseph S. Cook
source: 'Tempus Adest Floridum' 13th Century spring carol; first published in the Swedish Piae Cantones, 1582

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Gentle Mary laid her Child lowly in a
manger; There He lay, the undefiled,
to the world a Stranger:
Such a Babe in such a place,
can He be the Savior? Ask the saved of all
