the race who have found His favor.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Gentle Mary laid her Child lowly in a
manger; He is still the undefiled,
but no more a stranger: Son of God,
of humble birth, beautiful the story;
Praise His Name in all the earth,
hail the King of glory!

title: Glorious Things of Thee are Spoken
author: John Newton
source: 'Austria (Haydn)' or 'Austrian Hymn' Franz Joseph Haydn, 1797

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Glorious things of thee are spoken,
Zion city of our God; He,
Whose Word cannot be broken Formed thee for
His Own abode: On the Rock of Ages founded,
What can shake thy sure repose?
With salvation's walls surrounded,
Thou mayst smile at all thy foes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See, the streams of living waters,
Springing from Eternal Love,
Well supply thy sons and daughters,
And all fear of want remove: Who can faint,
while such a river Ever will their thirst
assuage? Grace, which,
like the Lord the Giver,
Never fails from age to age.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Round each habitation hov'ring,
See the cloud and fire appear,
For a glory and a cov'ring:
Showing that the Lord is near.
Thus deriving from their banner Light by
night, and shade by day,
Safe they feed upon the manna,
Which He gives them on their way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Savior, if of Zion's city I, through grace,
a member am, Let the world deride or pity,
I will glory in Thy Name:
Fading is the worldling's pleasure,
All his boasted pomp and show:
Solid joys and lasting treasure None but
Zion's children know.

title: Go To Dark Gethsemane
author: James Montgomery

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Calv'ry's mournful mountain climb; there,
adoring at His feet, Mark that miracle of
time, God's own sacrifice complete.
"It is finished!" hear Him cry;
learn from Jesus Christ to die.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Early hasten to the tomb where they laid His
breathless clay; All is solitude and gloom.
Who has taken Him away? Christ is ris'n!
He meets our eyes; Savior,
teach us so to rise.

title: God Himself is Present
author: Gerhard Tersteegen
source: 'Wunderbarer König' or 'Arnsberg' or 'Groeningen' Joachim Neander, 1680

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God Himself is present:
Let us now adore Him, And with awe ap pear
before Him. God is in His temple,
all within keep silence,
Prostrate lie with deepest reverence.
Him alone God we own, Him our God and
Savior; Praise His name forever.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
God Himself is present:
Hear the harps resounding!
See the crowds the throne surrounding!
"Holy, holy, holy", hear the hymn as
cending, Angels, saints,
their voices blending!
Bow Thine ear to us here: Hear, O Christ,
the praises That Thy Church now raises.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Thou fount of blessing, Purify my spirit;
Trusting only in Thy merit,
Like the holy angels Who behold Thy glory,
May I ceaselessly adore Thee,
Let Thy will Ever still Rule Thy Church
terrestrial, As the hosts celestial.

title: God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen
author: Traditional English
source: 'God Rest Ye Merry Gentlemen' Traditional English.  Setting: "Carols Old And Carols New", 1918

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God rest ye merry, gentlemen,
let nothing you dismay,
Remember Christ our Savior was born on
Christmas Day; To save us all from Satan's
pow'r when we were gone astray.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
O tidings of comfort and joy,
comfort and joy; O tidings of comfort and
joy.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
In Bethlehem, in Israel,
this blessèd Babe was born,
And laid within a manger upon this blessèd
morn; The which His mother Mary did nothing
take in scorn.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
From God our heav'nly Father a blessèd angel
came; And unto certain shepherds brought
tidings of the same; How that in Bethlehem
was born the Son of God by name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Fear not, then," said the angel,
"Let nothing you afright This day is born a
Savior of a pure Virgin bright,
To free all those who trust in Him from
Satan's pow'r and might."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The shepherds at those tidings rejoiced much
in mind, And left their flocks afeeding in
tempest, storm and wind,
And went to Bethl'em straightaway this
blessèd Babe to find.

title: God the Father Be Our Stay
author: 15th Century Litany, adapted by Martin Luther
source: 'Gott Der Vater, Wohn Uns Bei' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God the Father, be our Stay,
When hell's dread pow'rs assail us;

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Cleanse us from our sins, we pray,
Nor in our last hour fail us.
Keep us from the Evil One;
Firm in the faith abiding,
In Christ our Savior hiding,
And heartily confiding.
Let us put God's armor on:
With all true Christians running Our
heav'nly race and shunning The devil's wiles
and cunning. Amen, Amen, this be done,
So sing we, Hallelujah!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text: Jesus Christ be Thou our Stay,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text: Holy Ghost, be Thou our Stay,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text: 1(alt). Triune God, be Thou our Stay,

title: God Will Take Care of You
author: Civilla Durfee Martin
source: 'Martin' Walter Stillman Martin, 1905. Setting: "Alexander's Gospel Songs", 1908

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Be not dismayed whate'er betide,
God will take care of you;
Beneath His wings of love abide,
God will take care of you.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
God will take care of you,
through ev'ry day, o'er all the way;
He will take care of you,
God will take care of you.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Through days of toil when heart doth fail,
God will take care of you;
When dangers fierce your path assail,
God will take care of you.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All you may need He will provide,
God will take care of you;
Nothing you ask will be denied,
God will take care of you.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
No matter what may be the test,
God will take care of you; Lean, weary one,
upon His breast, God will take care of you.

title: God, That Madest Earth and Heaven
author: verse 1, Reginald Heber
source: 'Ar Hyd Y Nos' traditional Welsh.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God, that madest earth and Heaven,
darkness and light; Who the day for toil
hast given, for rest the night;
May Thine angel guards defend us,
Slumber sweet Thy mercy send us;
Holy dreams and hopes attend us,
all through the night.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And when morn again shall call us,
to run life's way, May we still,
whate'er befall us, Thy will obey.
From the pow'r of evil hide us,
In the narrow pathway guide us,
Nor Thy smile be e'er denied us all through
the day.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Guard us waking, guard us sleeping,
and when we die, May we in Thy mighty
keeping all peaceful lie;
When the last dread call shall wake us,
Do not Thou, our God, forsake us,
But to reign in glory take us with Thee on
high.

title: God, Whose Almighty Word
author: John Marriott
source: 'Italian Hymn' Felice de Giardini, 1769.  Setting: "The Methodist Sunday School Hymnal", 1911

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
God, whose almighty word Chaos and darkness
heard And took their flight: Hear us,
we humble pray, And where the Gospel day
Sheds not its glorious ray,
Let there be light!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, who once came to bring,
On your redeeming wing, Healing and sight,
Health to the sick in mind,
Sight to the inly blind: Oh,
now to humankind Let there be light!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Spirit of truth and love, Life giving,
holy dove, Speed forth your flight;
Move on the water's face,
Bearing the lamp of grace,
And in earth's darkest place Let there be
light!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Holy and blessed three, Glorious Trinity,
Wisdom, love, might! Boundless as ocean's
tide, Rolling in fullest pride,
Through the earth, far and wide,
Let there be light!

title: Guide Me, O Thou Great Jehovah
author: William Williams
source: 'Cwm Rhondda' John Hughes, 1907.  Setting: "The Methodist Hymnbook" (UK), 1933

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Guide me, O Thou great Jehovah,
Pilgrim through this barren land. I am weak,
but Thou art mighty; Hold me with Thy
pow'rful hand. Bread of Heaven,
Bread of Heaven, Feed me till I want no
more; Feed me till I want no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Open now the crystal fountain,
Whence the healing stream doth flow;
Let the fire and cloudy pillar Lead me all
my journey through. Strong Deliv'rer,
strong Deliv'rer, Be Thou still my Strength
and Shield; Be Thou still my Strength and
Shield.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, I trust Thy mighty power,
Wondrous are Thy works of old;
Thou deliver'st Thine from thralldom,
Who for naught them selves had sold:
Thou didst conquer, Thou didst conquer, Sin,
and Satan and the grave, Sin,
and Satan and the grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When I tread the verge of Jordan,
Bid my anxious fears subside;
Death of deaths, and hell's destruction,
Land me safe on Canaan's side.
Songs of praises, songs of praises,
I will ever give to Thee;
I will ever give to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Musing on my habitation,
Musing on my heav'nly home,
Fills my soul with holy longings: Come,
my Jesus, quickly come; Vanity is all I see;
Lord, I long to be with Thee! Lord,
I long to be with Thee!

title: Hallelujah, What a Savior!
author: Philip Paul Bliss

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Man of Sorrows! what a name For the Son of
God, who came Ruined sinners to reclaim.
Hallelujah! What a Savior!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
When He comes, our glorious King,
All His ransomed home to bring,
Then anew His song we'll sing:

title: Happy the Man Who Feareth God
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Wo Gott Zum Haus (Walter)' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Happy the man who feareth God,
Whose feet His holy ways have trod;
Thine own good hand shall nourish thee,
And well and happy shalt thou be.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy wife shall, like a fruitful vine,
Fill all thy house with clusters fine;
Thy children all be fresh and sound,
Like oliveplants thy table round.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lo! to the man these blessings cleave Who in
God's holy fear doth live;
From him the ancient curse hath fled By
Adam's race inherited.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Out of Mount Zion God shall send,
And crown with joy thy latter end;
That thou Jerusalem mayst see,
In favor and prosperity.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He shall be with thee in thy ways,
And give thee health and length of days Yea,
thou shalt children's children see,
And peace on Israel shall be.

title: Hark the Glad Sound
author: Philip Doddridge
source: 'Chesterfield' or 'Richmond (Haweis)' or 'Spa Fields Chapel' Thomas Haweis, 1792

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark, the glad sound! the Savior comes!
The Savior promised long;
Let every heart prepare a throne,
And every voice a song.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On Him the Spirit, largely poured,
Exerts its sacred Fire; Wisdom and might,
and zeal and love, His holy Breast inspire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He comes the pris'ners to release,
In Satan's bondage held;
The gates of brass before Him burst,
The iron fetters yield.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He comes from thickest films of vice To
clear the mental ray, And on the eyeballs of
the blind To pour celestial day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He comes the broken heart to bind,
The bleeding soul to cure;
And with the treasures of His grace T'enrich
the humble poor.

title: Hark, Hark, My Soul!
author: Frederick W. Faber
source: 'Finlandia' Jean Sibelius, 1899.  Setting: from Jean Sibelius, 1900

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark! hark, my soul! angelic songs are
swelling O'er earth's green fields and
ocean's wavebeat shore:
How sweet the truth those blessèd strains
are telling Of that new life when sin shall
be no more! Onward we go,
for still we hear them sing, "Come,
weary souls, for Jesus bids you come";

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And through the dark, its echoes sweetly
ringing, The music of the Gospel leads us
home. Far, far away, like bells at ev'ning
pealing, The voice of Jesus sounds o'er land
and sea, And laden souls,
by thou sands meekly stealing,
Kind Shepherd, turn their weary steps to
Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Faith's journeys end in welcome to the
weary, And Heav'n, the heart's true home
will come at last. Angels, sing on,
your faithful watches keeping,
Sing us sweet fragments of the songs above;
Till morning's joy shall end the night of
weeping, And life's long shadows break in
cloudless love.

title: Hark, the Voice of Jesus Calling
author: Daniel March
source: 'Galilean' Joseph Barnby, 1883.  Setting: "In Excelsis", 1911

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark, the voice of Jesus calling,
"Who will go and work today?
Fields are ripe and harvests waiting,
Who will bear the sheaves away?" Long and
loud the Master calls us,
Rich reward He offers free; Who will answer,
gladly saying, "Here am I, send me,
send me?"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
If you cannot cross the ocean,
And the distant lands explore,
You can find the lost around you,
You can help them at your door;
If you cannot give your thousands,
You can give the widow's mite;
What you truly give for Jesus,
Will be precious in His sight.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If you cannot speak like angels,
If you cannot preach like Paul,
You can tell the love of Jesus,
You can say He died for all.
If you cannot rouse the wicked,
With the judgment's dread alarms,
You can lead the little children To the
Savior's waiting arms.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
If you cannot be the watchman,
Standing high on Zion's wall,
Pointing out the path to heaven,
Off'ring life and peace to all,
With your prayers and with your bounties You
can do what heav'n demands;
You can be like faithful Aaron,
Holding up the prophet's hands.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
If among the older people,
You may not be apt to teach,
"Feed My lambs," said Christ, our Shepherd,
"Place the food within their reach." And it
may be that the children You have led with
trembling hand, Will be found among your
jewels, When you reach the better land.

title: Hark! The Herald Angels Sing
author: Charles Wesley
source: 'Mendelssohn' from 'Festgesang' Felix Mendelssohn, 1840.  Setting: William H. Cummings, 1857

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hark! The herald angels sing,
"Glory to the newborn King; Peace on earth,
and mercy mild, God and sinners reconciled!"
Joyful, all ye nations rise,
Join the triumph of the skies;
With th'angelic host proclaim,
"Christ is born in Bethlehem!"

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Hark! the herald angels sing,
"Glory to the newborn King!"

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Christ, by highest Heav'n adored;
Christ the everlasting Lord; Late in time,
behold Him come, Offspring of a virgin's
womb. Veiled in flesh the Godhead see;
Hail th'incarnate Deity,
Pleased with us in flesh to dwell,
Jesus our Emmanuel.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hail the heav'nly Prince of Peace!
Hail the Sun of Righteousness!
Light and life to all He brings,
Ris'n with healing in His wings.
Mild He lays His glory by,
Born that man no more may die.
Born to raise the sons of earth,
Born to give them second birth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, Desire of nations, come,
Fix in us Thy humble home; Rise,
the woman's conqu'ring Seed,
Bruise in us the serpent's head.
Now display Thy saving power,
Ruined nature now restore;
Now in mystic union join Thine to ours,
and ours to Thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Adam's likeness, Lord, efface,
Stamp Thine image in its place:
Second Adam from above,
Reinstate us in Thy love. Let us Thee,
though lost, regain, Thee, the Life,
the inner man: O, to all Thyself impart,
Formed in each believing heart.

title: Have Mercy On Me, O My God
author: Brian L. Penney
source: 'Third Mode Melody' Thomas Tallis, 1567.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Have mercy on me, O my God According to Your
grace; According to Your tender Love Blot
out transgressions great;
For I acknowledge all my sin,
Before my face they stand;
Against You only have I sinned,
There's evil on my hands.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O purge me now and I'll be clean,
As clean and white as snow;
O wash me in the Blood of Christ,
Make me Your gladness know;
Create in me a clean heart, Lord,
Renew me thoroughly; Restore salvation's joy
again, Uphold me tenderly.

title: He Keeps Me Singing
author: Luther B. Bridgers
source: 'He Keeps Me Singing' or 'Melody of Love' Hans Engelmann, 1903

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There's within my heart a melody Jesus
whispers sweet and low, "Fear not,
I am with thee, peace,
be still," In all of life's ebb and flow.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Jesus, Jesus, Jesus,Sweetest name I know,
Fills my ev'ry longing,
Keeps me singing as I go.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
All my life was wrecked by sin and strife,
Discord filled my heart with pain,
Jesus swept across the broken strings,
Stirred the slumb'ring chords again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Feasting on the riches of His grace,
Resting 'neath His shelt'ring wing,
Always looking on His smiling face,
That is why I shout and sing.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though sometimes He leads through waters
deep, Trials fall across the way,
Though sometimes the path seems rough and
steep, See His footprints all the way.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Soon He's coming back to welcome me,
Far beyond the starry sky;
I shall wing my flight to worlds unknown,
I shall reign with Him on high.

title: He Leadeth Me
author: Joseph H. Gilmore
source: 'He Leadeth Me' William B. Bradbury, 1864

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He leadeth me, O blessèd thought!
O words with heav'nly comfort fraught!
Whate'er I do, where'er I be Still 'tis
God's hand that leadeth me.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
He leadeth me, He leadeth me,
By His own hand He leadeth me;
His faithful follow'r I would be,
For by His hand He leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Sometimes mid scenes of deepest gloom,
Sometimes where Eden's bowers bloom,
By waters still, ov'r troubled sea,
Still 'tis His hand that leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, I would place my hand in Thine,
Nor ever murmur nor repine; Content,
whatever lot I see, Since 'tis my God that
leadeth me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And when my task on earth is done,
When by Thy grace the vict'ry's won,
E'en death's cold wave I will not flee,
Since God through Jordan leadeth me.

title: He Was Not Willing
author: Lucy R. Meyer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
"He was not willing that any should perish";
Jesus enthroned in the glory above,
Saw our poor fallen world,
pitied our sorrows, Poured out His life for
us, wonderful love! Perishing, perishing!
Thronging our pathway,
Hearts break with burdens too heavy to bear:
Jesus would save, but there's no one to tell
them, No one to lift them from sin and
despair.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"He was not willing that any should perish";
Clothed in our flesh with its sorrow and
pain, Came He to seek the lost,
comfort the mourner, Heal the heart broken
by sorrow and shame. Perishing, perishing!
Harvest is passing, Reapers are few and the
night draweth near: Jesus is calling thee,
haste to the reaping, Thou shalt have souls,
precious souls for thy hire.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Plenty for pleasure, but little for Jesus;
Time for the world with its troubles and
toys, No time for Jesus' work,
feeding the hungry, Lifting lost souls to
eternity's joys. Perishing, perishing! Hark,
how they call us; Bring us your Savior, oh,
tell us of Him! We are so weary,
so heavily laden, And with long weeping our
eyes have grown dim.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: He Who Would Valiant Be
author: John Bunyan
source: 'Monks Gate' traditional English.  Setting: Ralph Vaughan Williams, 1904

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
He who would valiant be 'gainst all
disaster, Let him in constancy follow the
Master. There's no discouragement shall make
him once relent His first avowed intent to
be a pilgrim.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who so beset him round with dismal stories
Do but themselves confound his strength the
more is. No foes shall stay his might;
though he with giants fight,
He will make good his right to be a pilgrim.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Since, Lord, Thou dost defend us with Thy
Spirit, We know we at the end,
shall life inherit. Then fancies flee away!
I'll fear not what men say,
I'll labor night and day to be a pilgrim.

title: His Gifts
author: Brian J. Dumont

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It's His gift, this creation,
all the glory we see, It's the gift laid out
for Adam and for Eve, But as they turned
away from His world so bright,
It would plunge us deep into fear of the
Light.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Life, life poured out on you and me He calls
us to live and His Glory to see Our Lord
calls us home with Him to be in His presence
living eternally!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It's His gift, incarnation,
He became us to be All the things our fallen
race could never be. Our nature He would
take and then justify,
To the Law's demands Christ would fully
comply.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It's His gift, our redemption,
bought and paid in His blood All God's wrath
poured out in one tremendous flood.
The ransom paid for all in His act of Grace
meant to bring you into His loving embrace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It's His gift, resurrection Raised to life
so that we May also with Him in glory always
be. His new life is God's promise and
guarantee of the gift He prepares for you
and for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
It's His gift, His ascension we await His
return. Not alone, yet for His nearer
presence yearn. Christ leads us to the
Father and makes our home Where we'll sing
together around His Throne.

title: Holy Ghost, with Light Divine
author: verses 1-6 Andrew Reed
source: 'Canterbury' or 'Song 13' Orlando Gibbons, 1623.  Setting: "Common Service Book" (ULCA), 1917

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy Ghost, with light divine Shine upon
this heart of mine; Chase the shades of
night away, Turn the darkness into day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Let me see my Savior's face,
Let me all His beauties trace;
Show those glorious truths to me Which are
only known to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Holy Ghost, with pow'r divine Cleanse this
guilty heart of mine; In Thy mercy pity me,
From sin's bondage set me free.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Holy Ghost, with joy divine Cheer this
saddened heart of mine; Yield a sacred,
settled peace, Let it grow and still
increase.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Holy Spirit, all divine,
Dwell within this heart of mine;
Cast down every idolthrone, Reign supreme,
and reign alone.

title: Holy God, We Praise Thy Name
author: attr. Ignaz Franz
source: 'Te Deum' or 'Hursley' or 'Grosser Gott, wir Loben Dich' from Katholisches Gesangbuch,

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy God, we praise Thy Name; Lord of all,
we bow before Thee! All on earth Thy scepter
claim, All in Heaven above adore Thee;
Infinite Thy vast domain,
Everlasting is Thy reign.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hark! the loud celestial hymn Angel choirs a
bove are raising, Cherubim and seraphim,
In unceasing chorus praising;
Fill the heavens with sweet accord: Holy,
holy, holy, Lord.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lo! the apostolic train Join the sacred Name
to hallow; Prophets swell the loud refrain,
And the white robed martyrs follow;
And from morn to set of sun,
Through the Church the song goes on.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Holy Father, Holy Son, Holy Spirit,
Three we name Thee; While in essence only
One, Undivided God we claim Thee;
And adoring bend the knee,
While we own the mystery.

title: Holy Spirit, Ever Dwelling
author: Timothy Rees
source: 'Ebenezer' or 'Ton-Y-Botel' Thomas J. Williams, 1890.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy Spirit, ever dwelling in the holiest
realms of light Holy Spirit,
ever brooding o'er a world of gloom and
blight Holy Spirit, ever raising earthbound
souls to glory high Living,
lifeimparting Spirit you we praise and
magnify.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Holy Spirit, ever breathing on the church
the breath of life Holy Spirit,
ever striving through your people's
ceaseless strife Holy Spirit,
ever forming in the church the mind of
Christ In our worship we will praise you for
your fruit and gifts unpriced.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Holy Spirit, ever working through the
church's ministry Quick'ning, strength'ning,
and absolving setting captive sinners free
Holy Spirit, ever binding age to age and
soul to soul In community unending you we
worship and extol.

title: Holy, Holy, Holy
author: Reginald Heber
source: 'Nicaea' John Bacchus Dykes, 1861.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
Early in the morning our song shall rise to
Thee; Holy, holy, holy, merciful and mighty!
God in three Persons, blessed Trinity!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy! All the saints adore Thee,
Casting down their golden crowns around the
glassy sea; Cherubim and seraphim falling
down before Thee, Who was, and is,
and evermore shall be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy! though the darkness hide
Thee, Though the eye of sinful man Thy glory
may not see; Only Thou art holy;
there is none beside Thee, Perfect in pow'r,
in love, and purity.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Holy, holy, holy! Lord God Almighty!
All Thy works shall praise Thy Name,
in earth, and sky, and sea; Holy, holy,
holy; merciful and mighty!
God in three Persons, blessed Trinity!

title: Hosanna, Loud Hosanna
author: Jeanette Threlfall
source: 'Ellacombe' from Gesangbuch der Herzogl. Hofkapelle, Wurttemberg, 1784

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Hosanna, loud hosanna,
the little children sang;
Through pillared court and temple the lovely
anthem rang. To Jesus,
Who had blessed them close folded to His
breast, The children sang their praises,
the simplest and the best.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From Olivet they followed mid an exultant
crowd, The victor palm branch waving,
and chanting clear and loud.
The Lord of men and angels rode on in lowly
state, Nor scorned that little children
should on His bidding wait.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
"Hosanna in the highest!" that ancient song
we sing, For Christ is our Redeemer,
the Lord of heav'n our King.
O may we ever praise Him with heart and life
and voice, And in His blissful presence
eternally rejoice!

title: How Firm A Foundation
author: John Rippon
source: 'Foundation (Funk)' or 'Protection' Joseph Funk, 1832.  Setting: "Union Harmony", 1837

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How firm a foundation,
ye saints of the Lord,
Is laid for your faith in His excellent
Word! What more can He say than to you He
hath said, You, who unto Jesus for refuge
have fled?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Fear not, I am with thee, O be not dismayed,
For I am thy God and will still give thee
aid; I'll strengthen and help thee,
and cause thee to stand Upheld by My
righteous, omnipotent hand.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When through the deep waters I call thee to
go, The rivers of woe shall not thee
overflow; For I will be with thee,
thy troubles to bless,
And sanctify to thee thy deepest distress.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When through fiery trials thy pathways shall
lie, My grace, all su fficient,
shall be thy supply; The flame shall not
hurt thee; I only design Thy dross to
consume, and thy gold to refine.

title: How Shall We Answer Terror's Cry?
author: Richard W. Adams
source: 'Melita' John Bacchus Dykes, 1861.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
How shall we answer terror's cry,
The cunning blade, the flaming sky?
When murderous spite knocks down our door
And violence breaks upon our shore,
O let us come and look to You To know Your
will what shall we do?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When Satan whispers, 'Hate your foe,
Now take your vengeance draw the bow,'
Protect us from the tempter's guile,
The lying voice, the evil smile.
O let us come in trust to You,
To hear the word we know is true.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When executioners hung You high You turned
Your prayer up to the sky,
And pled the Father to forgive,
You asked that cruel men might live.
O let us Your ex ample take,
And pray for sinners as we ache.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We pray that You their hearts will turn;
And light a holy fire to burn Their dross
away, so they may be Like gold refined,
eternally. O let us pray that they become,
Like us, with You forever one.

title: I Am Jesus' Little Lamb
author: Henrietta L. von Hayn
source: 'Weil Ich Jesu Schäflein Bin' from Bruder Choral-Buch, 1784

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I am Jesus' little lamb,
Ever glad at heart I am;
For my Shepherd gently guides me,
Knows my need, and well provides me,
Loves me ev'ry day the same,
Even calls me by my name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Day by day, at home, away,
Jesus is my Staff and Stay. When I hunger,
Jesus feeds me, Into pleasant pastures leads
me; When I thirst, He bids me go Where the
quiet waters flow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Who so happy as I am, Even now the
Shepherd's lamb? And when my short life is
ended, By His angel host attended,
He shall fold me to His breast,
There within His arms to rest.

title: I Bind Unto Myself Today
author: attributed to St. Patrick of Ireland (circa 387-466). Paraphrased by Cecil F. Alexander
source: 'St. Patricks Breastplate' Charles V. Stanford, 1902.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I bind unto myself today The strong Name of
the Trinity, By invocation of the same The
Three in One and One in Three.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
2. His bursting from the spicèd tomb,
His riding 3. Confessors' faith,
Apostles' word, The Patriarchs' 4.
The flashing of the lightning free,
The whirling 5. The wisdom of my God to
teach, His hand to up the heav'nly way,
His coming at the day of prayers,
the prophets' scrolls,
All good deeds done unto the wind's
tempestuous shocks, The stable earth,
the deep salt guide, His shield to ward;
The word of God to give me doom I bind unto
myself today. Lord And purity of virgin
souls. sea Around the old eternal rocks.
speech, His heav'nly host to be my guard.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
I bind unto myself the power Of the great
love of cherubim; The sweet "Well done" in
judgment hour, The service of the seraphim,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I bind unto myself today The virtues of the
star lit heaven, The glorious sun's life
giving ray, The whiteness of the moon at
even,

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I bind unto myself today The power of God to
hold and lead, His eye to watch,
His might to stay, His ear to hearken to my
need.

title: I Come, O Savior, To Thy Table
author: Friedrich C. Heyder

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I come, O Savior, to Thy table,
For weak and weary is my soul; Thou,
Bread of Life, alone art able To satisfy and
make me whole:

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Lord, may Thy body and Thy blood Be for my
soul the highest good!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh, grant that I in manner worthy May now
approach Thy heav'nly board And,
as I lowly bow be fore Thee,
Look only unto Thee, O Lord!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Unworthy though I am, O Savior,
Be cause I have a sinful heart,
Yet Thou Thy lamb wilt banish never,
For Thou my faithful Shepherd art:

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh, let me loathe all sin forever As death
and poison to my soul That I through willful
sinning never May see Thy judgment take its
toll!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy heart is filled with fervent yearning
That sinners may salvation see Who, Lord,
to Thee in faith are turning; So I,
a sinner, come to Thee.

title: I Heard The Bells On Christmas Day
author: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
source: 'Waltham (Calkin)' John B. Calkin, 1872.  Setting: "The Book of Common Praise", 1885

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I heard the bells on Christmas day Their old
familiar carols play, And wild and sweet the
words repeat Of peace on earth,
good will to men.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And thought how, as the day had come,
The belfries of all Christendom Had rolled
along th'unbroken song Of peace on earth,
good will to men.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Till ringing, singing on its way The world
revolved from night to day, A voice,
a chime, a chant sublime Of peace on earth,
good will to men.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And in despair I bowed my head "There is no
peace on earth," I said,
"For hate is strong and mocks the song Of
peace on earth, good will to men."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then pealed the bells more loud and deep:
"God is not dead, nor doth He sleep;
The wrong shall fail, the right prevail With
peace on earth, good will to men."

title: I Know That My Redeemer Lives
author: Samuel Medley

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
He lives to bless me with His love,
He lives to plead for me above.
He lives my hungry soul to feed,
He lives to help in time of need.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He lives triumphant from the grave,
He lives eternally to save,
He lives all glorious in the sky,
He lives exalted there on high.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He lives to grant me rich supply,
He lives to guide me with His eye,
He lives to comfort me when faint,
He lives to hear my soul's complaint.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He lives to silence all my fears,
He lives to wipe away my tears He lives to
calm my troubled heart,
He lives all blessings to impart.

title: I Know Whom I Have Believed
author: Daniel Webster Whittle (a.k.a. Elias Nathan)
source: 'I Know Whom I Have Believed' James McGranahan, 1892

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I know not why God's wondrous grace To me He
hath made known, Nor why, unworthy,
Christ in love Redeemed me for His own.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
But I know Whom I have believèd,
And am persuaded that He is able To keep
that which I've committed Unto Him against
that day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I know not how this saving faith To me He
did impart, Nor how believing in His Word
Wrought peace within my heart.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I know not how the Spirit moves,
Convincing us of sin, Revealing Jesus
through the Word, Creating faith in Him.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I know not what of good or ill May be
reserved for me, Of weary ways or golden
days, Before His face I see.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I know not when my Lord may come,
At night or noonday fair,
Nor if I walk the vale with Him,
Or meet Him in the air.

title: I Need Thee Every Hour
author: Annie Sherwood Hawks
source: 'I Need Thee Every Hour' Robert Lowry, 1872.  Setting: "Pentecostal Hymns, No. 2", 1898

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I need Thee ev'ry hour, Most gracious Lord;
No tender voice like Thine Can peace afford.

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
I need Thee ev'ry hour, In joy or pain;
Come quickly and abide, Or life is vain.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I need Thee ev'ry hour, Teach me Thy will;
And Thy rich promises In me fulfill.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I need Thee ev'ry hour, Most Holy One;
O make me Thine indeed, Thou blessed Son!

title: I Place My Trust In God
author: verses by Dorothy Amstutz
source: 'Haly - Trust' Loren J. Kropf, 2010

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I placed my trust in God today,
For it is He who knows the way,
And when uncertainties arise,
I trust His judgment, true and wise.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
I'll place my trust in God today,
Even when I cannot see the way,
He'll lead me on with His strong hand,
Until I reach the promised land.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I placed my trust in God today,
Alone I could not find my way.
Led by His guidance, safe and sure,
I then can rest in peace, secure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I place my trust in God each day, Committed,
yielded to His way. Naught can o'erthrow me
when I'm there Beneath His everlasting care.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I'll place my trust in God each day,
And while I walk the narrow way,
Each burden God will help me bear;
He hears my cry, my ev'ry prayer.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I'll place my trust in God each day, Yes,
even though the skies are gray.
Led by His hand, I will not fear;
I know that God is always near.

title: I Sing the Mighty Power of God
author: Isaac Watts
source: 'Ellacombe' from Gesangbuch der Herzogl. Hofkapelle, Wurttemberg, 1784. Setting: "Amore Dei", 1897

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I sing the mighty pow'r of God,
That made the mountains rise;
That spread the flowing seas abroad,
And built the lofty skies.
I sing the wisdom that ordained The sun to
rule the day: The moon shines full at His
command, And all the stars obey.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I sing the goodness of the Lord,
That filled the earth with food:
He formed the creatures with His word,
And then pronounced them good. Lord,
how Thy wonders are displayed,
Where'er I turn my eye;
If I survey the ground I tread,
Or gaze upon the sky.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There's not a plant or flow'r below,
But makes Thy glories known;
And clouds arise and tempests blow,
By order from Thy throne.
Creatures that borrow life from Thee Are
subject to Thy care: There's not a place
where we can flee, But God is present there.

title: I'm But A Stranger Here
author: Thomas Rawson Taylor
source: 'St. Edmund (Sullivan)' Arthur Seymour Sullivan, 1872.  Setting: "Church Praise, with Tunes", 1885

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I'm but a stranger here, Heav'n is my home;
Earth is a desert drear, Heav'n is my home.
Danger and sorrow stand round me on every
hand; Heav'n is my fatherland,
Heav'n is my home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What though the tempest rage,
Heav'n is my home; Short is my pilgrimage,
Heav'n is my home; Time's wild and wintry
blast soon shall be over past;
I shall reach home at last,
Heav'n is my home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There at my Savior's side Heav'n is my home;
I shall be glorified, Heav'n is my home.
There are the good and blest,
those I loved most and best; There, too,
I soon shall rest, Heav'n is my home.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: If God Had Not Been on Our Side
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Wär Gott nicht mit uns diese Zeit (1524)' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
If God had not been on our side And had not
come to aid us, The foes with all their
pow'r and pride Would surely have dismayed
us; For we, His flock,
would have to fear The threat of men both
far and near Who rise in might against us.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Their furious wrath, did God permit,
Would surely have consumed us And as a deep
and yawning pit With life and limb entombed
us. Like men o'er whom dark waters roll
Their wrath would have en gulfed our soul
And, like a flood, o'erwhelmed us.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest be the Lord, who foiled their threat
That they could not devour us; Our souls,
like birds, escaped their net,
They could not overpow'r us.
The snare is broken we are free!
Our help is ever, Lord, in Thee,
Who madest earth and heaven.

title: If God Himself Be For Me
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Woodbird' or 'Es Flog Ein Kleins Waldvögelein' traditional German found in

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
If God Himself be for me, I may a host defy;
For when I pray, before me My foes,
confounded, fly. If Christ,
my Head and Master, Befriend me from above,
What foe or what disaster Can drive me from
His love?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
This I believe, yea, rather,
Of this I make my boast,
That God is my dear Father,
The Friend who loves me most, And that,
whate'er betide me, My Savior is at hand
Through stormy seas to guide me And bring me
safe to land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I build on this foundation,
That Jesus and His blood Alone are my
salvation, The true, eternal good.
Without Him all that pleases Is valueless on
earth; The gifts I owe to Jesus Alone my
love are worth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My Jesus is my Splendor, My Sun, my Light,
alone; Were He not my Defender Before God's
awefull throne, I never should find favor
And mercy in His sight,
But be destroyed forever As darkness by the
light.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He canceled my offenses,
Delivered me from death;
He is the Lord who cleanses My soul from sin
through faith. In Him I can be cheerful,
Bold, and undaunted aye;
In Him I am not fearful Of God's great
Judgment Day.

title: Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise
author: Walter Chalmers Smith
source: 'St. Denio' or 'Joanna' or 'Palestrina'

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Immortal, invisible, God only wise,
In light inaccessible hid from our eyes,
Most blessèd, most glorious,
the Ancient of Days, Almighty, victorious,
Thy great Name we praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Unresting, unhasting, and silent as light,
Nor wanting, nor wasting,
Thou rulest in might; Thy justice,
like mountains, high soaring above Thy
clouds, which are fountains of goodness and
love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To all, life Thou givest,
to both great and small;
In all life Thou livest,
the true life of all; We blossom and
flourish as leaves on the tree,
And wither and perish but naught changeth
Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Great Father of glory, pure Father of light,
Thine angels adore Thee,
all veiling their sight;
But of Thy rich graces this grace, Lord,
impart Take the veil from our face,
the vile from our heart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
All laud we would render;
O help us to see 'Tis only the splendor of
light hideth Thee, And so let Thy glory,
almighty, impart, Through Christ in His
story, Thy Christ to the heart.

title: In His Temple Now Behold Him
author: verses 1-3, Henry J. Pye
source: 'Westminster Abbey' Henry Purcell, circa 1692.  Setting: Ernest Hawkins, 1843

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
In the arms of her who bore Him,
Virgin pure, behold Him lie,
While his agèd saints adore Him Ere in faith
and hope they die. Hallelujah! Hallelujah!
Lo, th'incarnate God most high.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus, by Thy presentation, Thou,
who didst for us endure,
Make us see our great salvation,
Seal us with Thy promise sure.
And present us in Thy glory To Thy Father,
cleansed and pure.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Prince and Author of salvation,
Be Thy boundless love our theme! Jesus,
praise to Thee be given By the world Thou
didst redeem. With the Father and the
Spirit, Lord of majesty supreme!

title: In Peace and Joy I Now Depart
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Mit Fried und Freud ich Far Dahin' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In peace and joy I now depart At God's
disposing; For full of comfort is my heart,
Soft reposing. So the Lord hath promised me,
And death is but a slumber.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis Christ that wrought this work for me,
My faithful Savior, Whom Thou hast made mine
eyes to see By Thy favor.
Now I know He is my Life,
My Help in need and dying.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Him Thou hast unto all set forth Their great
Salvation And to His kingdom called the
earth, Every nation, By Thy dear and
wholesome Word, In every place resounding.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He is the Hope and saving Light Of lands
benighted; By Him are they who dwelt in
night Fed and lighted.
He is Israel's Praise and Bliss, Their Joy,
Reward, and Glory.

title: In The Bleak MidWinter
author: Christina Georgina Rossetti
source: 'Cranham' Gustav Theodore Holst, 1906, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
In the bleak midwinter,
frosty wind made moan,
Earth stood hard as iron,
water like a stone; Snow had fallen,
snow on snow, snow on snow on snow,
In the bleak midwinter, long ago.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Our God, Heav'n cannot hold Him,
nor earth sustain; Heav'n and earth shall
flee away when He comes to reign.
In the bleak midwinter a stable place
sufficed The Lord God Almighty,
Jesus Christ.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Enough for Him, whom cherubim,
worship night and day, Breastful of milk,
and a mangerful of hay; En ough for Him,
whom angels fall down before,
Ox and ass and camel which adore.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Angels and archangels may have gathered
there, Cherubim and seraphim thronged the
air; But His mother only,
in her maiden bliss, Worshiped the beloved
with a kiss.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: In These Our Days So Perilous
author: Latin c. 6th century, adapted by Martin Luther
source: 'Verleih uns Frieden Gnädiglich' Martin Luther.  Found in Klug's Geistliche Lieder, 1533

sections.label: Verse 1

title: Isaiah, Mighty Seer, In Days of Old
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Jesaia Dem Propheten das Geschah' Martin Luther, 1526 in the German Mass.  Setting: Erythraeus, 1608

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Isaiah, mighty seer, in days of old The Lord
of all in Spirit did behold High on a lofty
throne, in splendor bright,
With flowing train that filled the Temple
quite. Above the throne were stately
seraphim, Six wings had they,
these messengers of Him.
With twain they veiled their faces,
as was meet, With twain in reverent awe they
hid their feet, And with the other twain
aloft they soared, One to the other called
and praised the Lord: "Holy is God,
the Lord of Sabaoth! Holy is God,
the Lord of Sabaoth! Holy is God,
the Lord of Sabaoth! Behold,
His glory filleth all the earth!" The beams
and lintels trembled at the cry,
And clouds of smoke enwrapped the throne on
high.

title: It Came Upon A Midnight Clear
author: Edmund H. Sears

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
It came upon the midnight clear,
That glorious song of old,
From angels bending near the earth,
To touch their harps of gold;
"Peace on the earth, good will to men,
From Heaven's all gracious King." The world
in solemn stillness lay,
To hear the angels sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Still through the cloven skies they come
With peaceful wings unfurled,
And still their heavenly music floats O'er
all the weary world; Above its sad and lowly
plains, They bend on hov'ring wing,
And ever over its Babel sounds The blessèd
angels sing.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet with the woes of sin and strife The
world has suffered long;
Beneath the angel strain have rolled Two
thousand years of wrong; And man,
at war with man, hears not The lovesong
which they bring; O hush the noise,
ye men of strife And hear the angels sing.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And ye, beneath life's crushing load,
Whose forms are bending low,
Who toil along the climbing way With painful
steps and slow, Look now!
for glad and golden hours Come swiftly on
the wing. O rest beside the weary road,
And hear the angels sing!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
For lo! the days are hast'ning on,
By prophetbards foretold,
When with the ever circling years Comes
round the age of gold;
When peace shall over all the earth Its
ancient splendors fling,
And the whole world send back the song Which
now the angels sing.

title: It Is Well With My Soul
author: Horatio G. Spafford

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When peace, like a river, attendeth my way,
When sorrows like sea billows roll;
Whatever my lot, Thou has taught me to say,
It is well, it is well, with my soul.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
It is well, with my soul, It is well,
it is well with my soul. It is well,
with my soul,

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though Satan should buffet,
though trials should come,
Let this blest assurance control,
That Christ has regarded my helpless es
tate, And hath shed His own blood for my
soul.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My sin, oh, the bliss of this glorious
thought! My sin, not in part but the whole,
Is nailed to the cross,
and I bear it no more, Praise the Lord,
praise the Lord, O my soul!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For me, be it Christ, be it Christ hence to
live: If Jordan above me shall roll,
No pang shall be mine,
for in death as in life Thou wilt whisper
Thy peace to my soul.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Jerusalem the Golden
author: Bernard of Cluny
source: 'Ewing' Alexander C. Ewing, 1853.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1861

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jerusalem the golden, with milk and honey
blest, Beneath thy contemplation sink heart
and voice oppressed. I know not,
O I know not, what joys await us there,
What radiancy of glory,
what bliss beyond compare.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They stand, those halls of Zion,
all jubilant with song,
And bright with many'an angel,
and all the martyr throng;
The Prince is ever in them,
the daylight is serene.
The pastures of the blessèd are decked in
glorious sheen.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is the throne of David, and there,
from care released, The shout of them that
triumph, the song of them that feast;
And they are with their Leader,
who conquered in the fight,
And won for them forever their gleaming
robes of white.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O sweet and blessèd country,
the home of God's elect!
O sweet and blessèd country,
that eager hearts expect! Jesus,
in mercy bring us to that dear land of rest,
Who art, with God the Father, and Spirit,
ever blessed.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Brief life is here our portion,
brief sorrow, short lived care;
The life that knows no ending,
the tearless life, is there.
O happy retribution! Short toil,
eternal rest; For mortals and for sinners,
a mansion with the blest.

title: Jesus Came, the Heavens Adoring
author: Godfrey Thring
source: 'Sieh, hier bin ich, Ehrenkoenig' from Geistreiches Gesangbuch Darmstadt, Germany, 1698

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus came, the heav'ns adoring,
Came with peace from realms on high;
Jesus came for man's redemption,
Lowly came on earth to die. Alleluia!
Alleluia! Came in deep humility.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus comes again in mercy,
When our hearts are bowed with care;
Jesus comes again in answer To an earnest,
heartfelt prayer; Alleluia! Alleluia!
Comes to save us from despair.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus comes to hearts rejoicing,
Bringing news of sins forgiv'n;
Jesus comes in sounds of gladness,
Leading souls redeemed to Heav'n; Alleluia!
Alleluia! Now the gate of death is riv'n.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Jesus Christ Is Risen Today
author: 14th Century Bohemian Latin carol. Stanzas 1-3 translated in John Arnold's Compleat Psalmist
source: 'Easter Hymn' from Lyra Davidica, 1708.  Setting: composite found in "Church Praise: with tunes", 1885

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus Christ is ris'n today, Alleluia!
Our triumphant holy day, Alleluia!
Who did once, upon the cross, Alleluia!
Suffer to redeem our loss, Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Hymns of praise then let us sing, Alleluia!
Unto Christ, our heav'nly King, Alleluia!
Who endured the cross and grave, Alleluia!
Sinners to redeem and save, Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But the pain which He endured, Alleluia!
Our salvation hath procured, Alleluia!
Now above the sky He's king, Alleluia!
Where the angels ever sing, Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sing we to our God above, Alleluia!
Praise eternal as His love, Alleluia!
Praise Him, all you heav'nly host, Alleluia!
Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, Alleluia!

title: Jesus Christ Who Came to Save
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Jesus Christus Unser Heiland, Der Den Tod (Klug)' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus Christ, who came to save,
And overcame the grave, Is now arisen,
And sin hath bound in prison. Kyri' eleison.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who withouten sin was found,
Bore our transgression's wound.
He is our Savior, And brings us to God's
favor.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Life and mercy, sin and death,
All in His hands He hath;
Them He'll deliver, Who trust in Him
forever.

title: Jesus Christ, Our Blessed Savior
author: John Hus (
source: 'Jesus Christus Unser Heiland, Der Von Uns (Walter)' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus Christ, our Blessed Savior,
Turned away God's wrath forever;
Suff'ring pains no tongue can tell,
He saved us from the pains of hell.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To remind us that, to save us He hath died,
His flesh He gave us With this bread,
a quick'ning food, And with this wine,
His precious blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Whoso to this board repaireth,
Take good heed how He prepareth;
Death instead of life shall He Receive who
comes unworthily.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Praise the Father, God in heaven,
Who such dainty food hath given,
And for misdeeds thou hast done Gave to die
His beloved Son.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou shalt hold with faith unshaken,
That this food is to be taken By the sick
who are distressed, By those whose heart is
sinoppressed.

title: Jesus Grant That Balm and Healing
author: Johann Heermann
source: 'Der Am Kreuz' Johann Balthasar König, 1738.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, grant that balm and healing In Thy
holy wounds I find, Every hour that I am
feeling, Pains of body and of mind.
Should some evil thought within Tempt my
treacherous heart to sin, Show the peril,
and from sinning Keep me ere its first
beginning.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Should some lust or sharp temptation Prove
too strong for flesh and blood,
Let me think upon Thy Passion,
And the breach is soon made good.
Or should Satan press me hard,
Let me then be on my guard, Saying,
"Christ for me was wounded," That the
tempter flee confounded.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
If the world my heart entices On the broad
and easy road With its mirth and luring
vices, Let me think upon the load Thou didst
carry and endure That I flee all thoughts
impure, Banishing each wild emotion,
Calm and blest in my devotion.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Every wound that pains or grieves me,
By Thy stripes, Lord, is made whole;
When I'm faint, Thy cross revives me,
Granting new life to my soul. Yea,
Thy comfort renders sweet Every bitter cup I
meet; For Thy all atoning Passion Has
procured my soul's salvation.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O my God, my Rock and Tower,
Grant that in Thy death I trust,
Knowing death has lost his power Since Thou
trodd'st him in the dust. Savior,
let Thine agony Ever help and comfort me;
When I die, be my Protection,
Light and Life and Resurrection.

title: Jesus Is All the World To Me
author: Will L. Thompson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus is all the world to me, My life,
my joy, my all; He is my strength from day
to day, Without Him I would fall.
When I am sad, to Him I go,
No other one can cheer me so; When I am sad,
He makes me glad, He's my friend.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus is all the world to me,
my friend in trials sore;
I go to Him for blessings and He gives them
ov'r and o'er. He sends the sunshine and the
rain, He sends the harvest's golden grain;
Sunshine and rain, harvest of grain,
He's my friend.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus is all the world to me,
and true to Him I'll be;
O how could I this friend deny,
when He's so true to me?
Following Him I know I'm right,
He watches o'er me day and night;
Following Him, by day and night,
He's my friend.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Jesus is all the world to me,
I want no better friend; I trust Him now,
I'll trust Him when Life's fleeting days
shall end. Beautiful life with such a
friend; beautiful life that has no end;
Eternal life, eternal joy, He's my friend.

title: Jesus Loves Me
author: Anna B. Warner
source: 'untitled' by William B. Bradbury, 1862.  Setting: William B. Bradbury, 1866

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus loves me! This I know,
For the Bible tells me so.
Little ones to Him belong; They are weak,
but He is strong.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Yes, Jesus loves me! Yes, Jesus loves me!
Yes, Jesus loves me! The Bible tells me so.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus loves me! He who died Heaven's gate to
open wide; He will wash away my sin,
Let His little child come in.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus loves me! He will stay Close beside me
all the way; Thou hast bled and died for me,
I will henceforth live for Thee.

title: Jesus Shall Reign
author: Isaac Watts
source: 'Duke Street' John Hatton, 1793.  Setting: "Christian Hymns", 1908

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus shall reign where'er the sun Does his
suc cessive journeys run;
His kingdom stretch from shore to shore Till
moons shall wax and wane no more.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For Him shall endless prayer be made,
And praises throng to crown His head;
His Name, like sweet per fume shall rise
With every morning sacrifice.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
People and realms of every tongue Dwell on
His love with sweetest song;
And infant voices shall proclaim Their early
blessings on His Name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blessings abound where'er He reigns;
The prisoner leaps to lose his chains,
The weary find e ternal rest,
And all the sons of want are blest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Where He displays His healing power Death
and the curse are known no more;
In Him the tribes of Adam boast More
blessings than their father lost.

title: Jesus Sinners Doth Receive
author: Erdmann Neumeister
source: 'Meinen Jesum Lass` Ich Nicht (Darmstadt)' from Neu-verfertigtes Darmstädtiches Gesang-Buch, 1699

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus sinners doth receive;
Well may we this saying ponder Who in sin's
delusions live, And from God and Heaven
wander: Here is hope for all who grieveJesus
sinners doth receive.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We deserve but grief and shame,Yet His
words, rich grace revealing, Pardon, peace,
and life proclaim; Here their ills have
perfect healing Who with humble hearts
believeJesus sinners doth receive.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
As the shepherd seeks to find His lost sheep
that from Him strayeth,
So hath Christ each soul in mind,
And for its salvation prayeth;
Fain He'd have each wand'rer live:
Jesus sinners doth receive.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Come, then, all by guilt oppressed,
Jesus calls, and He would make you God's own
children, pure and blest,
And to glory He would take you;
Think on this, and well believe Jesus
sinners doth receive.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Savior, now I come to Thee: Great my sins,
a weary burden! Wilt Thou mercy show to me?
Can I hope to find a pardon? I will trust:
my soul relieve! Me, a sinner, Lord,
receive!

title: Jesus Wants All Of His Children
author: verses 1-5 Mrs. James W. Wood
source: 'Blessed Are They' Mrs. James W. Wood, from "Service in Song", Standard Pub. Co., 1909

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus wants all of His children to be good
and true; He will help if we but ask Him,
help us gladly too.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus was so meek and lowly,
As a little child. We will try to be like
Jesus, gentle, patient, mild.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus wants us to be loving,
helping when we may. We will try to be
kindhearted, merciful each day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"Blessed are the pure in heart," thus the
Savior taught. Clean in mind, in soul,
in body, pure in every thought.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When we find our friends are angry,
we will to them say, "Jesus wants you to be
loving, each and every day."

title: Jesus, In Thy Dying Woes
author: Thomas B. Pollock
source: 'Words on the Cross - The Litany' William H. Monk, 1889. Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, in Thy dying woes,
Even while Thy lifeblood flows,
Craving pardon for Thy foes; Hear us,
holy Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Savior, for our pardon sue,
When our sins Thy pangs renew,
For we know not what we do: Hear us,
holy Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O may we, who mercy need,
Be like Thee in heart and deed,
When with wrong our spirits bleed: Hear us,
holy Jesus.

title: Jesus, Joy of Man's Desiring
author: Martin Janus
source: 'Jesus bleibet meine Freude' Johann Schop, 1641 and Johann S. Bach, 1723

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus joy of man's desiring Holy wisdom,
love most bright; Drawn by Thee,
our souls aspiring Soar to uncreated light.
Word of God, our flesh that fashioned,
With the fire of life impassioned,
Striving still to truth unknown, Soaring,
dying round Thy throne.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Through the way where hope is guiding Hark,
what peaceful music rings; Where the flock,
in Thee confiding Drink of joy from
deathless springs. Theirs is beauty's
fairest pleasure; Theirs is wisdom's holiest
treasure. Thou dost ever lead Thine own In
the love of joys unknown.

title: Jesus, King of Glory
author: W. Hope Davison
source: 'St. Alban' Franz Joseph Haydn, 1774.  Setting: John Bacchus Dykes, 1868

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, King of glory, throned above the sky,
Jesus, tender Savior, hear Thy children cry.
Pardon our transgressions,
cleanse us from our sin,
By Thy Spirit help us heav'nly life to win.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Jesus, King of glory, throned above the sky,
Jesus, tender Savior, hear Thy children cry.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On this day of gladness,
Bending low the knee In thine earthly
temple, Lord, we worship thee;
Celebrate thy goodness, Mercy, grace,
and truth, All thy loving guidance Of our
heedless youth.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For the little children Who have come to
thee; For the glad, bright spirits Who thy
glory see; For the loved ones resting In thy
dear em brace; For the pure and holy Who
behold thy face,

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Help us ever steadfast in the faith to be:
In Thy Church's conflicts fighting
valiantly. Loving Savior,
strengthen these weak hearts of ours,
Through Thy cross to conquer crafty evil
powers.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
When the shadows lengthen, show us, Lord,
Thy way; Through the darkness lead us to the
heav'nly day; When our course is finished,
ended all the strife, Grant us,
with the faithful, palms and crowns of life.

title: Jesus, Tender Shepherd, Hear Me
author: Mary L. Duncan

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
All this day thy hand has led me,
And I thank Thee for Thy care;
Thou hast clothed me, warmed and fed me,
Listen to my evening prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let my sins be all forgiven;
Bless the friends I love so well; Take me,
when I die, to heaven,
Happy there with Thee to dwell.

title: Jesus, Thy Boundless Love To Me
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Yoakley' William Yoakley, 1820.  Setting: "The Lute of Zion", 1853

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Jesus, Thy boundless love to me No thought
can reach, no tongue declare;
Unite my thankful heart with Thee And reign
without a rival there. To Thee alone,
dear Lord, I live; Myself to Thee,
dear Lord, I give.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O, grant that nothing in my soul May dwell
but Thy pure love alone! Oh,
may Thy love possess me whole, My joy,
my treasure, and my crown!
All coldness from my heart remove;
My every act, word, thought, be love.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O love, how cheering is thy ray!
All pain before thy presence flies; Care,
anguish, sorrow, melt away Wher e'er thy
healing beams arise. O Jesus,
nothing may I see, Nothing desire or seek,
but Thee!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This love unwearied I pursue And dauntlessly
to Thee aspire. Oh, may Thy love my hope
renew Burn in my soul like heav'nly fire!
And day and night be all my care To guard
this sacred treasure there.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My Savior, Thou Thy love to me In shame,
in want, in pain, hast showed; For me,
on the accursed tree, Thou pourest forth Thy
guiltless blood; Thy wounds upon my heart
impress, Nor aught shall the lov'd stamp
efface.

title: Joy to the World
author: Isaac Watts
source: 'Antioch' pieced together from "Messiah" George F. Handel, 1741.  Setting: Lowell Mason, 1836

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Joy to the world, the Lord is come!
Let earth receive her King;
Let ev'ry heart prepare Him room,
And Heav'n and nature sing,
And Heav'n and nature sing, And Heav'n,
and Heav'n, and nature sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Joy to the earth, the Savior reigns!
Let men their songs employ;
While fields and floods, rocks,
hills and plains Repeat the sounding joy,
Repeat the sounding joy, Repeat, repeat,
the sounding joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No more let sins and sorrows grow,
Nor thorns infest the ground;
He comes to make His blessings flow Far as
the curse is found, Far as the curse is
found, Far as, far as, the curse is found.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He rules the world with truth and grace,
And makes the nations prove The glories of
His righteousness, And wonders of His love,
And wonders of His love, And wonders,
wonders, of His love.

title: Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee
author: Henry J. van Dyke
source: 'Ode to Joy' Ludwig van Beethoven; Adapted by Edward Hodges, 1824

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee, God of glory,
Lord of love; Hearts unfold like flowers
before Thee, opening to the sun above.
Melt the clouds of sin and sadness;
drive the dark of doubt away;
Giver of immortal gladness,
fill us with the light of day!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
All Thy works with joy surround Thee,
earth and heaven reflect Thy rays,
Stars and angels sing around Thee,
center of unbroken praise. Field and forest,
vale and mountain, flowery meadow,
flashing sea, Singing bird and flowing
fountain call us to rejoice in Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou art giving and forgiving,
ever blessing, ever blessed,
Wellspring of the joy of living,
ocean depth of happy rest! Thou our Father,
Christ our Brother, all who live in love are
Thine; Teach us how to love each other,
lift us to the joy divine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Mortals, join the happy chorus,
which the morning stars began;
Father love is reigning o'er us,
brother love binds man to man. Ever singing,
march we onward, victors in the midst of
strife, Joyful music leads us Sunward in the
triumph song of life.

title: Lamp of Our Feet
author: Bernard Barton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lamp of our feet! whereby we trace Our path,
when wont to stray; Stream from the fount of
heav'nly grace! Brook by the trav'ler's way!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Bread of our souls! whereon we feed;
True manna from on high! Our guide,
and chart wherein we read Of realms beyond
the sky.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Pillar of firethrough watches dark!
Or radiant cloud by day!
When waves would whelm our tossing barkOur
anchor and our stay!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Polestar on life's tempestuous deep! Beacon!
when doubts surround; Compass!
by which our course we keep;
Our deep sealead, to sound!

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Let All Mortal Flesh Keep Silence
author: from Liturgy of St. James, 4th Century.  Translated by Gerard Moultrie
source: 'Picardy' traditional French.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let all mortal flesh keep silence,
And with fear and trembling stand;
Ponder nothing earthly minded,
For with blessing in His hand,
Christ our God to earth descendeth,
Our full homage to demand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
King of kings, yet born of Mary,
As of old on earth He stood, Lord of lords,
in human vesture, In the body and the blood;
He will give to all the faithful His own
self for heav'nly food.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Rank on rank the host of heaven Spreads its
vanguard on the way, As the Light of light
descendeth From the realms of endless day,
That the pow'rs of hell may vanish As the
darkness clears away.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
At His feet the six wingèd seraph,
Cherubim with sleepless eye,
Veil their faces to the presence,
As with ceaseless voice they cry: Alleluia,
Alleluia Alleluia, Lord Most High!

title: Let Children Hear The Mighty Deeds
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let children hear the mighty deeds Which God
performed of old; Which in our younger years
we saw, And which our fathers told.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He bids us make His glories known,
His works of pow'r and grace;
And we'll convey His wonders down Through
every rising race.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Our lips shall tell them to our sons,
And they again to theirs;
That generations yet unborn May teach them
to their heirs.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus shall they learn in God alone Their
hope securely stands, That they may ne'er
forget His work But practice His commands.

title: Let Our Gladness Have No End
author: From the Kancional, by Tobias Zavorka
source: 'Narodil se Kristus Pán' or 'Salvator Natus' 15th Century Bohemian

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Let our gladness have no end, Hallelujah!
For to earth did Christ descend.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Hallelujah! On this day God gave us Christ,
His Son, to save us; Christ, His Son,
to save us.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See, the loveliest blooming rose,
Hallelujah! From the branch of Jesse grows.
Hallelujah!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Into flesh is made the Word. Hallelujah! He,
our refuge and our Lord. Hallelujah!

title: Lift High The Cross
author: George W. Kitchin (
source: 'Crucifier' Sydney H. Nicholson, 1916.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1922

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Come, brethren, follow where our Captain
trod, our King victorious,
Christ the Son of God.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Lift high the cross, the love of Christ
proclaim, Till all the world adore His
sacred Name.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Led on their way by this triumphant sign,
The hosts of God in conquering ranks
combine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Each newborn servant of the Crucified Bears
on the brow the seal of Him Who died.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This is the sign which Satan's legions fear
and angels veil their faces to revere.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Saved by this Cross whereon their Lord was
slain, the sons of Adam their lost home
regain.

title: Lift Up Your Heads, Ye Mighty Gates
author: Georg Weissel
source: 'Milwaukee' or 'Macht hoch die Tür (Lemke)' August Lemke, 1849

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lift up your heads, ye mighty gates! Behold,
the King of glory waits;
The King of kings is drawing near,
The Savior of the world is here;
Life and salvation doth He bring,
Wherefore rejoice and gladly sing:
We praise Thee, Father, now! Creator,
wise art Thou!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Lord is just, a Helper tried,
Mercy is ever at His side,
His kingly crown is holiness, His scepter,
pity in distress, The end of all our woe He
brings; Wherefore the earth is glad and
sings: We praise Thee, Savior, now!
Mighty in deed art Thou!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O blest the land, the city blest,
Where Christ the Ruler is con fessed!
O happy hearts and happy homes To whom this
King in tri umph comes!
The cloudless Sun of joy He is,
Who bringeth pure de light and bliss.
O Comforter divine, What boundless grace is
Thine!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Fling wide the portals of your heart;
Make it a temple, set a part From earthly
use for heav'ns employ,
Adorned with prayer and love and joy;
So shall your Sovereign enter in,
and new and nobler life begin; To Thee,
O God, be praise, For Word, and deed,
and grace!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Redeemer, come! I open wide My heart to
Thee; here, Lord, a bide!
Let me Thy inner presence feel,
Thy grace and love in me reveal.
Thy Holy Spirit guide us on,
Until our glorious goal be won!
Eternal praise and fame We offer to Thy
Name.

title: Lo, God To Heav'n Ascendeth
author: Gottfried Wilhelm Sacer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo, God to Heav'n ascendeth!
Throughout its regions vast With shouts
triumphant blendeth the trumpet's thrilling
blast: Sing praise to Christ the Lord;
sing praise with exultation,
King of each heathen nation,
the God of Hosts adored!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With joy is Heav'n resounding Christ's glad
return to see; Behold the saints surrounding
the Lord who set them free. Bright myriads,
thronging, come; the cherub band rejoices,
And loud seraphic voices Welcome Messiah
home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
No more the way is hidden,
Since Christ our Head arose:
No more to man forbidden The road to Heav'n
that goes. Our Lord is gone before;
yet here He will not leave us,
And soon in Heav'n receive us and open wide
the door.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Christ is our place preparing; to Heav'n we,
too, shall rise, And, joys angelic sharing,
Be where our treasure lies:
There may each heart be found!
Where Jesus Christ has entered,
There let our Hope be centered;
Our course still heav'nward bound.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
May we, His servants, thither In heart and
mind ascend, And let us sing together:
"We seek Thee, Christ, our friend, Thee,
God's exalted Son, our Life,
and Way to Heaven, To whom all pow'r is
given, our Joy and Hope and Crown."

title: Lo, How A Rose E'er Blooming
author: verses 1-2, 15th Century German.  Translated by Theodore Baker
source: 'Es Ist Ein Ros Entsprungen (Rhythmic)' German from Köln, 1599.  Setting: Michael Praetorius, 1609

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo, how a Rose e'er blooming from tender
stem hath sprung! Of Jesse's lineage coming,
as men of old have sung. It came,
a flow'ret bright, amid the cold of winter,
When half spent was the night.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Isaiah 'twas foretold it,
the Rose I have in mind;
With Mary we behold it,
the virgin mother kind.
To show God's love aright,
she bore to men a Savior,
When half spent was the night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The shepherds heard the story proclaimed by
angels bright, How Christ,
the Lord of glory was born on earth this
night. To Bethlehem they sped and in the
manger found Him, As angel heralds said.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This Flow'r, whose fragrance tender with
sweetness fills the air,
Dispels with glorious splendor the darkness
everywhere; True Man, yet very God,
from sin and death He saves us,
And lightens ev'ry load.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O Savior, Child of Mary,
who felt our human woe, O Savior,
King of glory, who dost our weakness know;
Bring us at length we pray,
to the bright courts of Heaven,
And to the endless day!

title: Lo! He Comes With Clouds Descending
author: John Cennick
source: 'Helmsley' attr. Thomas Olivers, 1765.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lo! He comes with clouds descending,
Once for ev'ry sinner slain;
Thousand thousand saints attending,
Swell the triumph of His train: Hallelujah!
Halle lujah! Hallelujah!
God appears on earth to reign.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Ev'ry eye shall now behold Him Robed in
dreadful majesty; Those who set at naught
and sold Him, Pierced and nailed Him to the
tree, Deeply wailing, deeply wailing,
deeply wailing, Shall the true Messiah see.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ev'ry island, sea, and mountain,
Heav'n and earth, shall flee away;
All who hate Him must, confounded,
Hear the trump proclaim the day:
Come to judgment! Come to judgment!
Come to judgment! Come to judgment!
Come away!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now redemption, long expected,
See in solemn pomp appear; All His saints,
by man rejected, Now shall meet Him in the
air: Hallelujah! Halle lujah! Hallelujah!
See the day of God appear!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Answer Thine own bride and Spirit, Hasten,
Lord, the gen'ral doom!
The new Heav'n and earth inherit,
Take Thy pining exiles home: All creation,
all cre ation, all creation, Travails!
groans! and bids Thee come!

title: Look Down, O Lord, From Heaven Behold
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Ach Gott vom Himmel' from Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524.  Setting: Karl August Haupt, 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Look down, O Lord, from heav'n behold,
And let thy pity waken!
How few the flock within thy fold,
Neglected and forsaken!
Almost thou'lt seek for faith in vain,
And those who should thy truth maintain Thy
Word from us have taken.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With frauds which they themselves invent Thy
truth they have confounded;
Their hearts are not with one consent On thy
pure doctrine grounded; And,
whilst they gleam with outward show,
They lead thy people to and fro,
In error's maze astounded.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
God surely will uproot all those With vain
deceits who store us, With haughty tongue
who God oppose, And say,
"Who'll stand before us?
By right or might we will prevail;
What we determine cannot fail,
For who can lord it o'er us?"

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
For this, saith God, I will arise,
These wolves my flock are rending;
I've heard my people's bitter sighs To
heav'n my throne ascending: Now will I up,
and set at rest Each weary soul by fraud
