opprest, The poor with might defending.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The silver sev'n times tried is pure From
all adulteration; So, through God's word,
shall men endure Each trial and temptation:
Its worth gleams brighter through the cross,
And, purified from human dross,
It shines through every nation.

title: Lord God, Thy Praise We Sing
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Herr Gott, dich loben wir' ancient Latin, alt by Martin Luther. Found in Klug's Gesangbuch, 1535

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To save mankind Thou hast not, Lord,
The Virgin Mary's womb abhorred;

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Lord God, Thy praise we sing;
Father in eternity, Lord God,
our thanks we bring; Angels all and heav'nly
host All the world worships Thee.
Of Thy glory loudly boast;
Both Cherubim and Seraphim Holy art Thou,
our God! Sing ever with loud voice this
hymn: Holy art Thou, our God,
the Lord of Sabaoth! Holy art Thou, our God!
Holy art Thou, our God, the Lord of Sabaoth!
Thy majesty and godly might Fill the earth
and all the realms of light.
The twelve apostles join in song The
martyrs' noble army raise The universal
Church doth Thee With the dear prophets'
goodly throng Their voice to Thee in hymns
of praise. Throughout the world confess to
be Thee, Father, on Thy highest throne,
Thy worthy, true, and well belov'd Son,
The Comforter, ev'n the Holy Ghost,
Whereof she makes her constant boast.
Thee King of all glory, Christ, we own,
Th'eternal Father's eternal Son.
Thy servants help whom Thou, O God,
Hast ransomed with that precious blood;
Grant that we share the heav'nly rest With
the happy saints eternally blest. Help us,
O Lord, from age to age,
And bless Thy chosen heritage.
Nourish and keep them by Thy pow'r,
And lift them up for evermore. Lord God,
we praise Thee day by day,
And sanctify Thy Name always.
Keep us this day, and at all times,
For mercy only, Lord, we plead;
Show us Thy mercy, Lord,
as we From secret sins and open crimes;
Be merciful to our great need.
Our steadfast trust repose in Thee. In Thee,
Lord, have we put our trust;
O never let our hope be lost! Amen. Amen.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thou over camest death's sharp sting,
Believers unto heav'n to bring;

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
At God's right hand Thou sittest,
clad In th'glory with the Father had;

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou shalt in glory come again,
To judge both dead and living men.

title: Lord Jesus Think On Me
author: Synesius of Cyrene, circa 430.  Translated by Allen W. Chatfield
source: 'Southwell' William Daman's Psalter, 1579.  Setting: "Common Service Book" (ULCA), 1917

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, think on me And purge away my
sin; From earthborn passions set me free And
make me pure within.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, think on me,
With many'a care oppressed;
Let me Thy loving servant be And taste Thy
promised rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, think on me Amid the battle's
strife; In all my pain and misery Be Thou my
Health and Life.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, think on me Nor let me go
astray; Through darkness and perplexity
Point Thou the heav'nly way.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, think on me When floods the
tempest high; When on doth rush the enemy,
O Savior, be Thou nigh!

title: Lord of Glory, Who Hast Bought Us
author: Eliza S. Alderson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of Glory, who hast bought us with Thy
lifeblood as the price,
Never grudging for the lost ones that
tremendous sacrifice; And with that hast
freely given blessings countless as the
sand, To th'unthankful and the evil with
Thine own unsparing hand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Grant us hearts, dear Lord,
to yield Thee gladly, freely, of Thine own.
With the sunshine of Thy goodness melt our
thankless hearts of stone.
Till our cold and selfish natures,
warmed by Thee, at length believe That more
happy and more blessed 'tis to give than to
receive.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wondrous honor hast Thou given to our
humblest charity. In Thine own mysterious
sentence, "Ye have done it unto Me." Can it
be, O gracious Master,
Thou dost deign for alms to sue,
Saying by Thy poor and needy,
"Give as I have given you"

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord of Glory, who hast bought us with Thy
lifeblood as the price,
Never grudging for the lost ones that
tremendous sacrifice; Give us faith,
to trust Thee boldly; hope,
to stay our souls on Thee; But O,
best of all Thy graces,
give us Thine own charity.

title: Lord of Life, All Praise Excelling
author: Clement C. Moore
source: 'HyFrydol' Rowland H. Prichard, 1830.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of life, all praise excelling, Thou,
in glory unconfined, Deignst to make Thy
humble dwelling With the poor of humble
mind. As Thy love, through all creation,
Beams like Thy diffusive light;
So the high and humble station Both are
equal in Thy sight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thus Thy care, for all providing,
Warmed Thy faithful prophet's tongue; Who,
the lot of all deciding,
To Thy chosen Israel sung.
When Thy harvest yields Thee pleasure,
Thou the golden sheaf shalt bind;
To the poor belongs the treasure Of the
scattered ears behind.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Still we read Thy Word declaring Mercy,
Lord, Thine own decree;
Mercy ev'ry sorrow sharing,
Warms the heart resembling Thee.
Still the orphan and the stranger,
Still the widow owns Thy care;
Screened by Thee in ev'ry danger,
Heard by Thee in ev'ry prayer.

title: Lord Of Our Life
author: Matthäus Apelles von Löwenstern
source: 'Iste Confessor' or 'Rouen' from Poitiers Antiphoner, 1746

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord of our life, and God of our salvation,
Star of our night, and Hope of every nation,
Hear and receive Thy church's supplication,
Lord God Almighty.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
See round Thine Ark the hungry billows
curling! See how Thy foes their banners are
unfurling! Lord, while their darts en
venomed they are hurling,
Thou canst preserve us.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, Thou canst help when earthly armor
faileth; Lord, Thou canst save when sin
itself assaileth; Lord,
o'er Thy Rock nor death nor hell prevaileth;
Grant us Thy peace, Lord.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Peace, in our hearts, our evil thoughts
assuaging, Peace, in Thy Church,
where brothers are engaging, Peace,
when the world its busy war is waging;
Calm Thy foes raging!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Grant us Thy help till backward they are
driven; Grant them Thy Truth,
that they may be forgiven;
Grant peace on earth, and after we have
striven, Peace in Thy Heaven.

title: Lord Who Throughout These Forty Days
author: Claudia F. Hernaman

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, who throughout these forty days For us
didst fast and pray, Teach us with Thee to
mourn our sins And close by Thee to stay.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
As Thou with Satan didst contend,
And didst the vict'ry win,
O give us strength in Thee to fight,
In Thee to conquer sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
As Thou didst hunger bear, and thirst,
So teach us, gracious Lord, To die to self,
and chiefly live By Thy most holy Word.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And through these days of penitence,
And through Thy passiontide, Yea,
evermore in life and death, Jesus,
with us abide.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Abide with us, that so,
this life Of suff'ring over past,
An Easter of unending joy We may attain at
last.

title: Lord, Dismiss Us With Thy Blessing
author: John Fawcett
source: 'Regent Square' Henry Smart, 1867.  Setting: "Psalms and Hymns for Divine Worship", 1867

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Thanks we give and adoration For Thy
Gospel's joyful sound;
May the fruits of Thy salvation In our
hearts and lives abound. Ever faithful,
ever faithful, To the truth may we be found.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So that when Thy love shall call us, Savior,
from the world away, Fear of death shall not
appall us, Glad Thy summons to obey.
May we ever, may we ever,
Reign with Thee in endless day.

title: Lord, Enthroned in Heavenly Splendor
author: George H. Bourne
source: 'Bryn Calfaria' William Owen, 1852.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, enthroned in heav'nly splendor,
First begotten from the dead, You alone,
our strong Defender, Now lift up Your
people's head. Jesus, true and living Bread!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Jesus, true and living Bread! Alleluia!
Alleluia! Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Here our humblest homage pay we,
Here in loving reference bow;
Here for faith's discernment pray we,
Lest we fail to know You now. Thou art here,
we ask not how. Thou art here,
we ask not how.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though the lowliest form doth veil Thee As
of old in Bethlehem, Here as there Thine
angels hail Thee, Branch and Flow'r of
Jesse's stem. We in worship join with them.
We in worship join with them.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Paschal Lamb, Your offering finished Once
for all when You were slain,
In its fullness undiminished Shall
forevermore remain. Cleansing souls from
every stain. Cleansing souls from every
stain.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Great High Priest of our profession,
Through the veil Thou wentest in,
By Thy mighty intercession,
Grace and peace for us to win. Jesus,
true and living Bread!

title: Lord, Keep Us Steadfast in Thy Word
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Erhalt Uns, Herr, bei deinem Wort' from Klug's "Geistliche Lieder auffs new gebessert", 1543

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, keep us steadfast in Thy Word;
Curb those who fain by craft and sword Would
wrest the kingdom from Thy Son And set at
naught all He hath done.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord Jesus Christ, Thy pow'r make known,
For Thou art Lord of lords alone;
Defend Thy Christendom that we May evermore
sing praise to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Comforter of priceless worth,
Send peace and unity on earth.
Support us in our final strife And lead us
out of death to life.

title: Lord, Thee I Love with All My Heart
author: Martin Schalling, circa
source: 'Herzlich Lieb hab ich Dich O Herr' Strassburg, 1577.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, Thee I love with all my heart;
I pray Thee, ne'er from me depart;
With tender mercy cheer me.
Earth has no pleasure I would share, Yea,
Heav'n itself were void and bare If Thou,
Lord, wert not near me.
And should my heart for sorrow break,
My trust in Thee can nothing shake.
Thou art the portion I have sought;
Thy precious blood my soul has bought.
Lord Jesus Christ, My God and Lord,
my God and Lord, Forsake me not!
I trust Thy Word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Yea, Lord, 'twas Thy rich bounty gave My
body, soul, and all I have In this poor life
of labor. Lord, grant that I in every place
May glorify Thy lavish grace And serve and
help my neighbor. Let no false doctrine me
beguile, Let Satan not my soul defile.
Give strength and patience unto me To bear
my cross and follow Thee. Lord Jesus Christ,
My God and Lord, my God and Lord,
In death Thy comfort still afford.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, let at last Thine angels come,
To Abr'am's bosom bear me home,
That I may die unfearing;
And in its narrow chamber keep My body safe
in peaceful sleep Until Thy reappearing.
And then from death awaken me,
That these mine eyes with joy may see,
O Son of God, Thy glorious face,
My Savior and my fount of grace.
Lord Jesus Christ, My prayer attend,
my prayer attend, And I will praise Thee
without end!

title: Lord, Who at Cana's Wedding Feast
author: Adelaide Thrupp

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Lord, who at Cana's wedding feast Didst as a
Guest appear, Thou dearer far than earthly
guest, Vouchsafe Thy presence here.
For holy Thou indeed dost prove The marriage
vow to be, Proclaiming it a type of love
Between the Church and Thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The holiest vow that man can make,
The golden thread in life,
The bond that none may dare to break,
That bindeth man and wife, Which,
blest by Thee, whate'er betide,
No evil shall destroy,
Through careworn days each care divides And
doubles every joy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
On those who at Thine altar kneel, O Lord,
Thy blessing pour, That each may wake the
other's zeal To love Thee more and more. Oh,
grant them here in peace to live,
In purity and love, And, this world leaving,
to receive A crown of life above.

title: Magnificat
author: Brian L. Penney
source: public domain.  This score is a part of the Open Hymnal Project, 2009 Revision

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My soul shall magnify the Lord,
And with my spirit I rejoice;
My Savior has regard for me,
He hears His lowly servant's voice.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Behold, I am forever blessed,
For God has done great things for me;
His mercy rests on those who fear,
Who honor His Name most holy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Lord has shown His mighty arm,
Those proud in heart He shall put down;
The haughty from their thrones re moved,
The lowly have God's blessing found.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The hungry with good things are filled,
They see God's kindness ev'ry day;
But on the rich no blessing rests,
With empty hands they're sent away.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The Lord helps His beloved ones,
In mercy He His cov'nant keeps;
Just as He promised long a go, to Abraham,
and to his Seed.

title: May God Bestow on Us His Grace
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Es Wollt uns Gott Genædig' adapted from older German hymn by Martin Luther. Found in Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
May God bestow on us His grace,
With blessings rich provide us,
And may the brightness of His face To life
eternal guide us That we His saving health
may know, His gracious will and pleasure,
And also to the heathen show Christ's riches
without measure And unto God convert them.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thine over all shall be the praise And
thanks of every nation,
And all the world with joy shall raise The
voice of exultation; For Thou shalt judge
the earth, O Lord, Nor suffer sin to
flourish; Thy people's pasture is Thy Word
Their souls to feed and nourish,
In righteous paths to keep them.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, let the people praise Thy worth,
In all good works increasing;
The land shall plenteous fruit bring forth,
Thy Word is rich in blessing.
May God the Father, God the Son,
And God the Spirit bless us!
Let all the world praise Him alone,
Let solemn awe possess us.
Now let our hearts say, Amen.

title: Moment By Moment
author: Daniel W. Whittle

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
Never a trial that He is not there,
Never a burden that He doth not bear,
Never a sorrow that He doth not share,
Moment by moment, I'm under His care.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Never a heartache, and never a groan,
Never a teardrop and never a moan;
Never a danger but there on the throne,
Moment by moment He thinks of His own.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Never a weakness that He doth not feel,
Never a sickness that He can not heal;
Moment by moment, in woe or in weal,
Jesus my Savior, a bides with me still.

title: More Love to Thee
author: Elizabeth Payson Prentis
source: 'More Love to Thee' William Howard Doane, 1870.  Setting: William Howard Doane, 1870, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
More love to Thee, O Christ;
More love to Thee; Hear Thou the pray'r I
make On bended knee; This is my earnest
plea, More love, O Christ, to Thee,
More love to Thee; More love to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Then shall my latest breath,
Whisper Thy praise, This be the parting cry
My heart shall raise; This still its pray'r
shall be, More love, O Christ, to Thee,
More love to Thee; More love to Thee.

title: My Faith Looks Up To Thee
author: Ray Palmer

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My faith looks up to Thee,
Thou Lamb of Calvary, Savior divine!
Now hear me while I pray,
take all my guilt away,
O let me from this day be wholly Thine!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
May Thy rich grace impart Strength to my
fainting heart, my zeal inspire!
As Thou hast died for me,
O may my love to Thee, Pure warm,
and changeless be, a living fire!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While life's dark maze I tread,
And griefs around me spread,
be Thou my Guide; Bid darkness turn to day,
wipe sorrow's tears away,
Nor let me ever stray from Thee aside.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When ends life's transient dream,
When death's cold sullen stream over me
roll; Blest Savior, then in love,
fear and dis trust remove;
O bear me safe above, a ransomed soul!

title: My Hope Is Built
author: Edward Mote, circa
source: 'Melita' John Bacchus Dykes, 1861.  Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1869

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My hope is built on nothing less Than Jesus'
blood and righteousness.
I dare not trust the sweetest frame,
But wholly trust in Jesus' Name.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
On Christ the solid Rock I stand,
All other ground is sinking sand.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
When darkness veils His lovely face,
I rest on His un changing grace.
In every high and stormy gale,
My anchor holds within the veil.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His oath, His covenant, His blood,
Support me in the whelming flood.
When all around my soul gives way,
He then is all my hope and stay.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When He shall come with trumpet sound,
Oh may I then in Him be found.
Dressed in His righteousness alone,
Fault less to stand before the throne.

title: My Jesus, As Thou Wilt
author: Benjamin Schmolck, circa
source: 'Jewett' or 'Weber' Carl M. von Weber, 1821.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt! Oh,
may Thy will be mine! Into Thy hand of love
I would my all resign; Through sorrow,
or through joy, conduct me as Thine own,
And help me still to say, my Lord,
Thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
If needy here and poor,
Give me Thy people's bread,
their portion rich and sure.
The manna of Thy Word Let my soul feed upon;
And if all else should fail, my Lord,
thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
Though seen through many'a tear,
Let not my star of hope grow dim or
disappear; Since Thou on earth hast wept,
and sorrowed oft alone,
If I must weep with Thee, my Lord,
Thy will be done!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My Jesus, as Thou wilt!
All shall be well for me;
Each changing future scene I gladly trust
with Thee: Straight to my home above I
travel calmly on, And sing,
in life or death, my Lord, Thy will be done!

title: My Neighbor
author: John G. Fleischmann
source: 'Tallis` Canon' Thomas Tallis, circa 1567.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Unclean and battered, torn by sin,
By things I do, my thoughts within,
I lie there bloodied on life's road with
death and sin my only load.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Across that road the world passed by turning
a deaf ear to my cry, No help to give,
they could not save and so they left me for
my grave.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And, what of me, when I saw need?
Did I my Savior's bidding heed?
Too often on the other side I've walked away
because of pride.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sin bleeds from me and stops my breath,
in Adam all I know is death;
My works are rags, my offerings vain,
From dust I came in dust remain.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But in my need my Savior died,
Not passing on the other side.
Rebreathed His Spirit in my dust,
bound up my wounds, declared me just.

title: My Savior's Love
author: Charles H. Gabriel
source: 'My Savior`s Love' or 'I Stand Amazed in the Presence' Charles H. Gabriel, 1905

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I stand amazed in the presence Of Jesus the
Nazarene, And wonder how He could love me,
A sinner, condemn'd, unclean.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
How marvelous! how wonderful!
And my song shall ever be: O how marvelous!
O how wonderful! And my song shall ever be:
How marvelous! how wonderful!
Is my Savior's love for me! O how marvelous!
O how wonderful! Is my Savior's love for me!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For me it was in the garden He pray'd "Not
my will, but Thine;" He had no tears for His
own griefs, But sweat drops of blood for
mine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In pity angels beheld Him,
And came from the world of light To comfort
Him in the sorrows, He bore for my soul that
night.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When with the ransomed in glory His face I
at last shall see, 'Twill be my joy thro'
the ages, To sing of His love for me.

title: My Song Shall Be Of Jesus
author: Fanny J. Crosby
source: 'Sondance' Kenneth W. Paxton, 1998.  Setting: Kenneth W. Paxton, 1998

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My song shall be of Jesus,
His Mercy crowns my days He fills my cup
with blessings and tunes my heart to praise
My song shall be of Jesus the precious Lamb
of God Who gave Himself my ransom and bought
me with His blood

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
And when my soul shall enter the many
mansions fair, A song of praise to Jesus
I'll sing forever there.
A song of praise to Jesus I'll sing forever.
My song shall be of Jesus.
I'll sing forever. My song shall be of
Jesus.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My song shall be of Jesus,
while sitting at His feet He calls to mind
His goodness, and makes my joy complete;
My song shall be of Jesus,
whatever ills befall, I'll sing the grace
that saves me, and triumphs over all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
My song shall be of Jesus,
when pressing on my way To where my home
shines glorious in pure and perfect day.
And when my soul shall enter the many
mansions fair, A song of praise to Jesus
I'll sing forever there.

title: My Soul, Now Praise Thy Maker
author: Johann Graumann
source: 'Nun Lob, Mein Seel' from Johannes Kugelmann`s Concentus Novi, 1540

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
My soul, now praise thy maker!
Let all within me bless His name Who maketh
thee partaker Of mercies more than thou
dar'st claim. Forget Him not whose meekness
Still bears with all thy sin,
Who healeth all thy weakness,
Renews thy life within.
Whose grace and care are endless And saved
thee through the past;
Who leaves no suff'rer friendless,
But rights the wronged at last.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He shows to man His treasure Of judgment,
truth, and righteousness,
His love beyond all measure,
His yearning pity o'er distress,
Nor treats us as we merit,
But lays His anger by. The humble,
contrite spirit Finds His compassion nigh;
And high as Heav'n above us,
As break from close of day, So far,
since He doth love us,
He puts our sins away.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For as a tender father Hath pity on his
children here, He in His arms will gather
All who are His in childlike fear.
He knows how frail our powers Who but from
dust are made; We flourish like the flowers,
And even so we fade; The wind but o'er them
passes, And all their bloom is o'er We
wither like the grasses,
Our place knows us no more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
God's grace alone endureth,
And children's children yet shall prove How
He with strength assureth The hearts of all
that seek His love. In Heav'n is fixed His
dwelling, His rule is over all; Angels,
in might excelling, Bright hosts,
before Him fall. Praise Him who ever
reigneth, All ye who hear His Word,
Nor our poor hymns disdainethMy soul,
O praise the Lord!

title: Nearer, My God, To Thee
author: st. 1-2 by Sarah F. Adams
source: 'Bethany (Mason)' Lowell Mason, 1856.  Setting: Lowell Mason, 1859

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Nearer, my God, to Thee, nearer to Thee!
E'en though it be a cross that raiseth me,
Still all my song shall be, nearer, my God,
to Thee.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Nearer, my God, to Thee, Nearer to Thee! 5.
Then evermore to be Nearer to Thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though like the wanderer, the sun gone down,
Darkness be over me, my rest a stone.
Yet in my dreams I'd be nearer,
my God to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nearer, my Lord, to thee, Nearer to thee!
Who to the cross didst come, Dying for me!
Strengthen my willing feet,
Hold me in service sweet

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Nearer, O Comforter, Nearer to thee!
Who with my loving Lord Dwellest with me!
Grant me thy fellowship!
Help me each day to keep

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But to be nearer still, Bring me, O God,
Not by the visioned steeps Angels have trod.
Here where thy cross I see, Jesus,
I wait for thee,

title: No, Not One!
author: Johnson Oatman, Jr
source: 'No, Not One' George Crawford Hugg, 1894.  Setting: "Pentecostal Hymns, No. 2", 1894

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There's not a friend like the lowly Jesus,
No, not one! no, not one!
None else could heal all our soul's
diseases, No, not one!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
no, not one! Jesus knows all about our
struggles, He will guide till the day is
done; There's not a friend like the lowly
Jesus, No, not one! no, not one!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
No friend like Him is so high and holy, No,
not one! no, not one! And yet no friend is
so meek and lowly, No, not one!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There's not an hour that He is not near us,
No, not one! no, not one!
No night so dark but His love can cheer us,
No, not one!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Did ever saint find this friend forsake him?
No, not one! no, not one!
Or sinner find that He would not take him?
No, not one!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Was e'er a gift like the Savior given? No,
not one! no, not one! Will He refuse us a
home in heaven? No, not one!

title: None Other Lamb
author: Christina Rossetti

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
None other Lamb, none other name,
None other hope in Heav'n or earth or sea,
None other hiding place from guilt and
shame, None beside Thee!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My faith burns low, my hope burns low;
Only my heart's desire cries out in me By
the deep thunder of its want and woe,
Cries out to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord, Thou art life, though I be dead;
Love's fire Thou art, however cold I be:
Nor Heav'n have I, nor place to lay my head,
Nor home, but Thee.

title: Not Worthy, Lord, to Gather Up the Crumbs
author: Edward Henry Bickersteth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Not worthy, Lord, to gather up the crumbs
With trembling hand that from Thy table
fall, A weary, heavy laden sinner comes To
plead Thy promise and obey Thy call.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
One word from Thee, my Lord, one smile,
one look, And I could face the cold,
rough world again; And with that treasure in
my heart could brook The wrath of devils and
the scorn of men.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And is not mercy Thy prerogativeFree mercy,
boundless, fathomless, divine? Me, Lord,
the chief of sinners, me forgive,
And Thine the greater glory, only Thine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I hear Thy voice; Thou bid'st me come and
rest; I come, I kneel,
I clasp Thy piercèd feet;
Thou bid'st me take my place,
a welcome guest Among Thy saints,
and of Thy banquet eat.

title: Now Praise We Christ, the Holy One
author: Coelius Sedulius, circa 450.  Translated to German by Martin Luther
source: 'Christum Wir Sollen Loben Schon' ancient Latin found in Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now praise we Christ, the Holy One,
The spotless virgin Mary's Son,
Far as the blesséd sun doth shine E'en to
the world's remote confine

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He, who Himself all things did make,
A servant's form vouchsafed to take,
That He as man mankind might win,
And save His creatures from their sin.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The grace of God, th'Almighty Lord,
On the chaste mother was outpoured a virgin
pure and undefiled In wondrous wise
conceived a child.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The holy maid became th'abode And temple of
the living God; And she, who knew not man,
was blest With God's own Word made manifest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The noble mother bare a Son,
For so did Gabriel's promise run,
Whom John confessed and leapt with joy,
Ere yet the mother knew her boy.

title: Now Rest Beneath Night's Shadow
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Innsbruck' or 'Nun ruhen alle Wälder' or 'O Welt, Ich Muss Dich Lassen' Heinrich Isaac, 1490

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now rest beneath night's shadow The
woodland, field, and meadow,
The world in slumber lies; But Thou,
my heart, awake thee, To prayer and song
betake thee; Let praise to thy Creator rise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The radiant sun hath vanished,
His golden rays are banished By night,
the foe of day; But Christ,
the Sun of gladness, Dispelling all my
sadness, Within my heart holds constant
sway.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The rule of day is over And shining jewels
cover The heaven's boundless blue.
Thus I shall shine in heaven,
Where crowns of gold are given To all who
faithful prove and true.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To rest my body hasteth,
Aside its garments casteth,
Types of mortality; These I put off and
ponder How Christ will give me yonder A robe
of glorious majesty.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, who dost love me, Oh,
spread Thy wings above me And shield me from
alarm! Though evil would assail me,
Thy mercy will not fail me:
I rest in Thy protecting arm.

title: Now Thank We All Our God
author: Martin Rinkart, c

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now thank we all our God,
with heart and hands and voices,
Who wondrous things has done,
in Whom this world rejoices;
Who from our mothers' arms has blessed us on
our way With countless gifts of love,
and still is ours today.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O may this bounteous God through all our
life be near us, With ever joyful hearts and
blessed peace to cheer us;
And keep us in His grace,
and guide us when perplexed;
And free us from all ills,
in this world and the next!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All praise and thanks to God the Father now
be given; The Son and Him Who reigns with
Them in highest Heaven; The one eternal God,
Whom earth and Heav'n adore;
For thus it was, is now,
and shall be evermore.

title: Now the Light Has Gone Away
author: Frances Ridley Havergal
source: 'Müde bin ich, geh zur Ruh' from Liederbuch für Kleinkinder-Schulen, 1842

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Now the light has gone away; Father,
listen while I pray, Asking Thee to watch
and keep And to send me quiet sleep.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus, Savior, wash away All that has been
wrong today; Help me every day to be Good
and gentle, more like Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let my near and dear ones be Always near and
dear to Thee. Oh, bring me and all I love To
Thy happy home above.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now my evening praise I give;
Thou didst die that I might live.
All my blessings come from Thee; Oh,
how good Thou art to me!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou, my best and kindest Friend,
Thou wilt love me to the end.
Let me love Thee more and more,
Always better than before.

title: O Be Glad All Nations on Earth
author: Brian L. Penney
source: 'Gwalia' Welsh hymn tune, traditional. Setting: David Evans, "Revised Church Hymnary", 1927

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O be glad, all nations on Earth,
Come let Jesus' Name be praised;
He is crowned, the King of glory,
At God's right hand He is raised.
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'nly throng;
Elders casting crowns before Him,
Singing an eternal song.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Great and marvelous are Your works,
Just and true are all Your ways;
All the nations bow in worship,
King of kings, Your Name they praise.
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'nly throng;
Elders casting crowns before Him,
Singing an eternal song.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
When shall Heav'n and Earth together,
Walk before the Lamb, its Light?
When shall all the saints be gathered,
and that Day shall end the night?
Angels bowing down before Him,
Singing with the heav'nly throng;
Elders casting crowns before Him,
Singing an eternal song.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lo, that day shall come with glory,
When Christ comes with trumpet sound;
Then the saints will cease their groaning,
Never more by death's chains bound.
Let us all bow down before Him, Sing,
O sing th'eternal song;
Work in hope until we meet Him,
And we join the heav'nly throng.

title: O Chief of Cities Bethlehem
author: Aurelius Clemens Prudentius (348-413). v. 1,2,4 Translated by N. B. Smithers
source: 'Puer Nobis Nascitur' Michael Praetorius, 1609

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O chief of cities, Bethlehem,
Of David's crown the fairest gem,
But more to us than David's name, In you,
as man, the Savior came.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beyond the sun in splendor bright,
Above you stands a wondrous light
Proclaiming from the conscious skies That
here, in flesh, the Godhead lies.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The wise men, seeing Him so fair,
Bow low be fore Him, and with prayer Their
treasured eastern gifts unfold Of incense,
myrrh, and royal gold.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The golden tribute owns Him King,
But frankin cense to God they bring,
And last, prophetic sign, with myrrh,
They shadow forth His sepulcher.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O Jesus, whom the Gentiles see, With Father,
Spirit, One in Three: To You, O God,
be glory giv'n By saints on earth and saints
in Heav'n.

title: O Come O Come Emmanuel
author: various, combined by unknown author approx 12th Century, Translated by John Mason Neale
source: 'Veni Emmanuel' 15th Century French processional.  Setting: "Common Service Book" (ULCA), 1917

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O come, O come, Emmanuel,
And ransom captive Israel,
That mourns in lonely exile here Until the
Son of God appear.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Rejoice! Rejoice! Emmanuel shall come to
thee, O Israel.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O come, Thou Wisdom from on high,
Who orderest all things mightily;
To us the path of knowledge show,
And teach us in her ways to go.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O come, Thou Rod of Jesse,
free Thine own from Satan's tyranny;
From depths of hell Thy people save,
And give them vict'ry ov'r the grave.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O come, Thou Dayspring,
come and cheer Our spirits by Thine advent
here; Disperse the gloomy clouds of night,
And death's dark shadows put to flight.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O come, Thou Key of David, come,
And open wide our heav'nly home;
Make safe the way that leads on high,
And close the path to misery.

title: O Come, All Ye Faithful
author: John F. Wade, circa
source: 'Adeste Fideles' or 'Portuguese Hymn' John F. Wade, 1743.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O come, all ye faithful,
joyful and triumphant, O come ye, O come ye,
to Bethlehem. Come and be hold Him,
born the King of angels;

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Lo! star led chieftains, Magi,
Christ adoring, Offer Him incense, gold,
and myrrh; We to the Christ Child bring our
hearts' oblations.

title: O Day of Rest And Gladness
author: Christopher Wordsworth
source: 'Woodbird' or 'Es Flog Ein Kleins Waldvögelein' traditional German found in

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O day of rest and gladness,
o day of joy and light,
O balm of care and sadness, most beautiful,
most bright: On thee, the high and lowly,
through ages joined in tune, Sing holy,
holy, holy, to the great God Triune.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On thee, at the creation,
the light first had its birth; On thee,
for our salvation, Christ rose from depths
of earth; On thee, our Lord, victorious,
the Spirit sent from heaven,
And thus on thee, most glorious,
a triple light was given.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou art a port, protected from storms that
round us rise; A garden,
intersected with streams of paradise;
Thou art a cooling fountain in life's dry,
dreary sand; From thee,
like Pisgah's mountain,
we view our promised land.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou art a holy ladder,
where angels go and come;
Each Sunday finds us gladder,
nearer to heaven, our home;
A day of sweet refection,
thou art a day of love,
A day of resurrection from earth to things
above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Today on weary nations the heavenly manna
falls; To holy convocations the silver
trumpet calls, Where Gospel light is glowing
with pure and radiant beams,
And living water flowing,
with soul refreshing streams.

title: O Father, All Creating
author: John Ellerton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Father, all creating, Whose wisdom, love,
and pow'r First bound two lives together In
Eden's primal hour, Today to these Thy
children Thy earliest gifts renew:
A home by Thee made happy,
A love by Thee kept true.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Savior, Guest most bounteous Of old in
Galilee, Vouchsafe today Thy presence With
these who call on Thee;
Their store of earthly gladness Transform to
heav'nly wine, And teach them,
in the tasting To know the gift is Thine.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O Spirit of the Father,
Breathe on them from above,
So mighty in Thy pureness,
So tender in Thy love; That,
guarded by Thy presence,
From sin and strife kept free,
Their lives may own Thy guidance,
Their hearts be rul'd by Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Except Thou build it, Father,
The house is built in vain; Except Thou,
Savior, bless it, The joy will turn to pain;
But naught can break the union Of hearts in
Thee made one, And love Thy Spirit hallow'd
Is endless love begun.

title: O For A Thousand Tongues
author: Charles Wesley

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O for a thousand tongues to sing My great
Redeemer's praise, The glories of my God and
King, The triumphs of His grace!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My gracious Master and my God,
Assist me to proclaim,
To spread through all the earth abroad The
honors of Thy name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Jesus! the name that charms our fears,
That bids our sorrows cease;
'Tis music in the sinner's ears, 'Tis life,
and health, and peace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He breaks the pow'r of canceled sin,
He sets the prisoner free;
His blood can make the foulest clean,
His blood availed for me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He speaks, and, listening to His voice,
New life the dead receive, The mournful,
broken hearts rejoice,
The humble poor believe.

title: O Holy Spirit, Enter In
author: Michael Schirmer
source: 'Wie Schön Leuchtet' Phillipp Nicolai, 1599.  Setting: "Mehrstimmiges ChoralBuch", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Holy Spirit, enter in,
And in our hearts Thy work begin Thy Temple
deign to make us; Sun of the soul,
Thou Light divine, Around and in us brightly
shine, To joy and gladness wake us.
That we to Thee Truly living,
To Thee giving Prayer unceasing May in love
be still increasing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Give to Thy Word impressive pow'r That in
our hearts, from this good hour,
As fire it may be glowing;
That we con fess the Father, Son, And Thee,
the Spirit, Three in One,
Thy glory ever showing. Stay Thou,
guide now Our souls ever that they never May
forsake Thee. But by faith their refuge make
Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou fountain whence all wisdom flows Which
God on pious hearts bestows,
Grant us Thy consolation.
That in our pure faith's unity We faithful
witnesses may be Of grace that brings
salvation. Hear us, cheer us,
By Thy teaching; let our preaching,
And our labor Praise Thee, Lord,
and serve our neighbor.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Thy heav'nly strength sustain our heart That
we may act the valiant part With Thee as our
Reliance; Be Thou our Refuge and our Shield
That we may never quit the field,
But stand in bold defiance. Descend,
defend From all errors And earth's terrors
Thy salvation Be our constant consolation.

title: O Holy, Blessed Trinity
author: Martin Behm
source: 'O Heilige Dreifaltigkeit' or 'Steht Auf, Ihr Lieben Kinderlein' Nikolaus Hermann, 1558

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Holy, Blessed Trinity, Divine,
Essential Unity, God Father, Son,
and Holy Ghost, Be Thou this day my Guide
and Host.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My soul and body keep from harm,
O'er all I have extend Thine arm,
That Satan may not cause distress Nor bring
me shame or wretchedness.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Father's might shield me this day,
The Son's pure wisdom cheer my way,
The Holy Spirit's light divine Illume my
heart's benighted shrine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My Maker, strengthen Thou my heart,
O my Redeemer, help impart, Blest Comforter,
keep at my side That faith and love in me
abide.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, bless and keep Thou me as Thine; Lord,
make Thy face upon me shine; Lord,
lift Thy countenance on me And give me
peacesweet peace, from Thee.

title: O Little Town of Bethlehem
author: Phillips Brooks

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O little town of Bethlehem,
how still we see thee lie!
Above thy deep and dreamless sleep the
silent stars go by. Yet in thy dark streets
shineth the everlasting Light;
The hopes and fears of all the years are met
in thee tonight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
For Christ is born of Mary,
and gathered all above, While mortals sleep,
the angels keep their watch of wond'ring
love. O morning stars together,
proclaim the holy birth,
And praises sing to God the King,
and peace to men on earth!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How silently, how silently,
the wondrous Gift is giv'n;
So God imparts to human hearts the blessings
of His Heav'n. No ear may hear His coming,
but in this world of sin,
Where meek souls will receive Him still,
the dear Christ enters in.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Where children pure and happy pray to the
blessèd Child, Where misery cries out to
Thee, Son of the mother mild;
Where charity stands watching and faith
holds wide the door, The dark night wakes,
the glory breaks, and Christmas comes once
more.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O holy Child of Bethlehem, descend to us,
we pray; Cast out our sin, and enter in,
be born in us today. We hear the Christmas
angels the great glad tidings tell;
O come to us, abide with us,
our Lord Emmanuel!

title: O Lord My Soul Convicted
author: James Maxwell
source: 'Winchester New' from "Musikalisches Handbuch", Hamburg, 1690.  Setting: Charles Lewis Hutchins, 1896

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, my soul convicted stands Of breaking
all Thy ten commands: And on me justly
might'st Thou pour Thy wrath in one eternal
show'r.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But thanks to God, its loud alarms Have
warn'd me of approaching harms; And now,
O Lord, my wants I see, Lost and undone,
I come to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I know my fig leaf righteousness Can ne'er
Thy broken law redress;
Yet in the gospel plan I see,
There's hope of pardon e'en for me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There, I behold with wonder, Lord!
That Christ hath to Thy law restor'd Those
honors on th'a toning day,
Which guilty sinners took away.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Amazing wisdom, pow'r and love,
Dis play'd to rebels from above! Do Thou,
O Lord, my faith increase To love and trust
Thy plan of grace.

title: O Lord of Heav'n and Earth and Sea
author: Christopher Wordsworth
source: 'Es Ist Kein Tag' Johann D. Meyer, 1692.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord of Heav'n and earth and sea,
To Thee all praise and glory be;
How shall we show our love to Thee,
Who givest all?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The golden sunshine, vernal air,
Sweet flow'rs and fruits, Thy love declare;
Where harvests ripen, Thou art there,
Who givest all.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For peaceful homes and healthful days,
For all the blessings earth displays,
We owe Thee thankfulness and praise,
Who givest all.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou didst not spare Thine only Son,
But gav'st Him for a world undone,
And freely, with that blessèd One,
Thou givest all.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou giv'st the Spirit's blessèd dow'r,
Spirit of life and love and pow'r,
And dost His sev'nfold graces show'r Upon us
all.

title: O Lord We Praise Thee
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Gott Sei Gelobet und Gebenedeiet' or 'Enchiridion' or 'Gud Være Lovet Evig Nu'

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, we praise Thee, bless Thee,
and adore Thee, In thanksgiving bow before
Thee Thou with Thy body and Thy blood didst
nourish Our weak souls that they may
flourish: O Lord, have mercy! May Thy body,
Lord, born of Mary, That our sins and
sorrows did carry, And Thy blood for us
plead In all trial, fear, and need: O Lord,
have mercy!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy holy body into death was given,
Life to win for us in heaven.
No greater love than this to Thee could bind
us; May this feast thereof remind us!
O Lord, have mercy! Lord,
Thy kindness did so constrain Thee That Thy
blood should bless and sustain me.
All our debt Thou hast paid;
Peace with God once more is made: O Lord,
have mercy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
May God bestow on us His grace and favor To
please Him with our behavior And live as
brethren here in love and union Nor repent
this blest Communion! O Lord, have mercy!
Let not Thy good Spirit forsake us;
Grant that heav'nly minded He make us;
Give Thy Church, Lord,
to see Days of peace and unity: O Lord,
have mercy!

title: O Lord, How Shall I Meet Thee
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Wie Soll ich Dich Empfange' Johann Crüger, 1653

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, how shall I meet Thee,
How welcome Thee aright?
All nations long to see Thee, My Hope,
my heart's Delight! O kindle, Lord,
most holy, Thy lamp within my breast,
To do in spirit lowly All that may please
Thee best.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy Zion palms is strewing,
And branches fresh and fair; My heart,
its pow'rs renewing, An anthem shall
prepare. My soul puts off her sadness Thy
glories to proclaim; With all her strength
and gladness She fain would serve Thy Name.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
What hast Thou left ungranted To give me
glad relief? When soul and body panted In
utmost depth of grief,
In deepest degradation,
Devoid of joy and peace, Then, Thou,
my soul's Salvation, Didst come to bring
release.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
I lay in fetters groaning,
Thou com'st to set me free; I stood,
my shame bemoaning, Thou com'st to honor me.
A glory Thou dost give me,
A treasure safe on high,
That will not fail nor leave me As earthly
riches fly.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Love caused Thine incarnation Love brought
Thee down to me; Thy thirst for my salvation
Procured my liberty. O love beyond all
telling, That led Thee to embrace,
In love all love excelling,
Our lost and fallen race!

title: O Lord, I Am Not Worthy
author: from Landshuter Gesangbuch
source: 'Non Dignus' traditional air, before 1871

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, I am not worthy That Thou should'st
come to me, But speak the words of comfort,
My spirit healed shall be.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Lord, Thou art all holy,
The angels Thee adore; How, then,
ought I sincerely My wrongs and sins
deplore!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But when Thou soon wilt enter My heart,
my sinful heart, Then heal me,
be my shelter, For Thou my Savior art.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O Lord, how can I thank Thee For such a gift
as this? A gift which truly filleth My soul
with heav'nly bliss!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
I praise Thee, I extol Thee,
I love Thee O my Sire,
Till once in joy and glory,
In heav'n I Thee admire.

title: O Lord, My God, I Thirst For You

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Lord, my God, I thirst for You,
I long to see your face,
Just as the hunted deer is stressed I falter
in the race; My heart cries out,
my tears run down, I am in deep distress,
'Where is your God?' men say to me,
They taunt me and oppress.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, when will I be helped by You,
I struggle day and night? O hear my prayer,
enable me to stand in your great might;
I look back on those days gone by when,
Lord, You were so near,
when in your house with festive throng I
praised your Name so dear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So why am I cast down, O Lord,
and why should I feel low? You are my God,
my Savior strong, Your praise from me shall
flow; I think of all your works, O Lord,
Your saving pow'r of old,
So when beset and overwhelmed,
I will your strength take hold.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Your lovingkindness fills my days,
Your song at night I sing,
And when my fears assail again to You I'll
tightly cling; My hope is fixed on God,
my Rock, His own He won't forget;
Be still my soul, my face will shine And I
will praise Him yet.

title: O Love, How Deep, How Broad, How High
author: Unknown, 15th Century; Translated by Benjamin Webb
source: 'Deo Gracias' or 'Agincourt' traditional English, circa 1415.  Setting: Charles Winfred Douglas, 1918, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O love, how deep, how broad, how high,
How passing thought and fantasy, That God,
the Son of God, should take Our mortal form
for mortals' sake!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He sent no angel to our race Of higher or of
lower place, But wore the robe of human
frame And He Himself, to this world came.

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
For us baptized, for us He bore His holy
fast and hungered sore,
For us temptations sharp He knew;
For us the tempter overthrew.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: O Sacred Head, Now Wounded
author: Bernard of Clairvaux
source: 'Passion Chorale' or 'Herzlich Tut Mich Verlangen' Hans Leo Hassler, 1601. Adapted by J.S. Bach, 1729

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O sacred Head, now wounded,
with grief and shame weighed down,
Now scornfully surrounded with thorns,
Thine only crown; O sacred Head, what glory,
what bliss till now was Thine! Yet,
though despised and gory,
I joy to call Thee mine.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What Thou, my Lord, hast suffered,
was all for sinners' gain; Mine,
mine was the transgression,
but Thine the deadly pain. Lo, here I fall,
my Savior! 'Tis I deserve Thy place;
Look on me with Thy favor,
vouchsafe to me Thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Men mock and taunt and jeer Thee,
Thou noble countenance,
Though mighty worlds shall fear Thee and
flee before Thy glance.
How art thou pale with anguish,
with sore abuse and scorn!
How doth Thy visage languish that once was
bright as morn!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now from Thy cheeks has vanished their color
once so fair; From Thy red lips is banished
the splendor that was there. Grim death,
with cruel rigor, hath robbed Thee of Thy
life; Thus Thou hast lost Thy vigor,
Thy strength in this sad strife.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
My burden in Thy Passion, Lord,
Thou hast borne for me,
For it was my transgression which brought
this woe on Thee. I cast me down before
Thee, wrath were my rightful lot;
Have mercy, I implore Thee; Redeemer,
spurn me not!

title: O That The Lord Would Guide My Ways
author: Isaac Watts
source: 'Evan' or 'Eva' William H. Havergal, 1847.  Setting: Lowell Mason, 1850

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O that the Lord would guide my ways To keep
His statutes still! O that my God would
grant me grace To know and do His will!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O send Thy Spirit down to write Thy law upon
my heart! Nor let my tongue indulge deceit,
Nor act the liar's part.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
From vanity turn off mine eyes;
Let no corrupt design,
Nor covetous desires arise Within this soul
of mine.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Order my footsteps by Thy Word,
And make my heart sincere;
Let sin have no dominion, Lord,
But keep my conscience clear.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Assist my soul, too apt to stray,
A stricter watch to keep;
And should I e'er forget Thy way,
Restore Thy wand'ring sheep.

title: O The Deep, Deep Love of Jesus
author: S. Trevor Francis
source: 'Ebenezer' or 'Ton-Y-Botel' Thomas J. Williams, 1890.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O the deep, deep love of Jesus, vast,
unmeasured, boundless, free!
Rolling as a mighty ocean in its fullness
over me! Underneath me, all around me,
is the current of Thy love Leading onward,
leading homeward to Thy glorious rest above!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
spread His praise from shore to shore!
How He loveth, ever loveth, changeth never,
nevermore! How He watches o'er His loved
ones, died to call them all His own;
How for them He intercedeth,
watcheth o'er them from the throne!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O the deep, deep love of Jesus,
love of every love the best!
'Tis an ocean full of blessing,
'tis a haven giving rest! O the deep,
deep love of Jesus, 'tis a heav'n of heav'ns
to me; And it lifts me up to glory,
for it lifts me up to Thee!

title: O Trinity of Blessed Light
author: Ambrose of Milan, 4th Century.  German version by M. Luther
source: 'O Lux Beata Trinitas' ancient Latin.  Setting: "A Hymnal" (Episcopal), 1916

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O Trinity of blessèd light,
O Unity of princely might,
The fiery sun now goes his way;
Shed Thou within our hearts a ray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To Thee our morning song of praise,
To Thee our evening prayer we raise;
O grant us with Thy saints on high To praise
Thee through eternity.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
All laud to God the Father be, All praise,
eternal Son, to Thee, All glory,
as is ever meet, To God the holy Paraclete.

title: O Wondrous Type, O Vision Fair
author: From the "Sarum Breviary"
source: 'Deo Gracias' or 'Agincourt' traditional English, circa 1415.  Setting: Charles Winfred Douglas, 1918, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O wondrous type! O vision fair Of glory that
the Church may share, Which Christ upon the
mountain shows, where brighter than the sun
He glows!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
From age to age the tale declare,
How with the three disciples there,
Where Moses and El ijah meet,
The Lord holds converse high and sweet.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The law and prophets there have place,
Two chosen witnesses of grace;
The Father's voice from out the cloud
proclaims His only Son aloud.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
With shining face and bright array,
Christ deigns to manifest today What glory
shall be theirs above who joy in God with
perfect love.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And faithful hearts are raised on high by
this great vision's mystery;
For which in joyful strains we raise the
voice of prayer, the hymn of praise.

title: Of The Father's Love Begotten
author: Aurelius Prudentius Clemens, 5th Century
source: 'Divinum Mysterium' or 'Corde Natus' Latin Plainsong, 13th Century

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Of the Father's love begotten Ere the worlds
began to be, He is Alpha and Omega,
He the source, the ending He,
Of the things that are, that have been,
And that future years shall see,
Evermore and evermore!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
He is found in human fashion,
Death and sorrow here to know,
That the race of Adam's children,
Doomed by law to endless woe,
May not henceforth die and perish In the
dreadful gulf below, Evermore and evermore!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh that birth forever blessèd!
When the virgin, full of grace,
By the Holy Ghost conceiving,
Bare the Savior of our race; And the Babe,
the world's Redeemer, First re vealed His
sacred face, Evermore and evermore!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O ye heights of heav'n adore Him;
Angel hosts, His prais es sing; Pow'rs,
dominions, bow before Him,
and extol our God and King:
Let no tongue on earth be silent,
Every voice in concert ring,
Evermore and evermore!

title: Oh, Blest the House
author: Christoph C. L. von Pfeil
source: 'Wo Gott Zum Haus' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, 1533

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Oh blest the house, whate'er befall,
Where Jesus Christ is All in All; Yea,
if He were not dwelling there,
How poor and dark and void it were!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Oh blest that house where faith ye find,
And all within have set their mind To trust
their God and serve Him still,
And do in all His holy will.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Blest, where their prayers shall daily rise
As fragrant incense to the skies,
While in their lives the world is taught
That forms without the heart are naught.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blest, where the busy hands fulfil Their
proper task with ready skill,
While through their different works ye see
One spirit run of unity.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Blest such a house, it prospers well,
In peace and joy the parents dwell,
And in their children's lot is shown How
richly God can bless His own.

title: On Jordan's Bank the Baptist's Cry
author: Charles Coffin
source: 'Puer Nobis Nascitur' Michael Praetorius, 1609

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
On Jordan's bank the Baptist's cry Announces
that the Lord is nigh; Come, then,
and hearken, for he brings Glad tidings from
the King of kings!

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
For Thou art our Salvation, Lord,
Our Refuge, and our great Reward.
Without Thy grace our souls must fade And
wither like a flow'r decayed.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Stretch forth Thine hand, to heal our sore,
And make us rise and fall no more;
Once more upon Thy people shine,
And fill the world with love divine.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
To Him Who left the throne of Heav'n To save
man kind, all praise be giv'n;
Like praise be to the Father done,
And Holy Spirit, Three in One.

title: On What Has Now Been Sown
author: John Newton

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
On what has now been sown Thy blessing,
Lord, bestow; The pow'r is Thine alone To
make it spring and grow.
Do Thou in grace the harvest raise,
And Thou alone shalt have the praise.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To Thee our wants are known,
From Thee are all our pow'rs;
Accept what is Thine own And pardon what is
ours. Our praises, Lord,
and prayers receive And to Thy Word a
blessing give.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, grant that each of us Now met before
Thee here May meet together thus When Thou
and Thine appear And follow Thee to Heav'n,
our home. E'en so, Amen, Lord Jesus, come!

title: One Thing's Needful
author: Johann H. Schröder
source: 'Eins ist Not' Adam Krieger (1634-1666).  Setting: Fridrich Layriz, 1853, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
One thing's needful: then, Lord Jesus,
Keep this one thing in my mind; All beside,
though first it please us,
Soon a grievous yoke we find:
Beneath it the heart is still fretting and
striving, No true, lasting happiness ever
deriving. The gain of this one thing all
loss can requite And teach me in all things
to find true delight.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Soul, wilt thou this one thing find thee?
Seek not midst created things;
What is earthly, leave behind thee,
over nature stretch thy wings;
For where God and man both in One are
united, With God's perfect fullness the
heart is delighted; There,
there is the worthiest lot and the best,
My One and my All, and my Joy, and my Rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
How were Mary's thoughts devoted,
Her eternal joy to find,
As intent each word she noted,
At her Savior's feet reclined:
How kindled her heart,
how devout was its feeling,
While hearing the lessons that Christ was
revealing; For Jesus all earthly con cerns
she forgot, And all was repaid in that one
happy lot.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thus my longings, heav'nward tending, Jesus,
rest alone on Thee; Help me,
thus on Thee depending, Savior!
come and dwell in me: Although all the world
should forsake and forget Thee,
In love I will follow Thee,
ne'er will I quit Thee; For Jesus,
both Spirit and life is Thy Word,
And is there a joy which Thou dost not
afford?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Wisdom's highest noblest treasure, Jesus,
lies conceal'd in Thee;
Grant that this may still the measure Of my
will and actions be: Humility there and
simplicity reigning, My steps shall in
wisdom for ever be training; Oh!
if I of Christ have this knowledge divine,
The fullness of heavenly wisdom is mine.

title: Open Now Thy Gates of Beauty
author: Benjamin Schmolck
source: 'Unser Herrscher' or 'Neander' Joachim Neander, 1680.  Setting: "Chorale Book for England", 1863

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Open now thy gates of beauty, Zion,
let me enter there, Where my soul in joyful
duty Waits for Him Who answers prayer. Oh,
how blessèd is this place,
Filled with solace, light and grace!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord, my God, I come before Thee,
Come Thou also unto me;
Where we find Thee and adore Thee,
There a heav'n on earth must be.
To my heart, oh, enter Thou,
Let it be Thy temple now!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Here Thy praise is gladly chanted,
Here Thy seed is duly sown; Let my soul,
where it is planted, Bring forth precious
sheaves alone, So that all I hear may be
Fruitful unto life in me.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou my faith increase and quicken,
Let me keep Thy gift divine,
Howsoe'er temptations thicken;
May Thy Word still o'er me shine As my
guiding star through life,
As my comfort in my strife.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Speak, O God, and I will hear Thee,
Let Thy will be done indeed;
May I undisturbed draw near Thee While Thou
dost Thy people feed. Here of life the
fountain flows, Here is balm for all our
woes.

title: Our Father Thou in Heaven Above
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Vater Unser im Himmelreich' attr. Martin Luther, found in Valentin Schumann's Geistliche Lieder, Leipzig, 1539

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our Father, Thou in heav'n above,
Who biddest us to dwell in love,
As brethren of one family,
To cry in ev'ry need to Thee,
Teach us no thoughtless word to say,
But from our inmost heart to pray.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Thy name be hallowed. Help us, Lord,
In purity to keep Thy Word,
That to the glory of Thy Name We walk before
Thee free from blame. Let no false doctrine
us pervert; All poor, deluded souls convert.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thy kingdom come. Thine let it be In time
and in eternity. Let Thy good Spirit e'er be
nigh Our hearts with graces to supply.
Break Satan's pow'r, defeat his rage;
Preserve Thy Church from age to age.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy gracious will on earth be done As 'tis
in heav'n before Thy throne;
Obedience in our weal and woe And patience
in all grief bestow. Curb flesh and blood
and ev'ry ill That sets itself against Thy
will.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Give us this day our daily bread And let us
all be clothed and fed.
From war and strife be our Defense,
From famine and from pestilence,
That we may live in godly peace,
Free from all care and avarice.

title: Our God, Our Help In Ages Past
author: Isaac Watts

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Our God, our help in ages past,
Our hope for years to come,
Our shelter from the stormy blast,
And our eternal home.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Under the shadow of Thy throne Thy saints
have dwelt secure; Sufficient is Thine arm
alone, And our defense is sure.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Before the hills in order stood,
Or earth received her frame,
From everlasting Thou art God,
To endless years the same.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thy Word commands our flesh to dust,
'Return, ye sons of men:' All nations rose
from earth at first, And turn to earth
again.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
A thousand ages in Thy sight Are like an
evening gone; Short as the watch that ends
the night Before the rising sun.

title: Out of the Deep I Cry to Thee
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Aus Tiefer Not (Luther)' or 'Af Dybsens Nød' Martin Luther from Erfurt Enchiridion, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Out of the deep I cry to Thee; O Lord God,
hear my crying: Incline Thy gracious ear to
me, With prayer to Thee applying.
For if Thou fix Thy searching eye On all sin
and iniquity, Who, Lord,
can stand before Thee?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
But love and grace with Thee prevail, O God,
our sins forgiving; The holiest deeds can
naught avail Of all before Thee living.
Before Thee none can boast him clear;
Therefore must each Thy judgment fear,
And live on Thy compassion.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For this, my hope in God shall rest,
Naught building on my merit;
My heart confides, of Him possest,
His goodness stays my spirit.
His precious word assureth me; My solace,
my sure Rock is he, Whereon my soul abideth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
And though I wait the livelong night And
till the morn returneth,
My heart undoubting trusts His might Nor in
impatience mourneth. Born of His Spirit,
Israel In the right Way thus fareth well,
And on his God reposeth

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
What though our sins are manifold?
Supreme His mercy reigneth;
No limit can His hand withhold,
Where evil most obtaineth.
He the good Shepherd is alone,
Who Israel will redeem and own,
Forgiving all transgression.

title: Over Kidron Jesus Treadeth
author: Thomas Hansen Kingo
source: 'Over Kedron Jesus Traeder' Ludvig Mathias Lindeman.  Setting: "The Lutheran Hymnary", 1913

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Over Kidron Jesus treadeth To His passion
for us all; Every human eye be weeping,
Tears of bitter grief let fall!
Round His Spirit flock the foes,
Place their shafts and bend their bows,
Aiming at the Savior solely,
While the world forsakes Him wholly.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
David once, with heart afflicted,
Crossed the Kidron's narrow strand,
Clouds of gloom and grief about him When an
exile from his land. But, O Jesus,
blacker now Bends the cloud above Thy brow,
Hasting to death's dreary portals For the
shame and sin of mortals.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See how, anguish struck,
He falleth Prostrate, and with struggling
breath, Three times on His God He calleth,
Praying that the bitter death And the cup of
doom may go, Still He cries, in all His woe:
"Not My will, but Thine,
O Father!" And the angels round Him gather.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
See how, in that hour of darkness,
Battling with the evil pow'r,
Agonies untold assail Him,
On His soul the arrows show'r;
All the garden flow'rs are wet With the
drops of bloody sweat,
From His anguished frame distillingWorld's
redemption thus fulfilling!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But, O flow'rs, so sadly watered By this
pure and precious dew,
In some blessed hour your blossoms 'Neath
the olive shadows grew!
Eden's garden did not bear Aught that can
with you compare, For the blood,
thus freely given, Makes my soul the heir of
heaven.

title: Pass Me Not, O Gentle Savior
author: Fanny J. Crosby
source: 'Pass Me Not O Gentle Savior' William Howard Doane, 1870.  Setting: "The Coronation", 1872

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Pass me not, O gentle Savior,
Hear my humble cry; While on others Thou art
calling, Do not pass me by.

sections.label: Chorus
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
3, Trusting only in Thy merit,
Would I seek Thy face; Heal my wounded,
broken spirit, Save me by Thy grace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou the Spring of all my comfort,
More than life to me, Whom have I on earth
beside Thee? Whom in Heav'n but Thee?

title: Praise God From Whom All Blessings Flow
author: Thomas Ken

sections.label: Verse 1

title: Praise My Soul The King Of Heaven
author: Henry F. Lyte
source: 'Praise My Soul' or 'Lauda Anima' or 'St. Paul' John Goss, 1869.  Setting: "The Choral Hymnal", 1888

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Praise, my soul, the King of heaven;
To His feet thy tribute bring. Ransomed,
healed, restored, forgiven,
Evermore His praises sing: Alleluia!
Alleluia! Praise the everlasting King.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Praise Him for His grace and favor To our
fathers in distress. Praise Him still the
same as ever, Slow to chide,
and swift to bless. Alleluia! Alleluia!
Glorious in His faithfulness.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Father like He tends and spares us;
Well our feeble frame He knows.
In His hands He gently bears us,
Rescues us from all our foes. Alleluia!
Alleluia! Widely yet His mercy flows.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Frail as summer's flower we flourish,
Blows the wind and it is gone;
But while mortals rise and perish Our God
lives unchanging on, Praise Him, Praise Him,
Hallelujah Praise the High Eternal One!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Angels, help us to adore Him;
Ye behold Him face to face; Sun and moon,
bow down before Him, Dwellers all in time
and space. Alleluia! Alleluia!
Praise with us the God of grace.

title: Praise The Lord, Ye Heavens Adore Him
author: verses 1-2, unknown
source: 'Austria (Haydn)' or 'Austrian Hymn' Franz Joseph Haydn, 1797

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Worship, honor, glory, blessing, Lord,
we offer unto Thee. Young and old,
Thy praise expressing,
In glad homage bend the knee.
All the saints in Heav'n adore Thee;
We would bow before Thy throne.
As Thine angels serve before Thee,
So on earth Thy will be done.

title: Praise To The Lord, The Almighty
author: Joachim Neander
source: 'Lobe den Herren' from Ander Theil des Erneuerten Gesangbuch, 1665

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Praise to the Lord, the Almighty,
the King of creation! O my soul, praise Him,
for He is thy health and salvation!
All ye who hear, now to His temple draw
near; Praise Him in glad adoration.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Praise to the Lord, Who o'er all things so
wondrously reigneth, Shelters thee under His
wings, yea, so gently sustaineth!
Hast thou not seen how thy desires have been
Granted in what He ordaineth

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Praise to the Lord, Who hath fearfully,
wondrously, made thee;
Health hath vouchsafed and,
when heedlessly falling, hath stayed thee.
What need or grief ever hath failed of
relief? Wings of His mercy did shade thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Praise to the Lord, Who doth prosper thy
work and defend thee; Surely His goodness
and mercy here daily attend thee.
Ponder anew what the Almighty can do,
If with His love He befriend thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Praise to the Lord, Who,
when tempests their warfare are waging, Who,
when the elements madly around thee are
raging, Biddeth them cease,
turneth their fury to peace,
Whirlwinds and waters assuaging.

title: Rejoice, My Heart, Be Glad and Sing
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Ich Singe dir mit Herz' Johann Balthasar König, 1738

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rejoice, my heart, be glad and sing,
A cheerful trust maintain; For God,
the Source of everything,
Thy Portion shall remain.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He is thy Treasure, He thy Joy,
Thy Life and Light and Lord,
Thy Counselor when doubts annoy,
Thy Shield and great Reward.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Why spend the day in blank despair,
In restless thought the night?
On thy Creator cast thy care;
He makes thy burdens light.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Did not His love and truth and pow'r Watch
o'er thy childhood day?
Has He not oft in threat'ning hour Turned
dreaded ills away?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His wisdom never plans in vain,
Ne'er falters or mistakes;
All that His counsels did ordain A happy
ending makes.

title: Rejoice, O Pilgrim Throng
author: Edward H. Plumptre

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rejoice, O pilgrim throng! Rejoice,
give thanks, and sing;
Your festal banner wave on high,
The cross of Christ your King.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Rejoice, rejoice, rejoice,
Give thanks and sing. Rejoice, rejoice,
rejoice, Give thanks and sing.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
With all the angel choirs,
With all the saints on earth,
Pour out the strains of joy and bliss,
True rapture, noblest mirth.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With voice as full and strong As ocean's
surging praise, Send forth the hymns our
fathers loved, The psalms of ancient days.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Still lift your standard high,
Still march in firm array,
As warriors through the darkness toil,
Till dawns the golden day.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Yes, on through life's long path,
Still chanting as ye go; From youth to age,
by night and day, In gladness and in woe.

title: Rescue the Perishing
author: Fanny Crosby
source: 'Rescue the Perishing' William Howard Doane, 1870

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Rescue the perishing, care for the dying,
Snatch them in pity from sin and the grave;
Weep o'er the erring one,
lift up the fallen, Tell them of Jesus,
the mighty to save.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Rescue the perishing, care for the dying,
Jesus is merciful, Jesus will save.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Though they are slighting Him,
still He is waiting, Waiting the penitent
child to receive; Plead with them earnestly,
plead with them gently;
He will forgive they should only believe.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Down in the human heart,
crushed by the tempter,
Feelings lie buried that grace can restore;
Touched by a loving heart,
wakened by kindness, Chords that were broken
will vibrate once more.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Rescue the perishing, duty demands it;
Strength for thy labor the Lord will
provide; Back to the narrow way patiently
win them; Tell the poor wand'rer a Savior
has died.

title: Rock of Ages
author: Augustus Montague Toplady

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Not the labor of my hands Can fulfill Thy
law's demands; Could my zeal no respite
know, Could my tears forever flow,
All for sin could not atone; Thou must save,
and Thou alone.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Nothing in my hand I bring,
Simply to the cross I cling; Naked,
come to Thee for dress;
Helpless look to Thee for grace; Foul,
I to the fountain fly; Wash me, Savior,
or I die.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
While I draw this fleeting breath,
When mine eyes shall close in death,
When I soar to worlds unknown,
See Thee on Thy judgment throne,
Rock of Ages, cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee.

title: Salvation Unto Us Has Come
author: Paul Speratus
source: 'Es ist das Heil uns Kommen Her' traditional German circa 1400 from Etlich Christlich Lider, Wittenberg, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Salvation unto us has come By God's free
grace and favor; Good works cannot avert our
doom, They help and save us never.
Faith looks to Jesus Christ alone,
Who did for all the world atone;
He is our one Redeemer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
What God did in His law demand And none to
Him could render Caused wrath and woe on
every hand For man, the vile offender.
Our flesh has not those pure desires The
spirit of the Law requires,
And lost is our condition.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It was a false, misleading dream That God
His Law had given So sinners could
themselves redeem And by their works gain
Heaven. The Law is but a mirror bright To
bring the inbred sin to light That lurks
within our nature.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From sin our flesh could not abstain Sin
held its sway unceasing;
The task was useless and in vain,
Our guilt was e'er increasing.
None can remove sin's poisoned dart Or
purify our guileful heart?
So deep is our corruption.

title: Savior Of The Nations Come
author: Ambrose of Milan, c. 397.  Translated to German by Martin Luther
source: 'Nun Komm, Der Heiden Heiland' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Savior of the nations, come; Virgin's Son,
here make Thy home! Marvel now,
O heav'n and earth, That the Lord chose such
a birth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not by human flesh and blood;
By the Spirit of our God Was the Word of God
made flesh, Woman's offspring,
pure and fresh.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Wondrous birth! O wondrous Child Of the
virgin undefiled! Though by all the world
disowned, Still to be in heaven enthroned.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
From the Father forth He came And returneth
to the same, Captive leading death and hell
High the song of triumph swell!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thou, the Father's only Son,
Hast o'er sin the vict'ry won.
Boundless shall Thy kingdom be;
When shall we its glories see?

title: Savior When In Dust To Thee
author: Robert Grant
source: 'Aberystwyth (Parry)' Joseph Parry, 1879.  Setting: "The English Hymnal", 1906

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Savior, when in dust to Thee Low we bow
th'adoring knee, When, repentant,
to the skies Scarce we lift our weeping
eyes, O by all the pains and woes Suffered
once for man below, Bending from Thy throne
on high, Hear our penitential cry!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
By Thy helpless infant years,
By Thy life of want and tears,
By Thy days of sore distress In the savage
wilderness, By the dread mysterious hour Of
th'insulting tempter's pow'r, Turn,
O turn a fav'ring eye,
Hear our penitential cry!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By the sacred griefs that wept O'er the
grave where Laz'rus slept,
By the boding tears that flowed Over Salem's
loved abode, By the anguished sigh that told
Treachery lurked within Thy fold,
From Thy seat above the sky,
Hear our penitential cry!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
By Thine hour of dire despair,
By Thine agony of prayer, By the cross,
