the nail, the thorn, Piercing spear,
and torturing scorn, By the gloom that
veiled the skies O'er the dreadful
sacrifice, Listen to our humble cry,
Hear our penitential cry!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
By Thy deep expiring groan,
By the sad sepulchral stone,
By the vault whose dark abode Held in vain
the rising God, O from earth to heaven
restored, Mighty, reascended Lord, Listen,
listen to the sigh Of our penitential cry!

title: Savior, Like A Shepherd Lead Us
author: attr. Dorothy Ann Thrupp
source: 'Bradbury' William B. Bradbury, 1859

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Savior, like a shepherd lead us,
much we need Thy tender care;
In Thy pleasant pastures feed us,
for our use Thy folds prepare.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast bought us, Thine we are.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We are Thine, Thou dost befriend us,
be the guardian of our way; Keep Thy flock,
from sin defend us, seek us when we go
astray. Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus! Hear,
O hear us when we pray. Blessèd Jesus,
blessèd Jesus! Hear, O hear us when we pray.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou hast promised to receive us,
poor and sinful though we be;
Thou hast mercy to relieve us,
grace to cleanse and pow'r to free.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
We will early turn to Thee. Blessèd Jesus,
blessèd Jesus! We will early turn to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Early let us seek Thy favor,
early let us do Thy will;
Blessèd Lord and only Savior,
with Thy love our bosoms fill.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.
Blessèd Jesus, blessèd Jesus!
Thou hast loved us, love us still.

title: Savior, Who Thy Flock Art Feeding
author: William Augustus Mühlenberg
source: 'Batty' or 'Ringe recht' from Johann Thommen's Musicalischer Christenschatz, Basel, 1745

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Savior, who Thy flock art feeding With the
Shepherd's kindest care,
All the feeble gently leading,
While the lambs Thy bosom share.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Now, these little ones receiving,
Fold them in Thy gracious arm; There,
we know, Thy Word believing,
Only there secure from harm.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Never, from Thy pasture roving,
Let them be the lion's prey;
Let Thy tenderness, so loving,
Keep them through life's dang'rous way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then within Thy fold eternal Let them find a
resting place, Feed in pastures ever vernal,
Drink the rivers of Thy grace.

title: See Amid the Winter's Snow
author: Edward Caswall

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See amid the winter's snow,
Born for us on earth below, See,
the gentle Lamb appears,
Promised from eternal years.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Hail that ever blessèd morn,
Hail redemption's happy dawn,
Sing through all Jerusalem:
Christ is born in Bethlehem.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Lo, within a manger lies He Who built the
starry skies; He Who, thronèd in height
sublime, Sits amid the cherubim.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Say, you holy shepherds, say,
Tell your joyful news today.
Why have you now left your sheep On the
lonely mountain steep?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
"As we watched at dead of night, Lo,
we saw a wondrous light;
Angels singing 'Peace on earth' Told us of
the Savior's birth."

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sacred Infant, all divine,
What a tender love was Thine,
Thus to come from highest bliss Down to such
a world as this.

title: See, The Lord Ascends In Triumph
author: Christopher Wordsworth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
See, the Lord ascends in triumph;
see the King in royal state,
Riding on the clouds, His chariot,
To His heav'nly palace gate. Hark!
the choirs of angel voices Joyful alleluias
sing, And the portals high are lifted To
receive their heav'nly King. 6. Holy Ghost,
Illuminator, shed Thy beams upon our eyes,
Help us to look up with Stephen,
and to see beyond the skies,
Where the Son of Man in glory Standing is at
God's right hand, Beck'ning on His martyr
army, succoring His faithful band.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Who is this that comes in glory,
with the trump of jubilee? Lord of battles,
God of armies, He has gained the victory.
He Who on the cross did suffer,
He who from the grave arose,
He has vanquished sin and Satan,
He by death has spoiled His foes. 7.
See Him, Who is gone before us,
Heav'nly mansions to prepare, See Him,
who is ever pleading For us with prevailing
prayer, See Him, who with sound of trumpet,
and with His angelic train,
Summoning the world to judgment,
on the clouds will come again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
While He lifts His hands in blessing,
He is parted from His friends While their
eager eyes behold Him,
He upon the cloud ascends;
He Who walked with God and pleased Him,
preaching truth and doom to come, He,
our Enoch, is translated to His everlasting
home. 8. Raise us up from earth to Heaven,
give us wings of faith and love,
Gales of holy aspirations wafting us to
realms above; That, with hearts and minds
uplifted, we with Christ our Lord may dwell,
Where He sits enthroned in glory in His
heav'nly Citadel.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Now our heav'nly Aaron enters,
with His blood, within the veil;
Joshua now is come to Canaan,
and the kings before Him quail;
Now He plants the tribes of Israel in their
promised resting place;
Now our great Elijah offers double portion
of His grace. 9. So at last,
when He appeareth, we from out our graves
may spring, With our youth renewed like
eagles, flocking round our Heav'nly King.
Caught up on the clouds of Heaven,
and may meet Him in the air,
Rise to realms where He is reigning,
and may reign for ever there.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
He has raised our human nature in the clouds
to God's right hand; There we sit in
heav'nly places, there with Him in glory
stand: Jesus reigns, adored by angels;
man with God is on the throne; Mighty Lord,
in Thine ascension we by faith behold our
own. 10. Glory be to God the Father,
Glory be to God the Son, Dying, ris'n,
ascending for us, who the heav'nly realm has
won; Glory to the Holy Spirit,
To One God in Persons Three;
Glory both in earth and Heaven, glory,
endless glory, be.

title: Silent Night
author: Josef Mohr
source: 'Stille Nacht' Franz Xaver Gruber, 1818.  Setting: "Concordia Kinderchöre", 1908

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Silent night, holy night, All is calm,
all is bright Round yon virgin mother and
Child. Holy Infant, so tender and mild,
Sleep in heavenly peace,
Sleep in heavenly peace.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Silent night, holy night,
Shepherds quake at the sight;
Glories stream from heaven afar,
Heavenly hosts sing Allelu ia!
Christ the Savior is born,
Christ the Savior is born!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Silent night, holy night, Son of God,
love's pure light; Radiant beams from Thy
holy face With the dawn of redeeming grace,
Jesus, Lord, at Thy birth, Jesus, Lord,
at Thy birth.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Silent night, holy night Wondrous star,
lend thy light; With the angels let us sing,
Alleluia to our King; Christ the Savior is
born, Christ the Savior is born!

title: Sing, O Sing, This Blessed Morn
author: Christopher Wordsworth

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Sing, O sing, this blessed morn,
Unto us a Child is born,
Unto us a Son is giv'n,
God Himself comes down from Heav'n.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Sing, O sing, this blessed morn,
Jesus Christ today is born.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Jesus Christ, the King of kings,
Maker of all worldly things,
Now descends from Heav'n to Earth,
To re-store us by His birth;

sections.label: Verse 3
Verse 4
Verse 5

title: Songs of Thankfulness and Praise
author: Christopher Wordsworth
source: 'St. George`s Windsor', George Job Elvey, 1858. Setting: "The Anglican Hymn Book", 1871

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Songs of thankfulness and praise, Jesus,
Lord, to Thee we raise,
Manifested by the star To the sages from
afar; Branch of royal David's stem In Thy
birth at Bethlehem; Anthems be to Thee
addressed, God in man made manifest.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Manifest at Jordan's stream, Prophet,
Priest, and King supreme; And at Cana,
wedding guest, In Thy Godhead manifest;
Manifest in pow'r divine,
Changing water into wine;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Manifest in making whole Palsied limbs and
fainting soul; Manifest in valiant fight,
Quelling all the devil's might;
Manifest in gracious will,
Ever bringing good from ill;
Anthems be to Thee addressed,
God in man made manifest.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Sun and moon shall darkened be,
Stars shall fall, the heav'ns shall flee,
Christ will then like lightning shine,
All will see His glorious sign:
All will then the trumpet hear;
All will see the Judge appear;
Thou by all wilt be confessed,
God in man made manifest.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Grant us grace to see Thee, Lord,
Mirrored in Thy holy Word;
May we imitate Thee now, And be pure,
as pure art Thou; That we like to Thee may
be At Thy great Epiphany;
And may praise Thee, ever blest,
God in man made manifest.

title: Souls of Men! Why Will Ye Scatter
author: Frederick William Faber
source: 'In Babilone' traditional Dutch found in "Oude en Nieuwe Hollantse Boerenlities en Contradansen", 1710

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Souls of men! why will ye scatter Like a
crowd of frightened sheep? Foolish hearts!
why will ye wander From a love so true and
deep? Was there ever kinder shepherd Half so
gentle, half so sweet,
As the Savior who would have us Come and
gather round His feet?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It is God: His love looks mighty,
But is mighti'r than it seems;
'Tis our Father: and His fondness Goes far
out beyond our dreams.
There's a wideness in God's mercy,
Like the wideness of the sea;
There's a kindness in His justice,
Which is more than liberty.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There is no place where earth's sorrows Are
more felt than up in Heav'n;
There is no place where earth's failings
Have such wondrous judgment giv'n.
There is welcome for the sinner,
Grace poured out as in a flood There is
mercy with the Savior;
There is healing in His blood.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
There is grace enough for thousands Of new
worlds as great as this;
There is room for fresh creations In that
upper home of bliss. For the love of God is
broader Than the measure of man's mind;
And the heart of the Eternal Is most
wonderfully kind.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
There is plentiful redemption In Christ's
blood that has been shed;
There is joy for all the members In the
sorrows of the Head. Not just all we owe to
Jesus; It is something more than all;
Greater good because of evil,
Larger mercy through the fall.

title: Stricken, Smitten, and Afflicted
author: Thomas Kelly
source: 'O Mein Jesu, Ich Muss Sterben' or 'Wo Ist Jesus, Mein Verlangen'  from Geistliches Volkslied, 1850

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Stricken, smitten, and afflicted,
See Him dying on the tree!
'Tis the Christ by man rejected; Yes,
my soul, 'tis He, 'tis He!
'Tis the long expected prophet, David's Son,
yet David's Lord; Proofs I see sufficient of
it: 'Tis a true and faithful Word.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Tell me, ye who hear Him groaning,
Was there ever grief like His?
Friends through fear His cause disowning,
Foes insulting his distress:
Many hands were raised to wound Him,
None would interpose to save;
But the deepest stroke that pierced Him Was
the stroke that Justice gave.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Ye who think of sin but lightly,
Nor suppose the evil great,
Here may view its nature rightly,
Here its guilt may estimate.
Mark the Sacrifice appointed!
See Who bears the awful load! 'Tis the Word,
the Lord's Anointed, Son of Man,
and Son of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Here we have a firm foundation,
Here the refuge of the lost.
Christ the Rock of our salvation,
Christ the Name of which we boast.
Lamb of God for sinners wounded!
Sacrifice to cancel guilt!
None shall ever be confounded Who on Him
their hope have built.

title: Take My Life And Let It Be
author: Frances R. Havergal

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Take my hands, and let them move at the
impulse of Thy love. Take my feet,
and let them be swift and beautiful for
Thee.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Take my voice, and let me sing always, only,
for my King. Take my lips,
and let them be filled with messages from
Thee.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Take my silver and my gold;
not a mite would I withhold.
Take my intellect, and use every pow'r as
Thou shalt choose.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Take my will, and make it Thine;
it shall be no longer mine. Take my heart,
it is Thine own; it shall be Thy royal
throne.

title: Take Thou My Hand and Lead Me
author: Julie Katharina von Hausmann
source: 'So Nimm Denn Meine Hände' Friedrich Silcher, 1842.  Setting: Donna Snell, circa 1975

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Take Thou my hand, and lead me o'er life's
rough way, with Heav'nly Manna feed me from
day to day. Alone my footsteps falter and
straggle wide, Lord who my life canst alter
be Thou my guide.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Take Thou my heart and hide it in folds of
grace Though pain or woe betide it to know
Thy face Draw, Lord, of Thy good pleasure
Thy child to Thee, And grant me faith's full
measure though naught I see.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Though oft I think Thou hidest Thy wondrous
might, Still to my goal Thou guidest me
through dark night, Take, then,
my hands and lead me till life is o'er,
With heav'nly manna feed me forevermore.

title: That Men a godly Life Might Live
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Dies sind die heil`gen zehu Gebot' or 'In Gottes Namen fahren wir' circa

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
That man a godly life might live,
God did these ten com mandments give By His
true servant Moses, high Upon the mount
Sinai. Have mercy, Lord.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I am thy God and Lord alone,
No other God be sides Me own;
On My great mercy venture thee,
With all thy heart love thou Me.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
By idle word and speech profane Take not My
holy Name in vain; And praise not aught as
good and true But what God doth say and do.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Hallow the day which God hath blest,
That thou and all thy house may rest;
Keep hand and heart from labor free,
That God may so work in thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Give to thy parents honor due,
Be dutiful and loving too;
And help them when their strength decays So
shalt thou have length of days.

title: The Advent of Our God
author: Charles Coffin
source: 'St. Thomas' Aaron Williams, 1770

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The advent of our God Shall be our theme for
prayer Come, let us meet him on the road And
place for Him prepare.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The everlasting Son Incarnate stoops to be,
Himself the servant's form puts on To set
His people free.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Come, Zion's daughter,
rise To meet your lowly King,
Nor let your faithless heart despise The
peace He comes to bring.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
As judge, on clouds of light,
He soon will come again And all His
scattered saints unite With Him on high to
reign.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Before the dawning day Let sin be put to
flight; No longer let the law hold sway,
But walk in freedom's light.

title: The Apostle Looked and Heard a Voice
author: Anthony Robertson

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Th'Apostle looked and heard a voice,
He saw a Lamb as had been slain;
As angels bowed and saints gave praise These
words were heard in their refrain.
"There'll be no war or foe to fight,
No searing sun, no dread of night;
No more distress, no more restraint,
No more be weak, no more feel faint.
No more be weak, no more feel faint.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They sigh no more, gone are their fears,
No crying make, shed no more tears;
They grow not old, sense no more loss,
Gone are their doubts and all their dross.
There'll be no sin and no more stain,
Unknown is sickness, gone is pain;
The death of death, no more the hearse,
The end of grief, the end of curse.
The end of grief, the end of curse."

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
These words are spoken faithfully, Alpha,
Omega, Lord is He; For all is done and done
for all, For all who come, for all who call.
Come see His face, His hands, His feet,
Come quench your thirst, partake the Feast,
Come enter in while still you may,
Then Jesus bring Eternal Day.
Then Jesus bring Eternal Day.

title: The Bridegroom Soon Will Call Us
author: Johann Walther
source: 'Act Gott Vom Himmelreiche' or 'Ich will ein Neues Singen' or 'Praetorius 7' from Musae Sionae

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Bridegroom soon will call us, Come,
all ye wedding guests!
May not His voice appall us,
While slumber binds our breasts;
May all our lamps be burning,
And oil be found in store, That we,
with Him returning, May open find the door.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There shall we see delighted Our dear
Redeemer's face, Who leads our souls
benighted To glory by His grace;
The patriarchs shall meet us,
The prophets' holy band, Apostles, martyrs,
greet us In that celestial land.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
They will not blush to own us As brothers,
sisters dear, Love ever will be shown us
When we with them appear;
We all shall come before Him,
Who for us Man became,
As Lord and God adore Him,
And ever bless His Name.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Our Father, rich in blessing,
Will give us crowns of gold And,
to His bosom pressing,
Impart a bliss untold,
Will welcome with embraces Of never ending
love, And deck us with His graces In
blissful realms above.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In yonder home shall never Be silent music's
voice; With hearts and lips forever We shall
in God rejoice; The angels shall adore Him,
All saints shall sing His praise,
And bring with joy before Him Their sweetest
heav'nly lays.

title: The Church's One Foundation
author: Samuel John Stone

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Church's one foundation Is Jesus Christ
her Lord, She is His new creation By water
and the Word. From heav'n He came and sought
her To be His holy bride;
With His own blood He bought her And for her
life He died.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
She is from every nation,
Yet one o'er all the earth;
Her charter of salvation, One Lord,
one faith, one birth; One holy Name she
blesses, Partakes one holy food,
And to one hope she presses,
With every grace endued.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The Church shall never perish!
Her dear Lord to defend, To guide, sustain,
and cherish, Is with her to the end:
Though there be those who hate her,
And false sons in her pale,
Against or foe or traitor She ever shall
prevail.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Though with a scornful wonder Men see her
sore oppressed, By schisms rent asunder,
By heresies distressed:
Yet saints their watch are keeping,
Their cry goes up, 'How long?' And soon the
night of weeping Shall be the morn of song!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
'Mid toil and tribulation,
And tumult of her war,
She waits the consummation Of peace
forevermore; Till, with the vision glorious,
Her longing eyes are blest,
And the great Church victorious Shall be the
Church at rest.

title: The Cloud Received Christ From Their Sight
author: Brian J. Dumont, 09 Dec
source: public domain.  This score is a part of the Open Hymnal Project, 2009 Revision

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The cloud received Christ from their sight.
They stood, their mouths agape.
Reminded of the things He taught His people
still do wait.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The cloud kept safe God's people as Through
the dry sea they trod,
And led them through the wilderness;
They truly walked with God!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
On Sinai's height the cloud did rest To make
a home below. The Ark first then His written
Word His presence now would show.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Appearing on the mercy seat within the
inmost place, the Temple showed God's
promises to save our fallen race.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
On mountain high Christ's face did shine
like sun, a blazing light.
The cloud once more appeared on earth a
truly fearful sight.

title: The Comforter Has Come
author: Frank Bottome
source: 'The Comforter Has Come' William J. Kirkpatrick, 1890.  Setting: "Pentecostal Hymns, No. 2", 1898

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
O spread the tidings 'round,
wherever man is found,
Wher ever human hearts and human woes
abound; Let ev'ry Christian tongue proclaim
the joyful sound: The Comforter has come!

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
The Comforter has come,
The Comforter has come!
The Holy Ghost from heav'n,
The Father's promise giv'n;
O spread the tidings 'round,
Wherever man is found:
The Comforter has come!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The long, long night is past,
the morning breaks at last,
And hush'd the dreadful wail and fury of the
blast, As o'er the golden hills the day
advances fast! The Comforter has come!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lo, the great King of kings,
with healing in His wings,
To ev'ry captive soul a full deliv'rance
brings; And thro' the vacant cells the song
of triumph rings; The Comforter has come!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O boundless love divine!
how shall this tongue of mine To wond'ring
mortals tell the matchless grace divine;
That I, a child of hell,
should in His image shine!
The Comforter has come!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Sing, till the echoes fly above the vaulted
sky, And all the saints above to all below
reply, In strains of endless love the song
that ne'er will die: The Comforter has come!

title: The Day is Surely Drawing Near
author: Bartholomäus Ringwaldt
source: 'Es ist Gewisslich an der Zeit' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The day is surely drawing near,
When God's Son, the Anointed,
Shall with great majesty appear,
As Judge of all appointed.
All mirth and laughter then shall cease When
flames on flames will still increase,
As Scripture truly teacheth.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
A trumpet loud shall then resound,
And all the earth be shaken;
Then all who in their graves are found Shall
from their sleep awaken.
But all that live shall in that hour,
By the Almighty's boundless pow'r Be changed
at His commanding.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A book is opened then to all,
A record truly telling What each hath done,
both great and small, When he on earth was
dwelling; And every heart be clearly seen,
And all be known as they have been,
In thoughts and words and actions.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Then woe to those who scorned the Lord,
And sought but carnal pleasures,
Who here despised His precious Word,
And loved their earthly treasures!
With shame and trembling they will stand,
And at the Judge's stern command To Satan be
delivered.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
O Jesus, who my debt didst pay And for my
sin wast smitten Within the Book of Life,
oh, may My name be also written!
I will not doubt; I trust in Thee,
From Satan Thou hast made me free And from
all condemnation.

title: The First Noel
author: Traditional English carol, possibly dating from as early as the 13th Century
source: 'The First Noel' Traditional English carol, possibly dating from as early as the 13th Century

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The first Noel the angel did say Was to
certain poor shepherds in fields as they
lay; In fields where they lay tending their
sheep, On a cold winter's night that was so
deep.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Noel, Noel, Noel, Noel,
Born is the King of Israel.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
They lookèd up and saw a star Shining in the
east, beyond them far;
And to the earth it gave great light,
And so it continued both day and night.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
And by the light of that same star Three
Wise Men came from country far;
To seek for a King was their intent,
And to follow the star wherever it went.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
This star drew nigh to the northwest,
Over Bethlehem it took its rest;
And there it did both stop and stay,
Right over the place where Jesus lay.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then did they know assuredly Within that
house the King did lie;
One entered it them for to see,
And found the Babe in poverty.

title: The Galilean Fishers Toil
author: Christopher Wordsworth
source: 'Old 137th' or 'Norwich' from Day's Psalter, 1563.  Setting: "The Holy Year", 1865

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Galilean fishers toil all night,
and nothing take; But Jesus comes,a wondrous
spoil is lifted from the lake. Lord,
when our labors are in vain and vain the
help of men, When fruitless is our care and
pain, Come blessed Jesus then!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The night is dark, the surges fill the bark,
the wild winds roar; But Jesus comes and all
is still,the ship is at the shore. O Lord,
when storms around us howl,
and all is dark and drear,
In all the tempests of the soul,
O blessed Jesus hear.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
A frail one, thrice denying Thee saw mercy
in Thine eyes, The penitent upon the tree
was borne to Paradise.
In hours of sin and deep distress o show us,
Lord, Thy Face, In penitential loneliness,
O give us Jesus grace!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The faithful few retire in fear to their
closed upper room; But suddenly with joyful
cheer they see their Master come.
Lord come to us, unloose our bands and bid
our terrors cease, Lift over us Thy blessed
hands, Speak, holy Jesus Peace!

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
In days, when faith will scarce be found,
and wolves be in the fold,
When sin and sorrow will abound and charity
wax cold, Then hear Thy saints,
who to Thee pray to bring them to their
home, Hear when the Bride and Spirit say,
"Come, Blessed Jesus, Come!"

title: The God of Abraham Praise
author: Daniel ben Judah, circa
source: 'Yigdal' or 'Leoni' Traditional Hebrew. Setting: Meyer Lyon, 1780

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The God of Abr'ham praise,
Who reigns enthroned above;
Ancient of everlasting days,
and God of Love; Jehovah, great I AM!
by earth and Heav'n confessed;
I bow and bless the sacred Name forever
blessed.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The God of Abr'ham praise,
at Whose supreme command From earth I rise
and seek the joys at His right hand;
I all on earth forsake, its wisdom, fame,
and pow'r; And Him my only Portion make,
my Shield and Tow'r.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The God of Abr'ham praise,
Whose all sufficient grace Shall guide me
all my happy days, in all my ways.
He calls a worm His friend,
He calls Himself my God!
And He shall save me to the end,
thro' Jesus' blood.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He by Himself has sworn;
I on His oath depend, I shall,
on eagle wings upborne, to Heav'n ascend.
I shall behold His face;
I shall His pow'r adore,
And sing the wonders of His grace
forevermore.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Tho' nature's strength decay,
and earth and hell withstand,
To Canaan's bounds I urge my way,
at His command. The wat'ry deep I pass,
with Jesus in my view;
And thro' the howling wilderness my way
pursue.

title: The Gospel Shows The Father's Grace
author: Matthias Loy
source: 'Herr Jesu Christ, Dict Zu Uns Wend' from Cantionale Germanicum, Dresden, 1628

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Gospel shows the Father's grace,
Who sent his Son to save our race,
Proclaims how Jesus lived and died That man
might thus be justified.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
It sets the Lamb before our eyes,
Who made th'atoning sacrifice,
And calls the souls with guilt oppressed To
come and find eternal rest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
It brings the Savior's righteousness Our
souls to robe in royal dress;
From all our guilt it brings release And
gives the troubled conscience peace.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
It is the pow'r of God to save From sin and
Satan and the grave; It works the faith,
which firmly clings To all the treasures
which it brings.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
It bears to all the tidings glad And bids
their hearts no more be sad;
The heavy laden souls it cheers And banishes
their guilty fears.

title: The King Shall Come
author: Unknown author. Translated by John Brownlie
source: 'Consolation' or 'Morning Song' John Wyeth, 1813

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And light triumphant breaks;
When beauty gilds the eastern hills,
And life to joy awakes.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Not as of old a little child To bear,
and fight, and die, But crowned with glory
like the sun That lights the morning sky.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O brighter than the rising morn When He,
victorious, rose, And left the lonesome
place of death, Despite the rage of foes.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O brighter than that glorious morn Shall
this fair morning be, When Christ, our King,
in beauty comes, And we His face shall see.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The King shall come when morning dawns,
And earth's dark night is past;
O haste the rising of that morn,
The day that aye shall last.

title: The Law Of God Is Good And Wise
author: Matthias Loy

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The law of God is good and wise,
And sets His will before our eyes,
Shows us the way of right eousness,
And dooms to death when we transgress.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Its light of holiness imparts The know ledge
of our sinful hearts, That we may see our
lost estate And seek deliv'rance ere too
late.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To those who help in Christ have found And
would in works of love abound It shows what
deeds are His delight And should be done as
good and right.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
When men the offered help disdain And will
fully in sin remain, Its terror in their ear
resounds And keeps their wickedness in
bounds.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The law is good, but since the fall Its ho
liness condemns us all;
It dooms us for our sin to die And has no
pow'r to justify.

title: The Lily of the Valley
author: C. W. Fry
source: 'Salvation' or 'The Lily of the Valley' William S. Hays, 1881.  Setting: Ira D. Sankey, 1887

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I've found a friend in Jesus,
He's everything to me,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul;
The Lily of the Valley,
in Him alone I see All I need to cleanse and
make me fully whole. In sorrow He's my
comfort, in trouble He's my stay;
He tells me every care on Him to roll.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
He's the Lily In sorrow He's my comfort,
in trouble He's my stay;
He tells me every care on Him to roll.
He's the Lily of the Valley,
the Bright and Morning Star,
He's the fairest of ten thousand to my soul.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
He all my grief has taken,
and all my sorrows borne;
In temptation He's my strong and mighty
tow'r; I'll all for Him forsake now,
I'll all my idols tear From my heart for now
He keeps me by His pow'r.
Though all the world forsake me,
and Satan tempt me sore,
Through Jesus I shall safely reach the goal.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
He'll never, never leave me,
nor yet forsake me here,
So I live by faith and do His blessed will;
A wall of fire about me,
I've nothing now to fear,
With His manna He my hungry soul shall fill.
When crown'd at last in glory,
I'll see His blessed face,
Where rivers of delight shall ever roll.

title: The Lord's My Shepherd
author: Psalm 23 from the Scottish Psalter
source: 'Marosa' or 'Brother James` Air' James Leith Macbeth Bain, 1915, alt

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The Lord's my shepherd I'll not want,
He makes me down to lie In pastures green He
leadeth me The quiet waters by.
He leadeth me, He leadeth me,
The quiet waters by, In pastures green He
leadeth me The quiet waters by.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
My soul He doth restore again,
And me to walk doth make.
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;
His Own Name's sake, His Own Name's sake,
E'en for His Own Name's sake;
Within the paths of blessedness,
E'en for His Own Name's sake.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yea, though I walk in death's dark vale,
Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod And staff
me comfort still; I'll fear no ill,
I'll fear no ill, Yet will I fear no ill,
For Thou art with me, and Thy rod And staff
me comfort still.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
My table Thou hast furnished well In
presence of my foes; My head Thou dost with
oil anoint, And my cup overflows;
It overflows, It overflows,
And my cup overflows; My head Thou dost with
oil anoint, And my cup overflows.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Goodness and mercy all my days Will surely
follow me: And in my Father's heart always
My dwelling place shall be;
My dwelling place, My dwelling place,
My dwelling place shall be,
And in my Father's heart always My dwelling
place shall be.

title: The Lord's Prayer (new)
author: Brian L. Penney
source: 'Erfyniad' Welsh Hymn Melody.  Setting: David Evans, "Revised Church Hymnary", 1927

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Father in heaven, Your name we confess,
High and exalted in bright holiness;
O may Your kingdom come, Your will be done,
And may the earth and heav'n be joined as
one.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O Father, now our daily bread supply,
And grant forgiveness for iniquity;
May we forgive as we have been forgiv'n,
Our hearts with mercy filled,
as Yours in heav'n.

sections.label: Verse 3

title: The Love of God
author: Frederick Martin Lehman
source: 'The Love of God' Frederick Martin Lehman, 1917.  Setting: Claudia Lehman Mays, 1917

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The love of God is greater far Than tongue
or pen can ever tell, It goes beyond the
highest star, And reaches to the lowest
hell; The guilty pair, bowed down with care,
God gave His Son to win; His erring child,
He reconciled, And pardoned from his sin.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Oh love of God, how rich and pure!
How measureless and strong!
It shall forevermore endure,
The saints' and angels' song.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
Could we with ink the ocean fill,
And were the skies of parchment made,
Were every stalk on earth a quill And every
man a scribe by trade;
To write the love of God above Would drain
the ocean dry; Nor could the scroll contain
the whole, Tho' stretched from sky to sky.

title: The Mouth of Fools Doth God Confess
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Es spricht der Unweisen Mund' from Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524.  Setting: Michael Praetorius, 1610

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The mouth of fools doth God confess,
But while their lips draw nigh Him,
Their heart is full of wickedness,
And all their deeds deny Him.
Corrupt are they, and every one Abominable
works hath done; There is not one welldoer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The Lord looked down from his high tow'r On
all mankind below Him,
To see if any owned His pow'r,
And truly sought to know Him;
Who all their understanding bent To search
His holy Word, intent To do his will in
earnest.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
But none there was who walked with God,
For all aside had slidden,
Delusive paths of folly trod,
And followed lusts forbidden;
Not one there was who practiced good,
And yet they deemed, in haughty mood,
Their deeds must surely please Him.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
How long, by folly blindly led,
Will ye oppress the needy,
And eat my people up like bread?
So fierce are ye, and greedy!
In God they put no trust at all,
Nor will on Him in trouble call,
But be their own providers.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Therefore their heart is never still,
A falling leaf dismays them;
God is with him who doth His will,
Who trusts him and obeys Him;
But ye the poor man's hope despise,
And laugh at him, e'en when he cries,
That God is his sure comfort.

title: The Old Rugged Cross
author: George Bennard

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
On a hill far away stood an old rugged
cross, The emblem of suff'ring and shame;
And I love that old cross where the dearest
and best For a world of lost sinners was
slain.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
So I'll cherish the old rugged cross,
Till my trophies at last I lay down;
I will cling to the old rugged cross,
And exchange it some day for a crown.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O that old rugged cross,
so despised by the world,
Has a wondrous attraction for me;
For the dear Lamb of God left His glory
above To bear it to dark Calvary.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
In that old rugged cross,
stained with blood so divine,
A won drous beauty I see,
For 'twas on that old cross Jesus suffered
and died, To pardon and sanctify me.

sections.label: Verse 4

title: The People That in Darkness Sat
author: John Morison

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The people that in darkness sat A glorious
light have seen; The light has shined on
them who long In shades of death have been.
In shades of death have been.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
To hail Thee, Sun of Righteousness,
The gath'ring nations come;
They joy as when the reapers bear Their
harvest treasures home.
Their harvest treasures home.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For Thou their burden dost remove And break
the tyrant's rod As in the day when Midian
fell Be fore the sword of God.
Before the sword of God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To us a Child of hope is born,
To us a Son is giv'n, And on His shoulder
ever rests All pow'r in earth and heav'n.
All pow'r in earth and heav'n.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
His name shall be the Prince of Peace,
The Ever lasting Lord, The Wonderful,
the Counselor. The God by all adored.
The God by all adored.

title: The Star Proclaims the King is Here
author: Coelius Sedulius, c. 450. German version by M. Luther
source: 'Wo Gott Zum Haus' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The star proclaims the King is here; But,
Herod, why this senseless fear?
He takes no realms of earth away Who gives
the realms of heav'nly day.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The wiser Magi see from far And follow on
His guiding star; And led by light,
to light they press And by their gifts their
God confess.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Within the Jordan's crystal flood In
meekness stands the Lamb of God And,
sinless, sanctifies the wave,
Mankind from sin to cleanse and save.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
At Cana first His pow'r is shown;
His might the blushing waters own And,
changing as He speaks the word, Flow wine,
obedient to their Lord.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
All glory, Jesus, be to Thee For this Thy
glad epiphany; Whom with the Father we adore
And Holy Ghost forevermore.

title: The Strife Is O'er, The Battle Done
author: from Symphonia Sirenum Selectarum, Köln
source: 'Victory' or  'Palestrina' Giovanni P. da Palestrina, 1591

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
sections.text:
Alleluia, Alleluia, Alleluia. Alleluia,
Alleluia, Alleluia.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
On that third morn He rose again In glorious
majes ty to reign; O let us swell the joyful
strain. Alleluia!

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
Lord, by the stripes which wounded Thee,
From death's dread sting Thy servants free,
That we may live, and sing to Thee.
Alleluia!

title: The Winds and Billows Loudly Roar
author: Christopher Wordsworth
source: 'Consolation' or 'Morning Song' John Wyeth, 1813

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
The winds and billows loudly roar We
flounder in the deep Our bark is frail,
far off the shore, And Jesus is asleep.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
"Save us, we perish, Lord," they cry;
To Thee we fly for aid; "Awake!
awake!" they say; but why So faithless and
afraid?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
His head is pillow'd on the stern,
As Man He is asleep; As God He all things
does discern, And endless vigils keep.

sections.label: Verse 4
Verse 5
sections.text:
O ye, who in the Church's Bark O'er life's
rough ocean sail, When all around is drear
and dark, and human efforts fail,

title: There's a Great Day Coming
author: Will L. Thompson
source: 'Theres a Great Day Coming' Will L. Thompson, 1886.  Setting: "Alexander's Hymns No. 3", 1915

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
There's a great day coming,
A great day coming, There's a great day
coming by and by; When the saints and the
sinners shall be parted right and left,

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Are you ready for that day to come?
Are you ready? Are you ready?
Are you ready for the judgment day?
Are you ready? Are you ready?
For the judgment day?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
There's a bright day coming,
A bright day coming, There's a bright day
coming by and by; But its brightness shall
only come to them that love the Lord,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
There's a sad day coming, A sad day coming,
There's a sad day coming by and by;
When the sinner shall hear his doom,
"Depart, I know ye not,"

title: Thine Arm, O Lord, in Days of Old

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thine arm, O Lord, in days of old,
was strong to heal and save;
It triumphed o'er disease and death,
o'er darkness and the grave.
To Thee they went, the blind, the dumb,
the palsied and the lame,
The leper with his tainted life,
the sick with fevered frame.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
And lo! Thy touch brought life and health,
gave speech, and strength and sight;
And youth renewed and fear relieved owned
Thee, the Lord of light; And now, O Lord,
be near to bless, Almighty as of yore,
In crowded street, by restless couch,
as by Gennesaret's shore.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Be Thou our great Deliverer still,
Thou Lord of life and death;
Restore and quicken, soothe and bless,
with Thine almighty breath.
To hands that work and eyes that see,
give wisdom's heavenly lore,
That whole and sick, and weak and strong,
may praise Thee evermore.

title: Thou, Who at Thy First Eucharist
author: William H. Turton
source: 'Unde Et Memores' William Henry Monk, 1875

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Thou, who at Thy first Eucharist didst pray
That all Thy Church might be forever one,
Grant us at ev'ry Eucharist to say With
longing heart and soul,
"Thy will be done." O may we all one bread,
one body be, Through this blest sacrament of
unity.

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
sections.text:
We pray Thee too for wand'rers from Thy
fold; O bring them back,
good Shepherd of the sheep,
Back to the faith which saints believed of
old, Back to the Church which still that
faith doth keep; Soon may we all one bread,
one body be, Through this blest sacrament of
unity.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
So, Lord, at length when sacraments shall
cease, May we be one with all Thy Church
above, One with Thy saints in one unbroken
peace, One with Thy saints in one unbounded
love; More blessèd still,
in peace and love to be One with the Trinity
in unity.

title: Though in the Midst of Life We Be
author: v.1 Medieval sequence, vs 2,3 Martin Luther
source: 'Mitten wir im Leben Sind' Medieval sequence altered by Martin Luther

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Though in midst of life we be,
Snares of death surround us;
Where shall we for succor flee,
Lest our foes confound us? To Thee alone,
our Savior. We mourn our grievous sin which
hath Stirr'd the fire of Thy fierce wrath.
Savior! Thou eternal God! Save us, Lord,
from sinking In the deep and bitter flood.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Kyrie eleison. Holy and gracious God!
Holy and mighty God! Holy and allmerciful

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Whilst in midst of death we be,
Hell's grim jaws o'ertake us;
Who from such dis tress will free.
Who secure will make us? Thou only, Lord,
canst do it! It moves Thy tender heart to
see Our great sin and misery. Savior!
Thou eternal God! Let not hell dismay us
With its deep and burning flood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Into hell's fierce agony Sin doth headlong
drive us: Where shall we for succor flee,
Who, O, who will hide us? Thou only,
blessed Saviour. Thy precious blood was shed
to win Peace and pardon for our sin. Savior!
Let us not, we pray, From the true faith's
comfort Fall in our last need away.

title: Through the Night of Doubt and Sorrow
author: Bernhardt S. Ingemann
source: 'Rex Gloriae' Henry Thomas Smart, 1868

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Through the night of doubt and sorrow Onward
goes the pilgrim band,
Singing songs of expectation,
Marching to the Promised Land.
Clear before us through the darkness Gleams
and burns the guiding light:
Brother clasps the hand of brother,
Stepping fearless through the night.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
One the light of God's own presence,
O'er His ransomed people shed,
Chasing far the gloom and terror,
Bright'ning all the path we tread:
One the object of our journey,
One the faith which never tires,
One the earnest looking forward,
One the hope our God inspires.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
One the strain that lips of thousands Lift
as from the heart of one; One the conflict,
one the peril One the march in God begun:
One the gladness of rejoicing On the far
eternal shore, Where the One Almighty Father
Reigns in love for evermore.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Onward, therefore, pilgrim brothers, Onward,
with the cross our aid! Bear its shame,
and fight its battle, Till we rest beneath
its shade. Soon shall come the great
awaking, Soon the rending of the tomb;
Then the scatt'ring of all shadows,
And the end of toil and gloom.

title: Tis Good, Lord, To Be Here
author: Joseph Armitage Robinson
source: 'Potsdam' adapted from Johann Sebastian Bach, 1750, by John Goss, 1854. Setting: John Goss, 1854

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Tis good, Lord, to be here,
Thy glory fills the night;
Thy face and garments, like the sun,
Shine with unborrowed light.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
'Tis good, Lord, to be here,
Thy beauty to behold Where Moses and Elijah
stand, Thy messengers of old.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Fulfiller of the past,
Promise of things to be,
We hail Thy body glorified And our
redemption see.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Before we taste of death,
We see Thy Kingdom come;
We fain would hold the vision bright And
make this hill our home.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
'Tis good, Lord, to be here.
Yet we may not remain;
But since Thou bidst us leave the mount,
Come with us to the plain.

title: To Avert From Men God's Wrath
author: Latin c
source: 'Gethsemane' or 'Petra' Richard Redhead, 1853

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To avert from men God's wrath Jesus suffered
in our stead; By an ignominious death He a
full atonement made; And by His most
precious blood, Brought us, sinners,
nigh to God.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That we never should forget This great Love
on us bestowed, He gave us His flesh to eat,
and to drink His precious blood;
All who sick and needy are May receive in
Him a share.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Hither each afflicted soul May repair,
though filled with grief; To the sick,
not to the whole, the Physician brings
relief; Fear not, therefore, but draw nigh,
Christ will all your wants supply.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He who in selfrighteousness Fixes any hope
or stay, Has not on a wedding dress,
And with shame is sent away; To the hungry,
weary heart, He will food and rest impart.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
But examine first your case,
Whether you be in the faith;
Do you long for pard'ning grace?
Is your only hope His death? Then,
howe'er your soul's oppressed, Come,
you are a worthy guest.

title: To God Be The Glory
author: Fanny Crosby

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To God be the glory, great things He has
done; So loved He the world that He gave us
His Son Who yielded His life an a tonement
for sin, And opened the life gate that all
may go in.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord,
Let the earth hear His voice!
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord,
Let the people rejoice!
O come to the Father, through Jesus the Son,
And give Him the glory,
great things He has done.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
O perfect redemption, the purchase of blood,
To every believer the promise of God;
The vilest offender who truly believes,
That moment from Jesus a pardon receives.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Great things He has taught us,
great things He has done,
And great our rejoicing through Jesus the
Son; But purer, and higher,
and greater will be Our wonder,
our transport, when Jesus we see.

title: To Jordan Came Our Lord, The Christ
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Christ, Unser Herr' Johann Walter, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To Jordan came our Lord the Christ,
To do God's pleasure willing,
And there was by Saint John baptized,
All righteousness fulfilling;
There did He consecrate a bath To wash away
transgression, And quench the bitterness of
death By His own blood and passion;
He would a new life give us.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
So hear ye all, and well perceive What God
doth call baptism, And what a Christian
should believe Who error shuns and schism:
That we should water use,
the Lord Declareth it His pleasure;
Not simple water, but the Word And Spirit
without measure; He is the true Baptizer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
To show us this, He hath His Word With signs
and symbols given; On Jordan's banks was
plainly heard The Father's voice from
Heaven: "This is My wellbeloved Son,
In whom My soul delighteth; Hear Him." Yea,
hear Him e very one Whom He Himself
inviteth, Hear and obey His teaching.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
In tender manhood Jesus straight To holy
Jordan wendeth; The Holy Ghost from Heaven's
gate In dovelike shape descendeth;
That thus the truth be not denied,
Nor should our faith e'er waver,
That the Three Persons all preside,
At baptism's holy laver,
And dwell with the believer.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Thus Jesus His disciples sent:
Go teach ye every nation,
That lost in sin they must repent;
And flee from condemnation:
He that be lieves and is baptized,
Obtains a mighty blessing; A newborn man,
no more he dies, Eternal life possessing,
A joyful heir of Heaven.

title: To Shepherds As They Watched By Night
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Vom Himmel Hoch' traditional German from Schumann's Geistliche Lieder, Leipzig, 1539

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
To shepherds as they watched by night
Appeared a host of angels bright;
Behold the tender Babe, they said,
In yonder lowly manger laid.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
At Bethlehem, in David's town,
As Micah did of old make known;
'Tis Jesus Christ, your Lord and King,
Who doth to all salvation bring.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Oh, then rejoice that through His Son God is
with sinners now at one;
Made like yourselves of flesh and blood,
Your Brother is th'eternal God.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
What harm can sin and death then do?
The true God now abides with you.
Let hell and Satan rage and chafe,
Christ is your Brother ye are safe.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Not one He will or can forsake Who Him his
confidence doth make. Let all his wiles the
Tempter try, You may his utmost pow'rs defy.

title: Today Thy Mercy Calls Me
author: Oswald Allen
source: 'Anthes' Friedrich K. Anthes, 1847.  Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Today Thy mercy calls me to wash away my
sin; However great my trespass,
whate'er I may have been;
However long from mercy I may have turned
away, Thy blood, O Christ, can wash me,
and make me clean today.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Today Thy gate is open,
and all who enter in Shall find a Father's
welcome, and pardon for their sin;
The past shall be forgotten,
a present joy be given;
A future grace be promised,
a glorious crown in Heav'n.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Today the Father calls me,
the Holy Spirit waits,
The blessèd angels gather around the
heav'nly gates; No question will be asked
me, how often I have come;
Although I oft have wandered,
it is my Father's home.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
O all embracing mercy, thou ever open door,
What shall I do without thee when heart and
eyes run o'er? When all things seem against
me, to drive me to despair,
I know one gate is open,
one ear will hear my prayer.

title: Twas In The Moon of Wintertime
author: Jean de Brébeuf
source: 'Huron Carol' or 'Jesous Ahatonia' or 'Une Jeunne Pucelle' traditional French, 1557

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
'Twas in the moon of wintertime,
When all the birds had fled,
That mighty Gitchi Manitou Sent angel choirs
instead; Before their light the stars grew
dim, And wand'ring hunters heard the hymn:

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Jesus your King is born, Jesus is born,
In excelsis gloria.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Within a lodge of broken bark The tender
babe was found, A ragged robe of rabbit skin
Enwrapped His beauty 'round;
But as the hunter braves drew nigh,
The angel song rang loud and high:

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
The earliest moon of wintertime Is not so
round and fair As was the ring of glory on
The helpless Infant there.
The chiefs from far before Him knelt With
gifts of fox and beaver pelt.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Oh children of the forest free,
Oh sons of Manitou, The holy Child of earth
and Heav'n Is born today for you.
Come kneel before the radiant Boy,
Who brings you beauty, peace and joy.

title: Under His Wings
author: William Orcutt Cushing
source: 'Under His Wings' Ira David Sankey, 1898

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Under His wings I am safely abiding,
Though the night deepens and tempests are
wild, Still I can trust Him;
I know He will keep me, He has redeemed me,
and I am His child.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Under His wings, under His wings,
Who from His love can sever?
Under His wings my soul shall abide,
Safely abide forever.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Under His wings, what a refuge in sorrow!
How the heart yearningly turns to His rest!
Often when earth has no balm for my healing,
There I find comfort, and there I am
blessed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Under His wings, oh, what precious
enjoyment! There will I hide till life's
trials are o'er; Sheltered, protected,
no evil can harm me, Resting in Jesus,
I'm safe evermore.

title: Wake, Awake, for Night Is Flying
author: Phillipp Nicolai
source: 'Wachet Auf' Phillip Nicolai, 1599.  Setting: "Common Service Book" (ULCA), 1917

sections.label: Verse 1
Verse 2
sections.text:
Zion hears the watchmen singing,
And all her heart with joy is springing;
She wakes, she rises from her gloom;
For her Lord comes down all glorious,
The strong in grace, in truth victorious.
Her Star is ris'n, her Light is come.
Ah come, Thou blessed One,
God's own beloved Son: Alleluia!
We follow till the halls we see Where Thou
hast bid us sup with Thee

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Now let all the heav'ns adore Thee,
And saints and angels sing before Thee,
With harp and cymbal's clearest tone;
Of one pearl each shining portal,
Where we are with the choir immortal Of
angels round Thy dazzling throne;
Nor eye hath seen, nor ear hath yet attained
to hear What there is ours,
but we rejoice and sing to Thee Our hymn of
joy eternally.

title: We All Believe in One True God
author: Medieval text expanded by Martin Luther
source: 'Wir Glauben all an Einen Gott, Schoepfer' or 'Apostolic Creed' Medieval tune altered

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We all believe in one true God,
Who created earth and heaven, The Father,
who to us in love Hath the right of children
given. He both soul and body feedeth,
All we need He doth provide us;
He through snares and perils leadeth,
Watching that no harm betide us.
He careth for us day and night,
All things are governed by His might.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
We all believe in Jesus Christ, His own Son,
our Lord, possessing An equal Godhead,
throne, and might, Source of every grace and
blessing. Born of Mary, virgin mother,
By the power of the Spirit, Made true man,
our elder Brother, That the lost might life
inherit; Was crucified for sinful men And
raised by God to life again.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We all confess the Holy Ghost,
Who sweet grace and comfort giveth And with
the Father and the Son In eternal glory
liveth; Who the Church, His own creation,
Keeps in uni ty of spirit.
Here forgiveness and salvation Daily come
through Jesus' merit. All flesh shall rise,
and we shall be In bliss with God eternally.

title: We Gather Together
author: Anonymous circa
source: 'Kremser' Traditional Dutch circa 1597.  Setting: Eduard Kremser, 1877

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We gather together to ask the Lord's
blessing; He chastens and hastens His will
to make known. The wicked oppressing now
cease from distressing.
Sing praises to His Name;
He forgets not His own.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Beside us to guide us,
our God with us joining, Ordaining,
maintaining His kingdom divine;
So from the beginning the fight we were
winning; Thou, Lord, were at our side,
all glory be Thine!

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
We all do extol Thee, Thou Leader
triumphant, And pray that Thou still our
Defender will be. Let Thy congregation
escape tribulation; Thy Name be ever
praised! O Lord, make us free!

title: We Give Thee But Thine Own
author: William W. How
source: 'Energy' William H. Monk (1823-1889). Setting: "Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book", 1931

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We give Thee but Thine own,
Whate'er the gift may be;
All that we have is Thine alone, A trust,
O Lord, from Thee.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
May we Thy bounties thus As stewards true
receive, And gladly, as Thou blessest us,
To Thee our firstfruits give.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
O hearts are bruised and dead,
And homes are bare and cold,
And lambs for whom the Shepherd bled Are
straying from the fold.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
To comfort and to bless,
To find a balm for woe,
To tend the lone and fatherless Is angels'
work below.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
The captive to release,
To God the lost to bring,
To teach the way of life and peace?
It is a Christlike thing.

title: We Know Thee Who Thou Art
author: William Bright
source: 'Sellinge' John Pyke Hullah, 1868. Setting: "Hymns Ancient and Modern", 1904

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We know Thee who Thou art, Lord Jesus,
Mary's Son; We know the yearnings of Thy
heart To end Thy work begun.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
That sacred fount of grace,
'Mid all the bliss of Heav'n,
Has joy whene'er we seek Thy face,
And kneel to be forgiv'n.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Brought home from ways perverse,
At peace Thine arms within, We pray Thee,
shield us from the curse Of falling back to
sin.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
We dare not ask to live Henceforth from
trials free; But oh! when next they tempt
us, give More strength to cling to Thee.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
We know Thee who Thou art,
Our own redeeming Lord; Be Thou by will,
and mind, and heart, Accepted, loved,
adored.

title: We Now Implore God the Holy Ghost
author: v.1 ancient German.  verses 2-4 Martin Luther
source: 'Nun Bitten wir den Heiligen Geist' ancient German found in Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
We now implore God the Holy Ghost For the
true faith, which we need the most,
That in our last moments He may befriend us
And, as homeward we journey, attend us.
Lord, have mercy.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Shine in our hearts, O most precious Light,
That we Jesus Christ may know aright,
Clinging to our Savior,
whose blood hath bought us.
Who again to our homeland hath brought us.
Lord, have mercy.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Thou sacred Love, grace on us bestow,
Set our hearts with heav'nly fire aglow That
with hearts u nited we love each other,
Of one mind, in peace with ev'ry brother.
Lord, have mercy!

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Thou highest Comfort in ev'ry need,
Grant that neither shame nor death we heed,
That e'en then our courage may never fail us
When the Foe shall accuse and assail us.
Lord, have mercy!

title: Were You There?
author: African-American Spiritual, before
source: 'Were You There' African-American Spiritual, before 1899.  Setting: attr. Charles Winfred Douglas, 1940

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?
Were you there when they crucified my Lord?

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Sometimes it causes me to tremble, tremble,
tremble.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Were you there when they nailed Him to the
tree? Were you there when they nailed Him to
the tree? Were you there when they nailed
Him to the tree?

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Were you there when they pierced Him in the
side? Were you there when they pierced Him
in the side? Oh! Were you there when they
pierced Him in the side?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Were you there when the sun refused to
shine? Were you there when the sun refused
to shine? Were you there when the sun
refused to shine?

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Were you there when they laid Him in the
tomb? Were you there when they laid Him in
the tomb? Were you there when they laid Him
in the tomb?

title: What A Friend We Have In Jesus
author: Joseph M. Scriven
source: 'untitled' Charles C. Converse, 1868.  Setting: "Book of hymns and tunes", 1874

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What a Friend we have in Jesus,
all our sins and griefs to bear!
What a privilege to carry everything to God
in prayer! O what peace we often forfeit,
O what needless pain we bear,
All because we do not carry everything to
God in prayer.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Have we trials and temptations?
Is there trouble anywhere?
We should never be discouraged;
take it to the Lord in prayer.
Can we find a friend so faithful who will
all our sorrows share?
Jesus knows our every weakness;
take it to the Lord in prayer.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Are we weak and heavy laden,
cumbered with a load of care?
Precious Savior, still our refuge,
take it to the Lord in prayer.
Do your friends despise, forsake you?
Take it to the Lord in prayer!
In His arms He'll take and shield you;
you will find a solace there.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Blessed Savior, Thou hast promised Thou wilt
all our burdens bear May we ever, Lord,
be bringing all to Thee in earnest prayer.
Soon in glory bright unclouded there will be
no need for prayer Rapture,
praise and endless worship will be our sweet
portion there.

title: What Child Is This?
author: William Chatterton Dix
source: 'Greensleeves' 16th Century English Traditional

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
What Child is this who,
laid to rest On Mary's lap is sleeping?
Whom angels greet with anthems sweet,
While shepherds watch are keeping? This,
this is Christ the King,
Whom shepherds guard and angels sing; Haste,
haste, to bring Him laud, The Babe,
the Son of Mary.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Why lies He in such mean estate,
Where ox and ass are feeding?
Good Christians, fear,
for sinners here The silent Word is
pleading. Nails, spear shall pierce Him
through, The cross be borne for me, for you.
Hail, hail the Word made flesh, The Babe,
the Son of Mary.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
So bring Him incense, gold and myrrh,
Come peasant, king to own Him;
The King of kings salvation brings,
Let loving hearts enthrone Him. Raise,
raise a song on high, The virgin sings her
lullaby. Joy, joy for Christ is born,
The Babe, the Son of Mary.

title: When I Survey the Wondrous Cross
author: Isaac Watts
source: 'Duke Street' John Hatton, 1793.  Setting: "Finest of the Wheat No. 3" Hymnal, 1904

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When I survey the wondrous cross On which
the Prince of Glory died,
My rich-est gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Forbid it, Lord, that I should boast,
Save in the death of Christ my God!
All the vain things that charm me most,
I sacrifice them to His blood.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
See from His head, His hands, His feet,
Sorrow and love flow mingled down!
Did e'er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
His dying crimson, like a robe,
Spreads o'er His body on the tree;
Then I am dead to all the globe,
And all the globe is dead to me.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were a present far too small;
Love so amazing, so divine, Demands my soul,
my life, my all.

title: When The Roll Is Called Up Yonder
author: James Milton Black
source: 'When The Roll Is Called Up Yonder' James Milton Black, 1893

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
When the trumpet of the Lord shall sound,
and time shall be no more,
And the morning breaks, eternal,
bright and fair; When the saved of earth
shall gather over on the other shore,
And the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll When the roll is called up
yonder, I'll be there,
When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll is called up is called up
yonder, I'll be there,
When the roll is called up yonder,
When the roll is called up yonder,
I'll be there.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
On that bright and cloudless morning when
the dead in Christ shall rise,
And the glory of His resurrection share;
When His chosen ones shall gather to their
home beyond the skies,

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Let us labor for the Master from the dawn
till setting sun, Let us talk of all His
wondrous love and care;
Then when all of life is over,
and our work on earth is done,

title: Where He Leads Me
author: Edward (or Ernest) William Blandy
source: 'Blandy' or 'Norris' attr. John Samuel Norris (1844-1907) or Philip Paul Bliss (1838-1876)

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
I can hear my Savior calling,
I can hear my Savior calling,
I can hear my Savior calling,
"Take thy cross and follow, follow Me."

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Where He leads me I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow,
Where He leads me I will follow;
I'll go with Him, with Him, all the way.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him through the garden,
I'll go with Him, with Him all the way.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him through the judgment,
I'll go with Him, with Him all the way.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
He will give me grace and glory,
He will give me grace and glory,
He will give me grace and glory,
And go with me, with me all the way.

title: While O'er Our Guilty Land, O Lord
author: verses 1-3, Samuel Davies
source: 'Federal Street' Henry K. Oliver, 1832

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
While o'er our guilty land, O Lord,
We view the terrors of Your sword,
O where can all the helpless fly?
To whom but You direct their cry?

sections.label: Verse 2
Verse 3
Verse 4
sections.text:
We are the old, the sick, the lame;
We blind and deaf cry Jesus' Name.
We plead Your mercy for His sake,
And trust that You will not forsake.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Christ is our only righteousness,
His death for us is our redress.
Your promise stronger than our sin;
Blot out O Lord what we have been.

title: Whiter Than Snow
author: James Nicholson
source: 'Whiter Than Snow' William Gustavus Fischer, 1872.  Setting: "Pentecostal Hymns, No. 2", 1898

sections.label: Verse 1
Chorus
Verse 2
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, look down from Thy throne in the
skies, And help me to make a complete
sacrifice; I give up myself,
and what ever I know, Now wash me and I
shall be whiter than snow.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, for this I most humbly entreat,
I wait, blessed Lord, at Thy crucified feet,
By faith, for my cleansing,
I see Thy blood flow, Now wash me and I
shall be whiter than snow.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Lord Jesus, Thou seest I patiently wait,
Come now, and with in me a new heart create;
To those who have sought Thee,
Thou never said'st ``No,'' Now wash me and I
shall be whiter than snow.

title: Wilt Thou, O Man, Live Happily
author: Martin Luther
source: 'Mensch, Willt du Leben Seligich' attr. Martin Luther. Found in Walter's Geistliche Gesangbüchlein, 1524

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Wilt thou, O man, live happily,
And dwell with God eternally,
The ten commandments keep,
for thus Our God Himself biddeth us.
Kyr' eleison!

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
I am the Lord and God!
take heed No other god doth thee mislead;
Thy heart shall trust alone in Me,
My kingdom then thou shalt be.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Honor My Name in word and deed,
And call on Me in time of need:
Hallow the Sabbath, that I may Work in thy
heart on that day.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
Obedient always, next to Me,
To father and to mother be; Kill no man:
even anger dread; Keep sacred thy marriage
bed.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Steal not, nor do thy neighbor wrong By
bearing wit ness with false tongue;
Thy neighbor's wife desire thou not,
Nor grudge him aught he hath got.

title: Within the Father's House
author: James Russell Woodford
source: 'Franconia' Johann Balthasar König, 1738.  Setting: William Henry Havergal, 1847

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Within the Father's house The Son hath found
His home; And to His temple suddenly The
Lord of Life hath come.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
The doctors of the law Gaze on the wondrous
child, And marvel at His gracious words Of
wisdom undefiled.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Yet not to them is giv'n The mighty truth to
know, To lift the fleshly veil which hides
Incarnate God below.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The secret of the Lord Escapes each human
eye, And faithful pond'ring hearts await The
full epiphany.

sections.label: Verse 5

title: Yet Before We See Your Plans
author: Brian J. Dumont

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
Yet before we see Your plans, Lord;
While the path is still unknown Bless us
Lord to shout Your praises,
May Your work through us be shown.

sections.label: Chorus
sections.text:
Give us faith to trust Your mercy,
Make us confident to be Called and holy as
Your Church who Shout and sing Your victory.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Marching round the walls of Jer'cho Went
Your trumpeted parade.
Celebrating Your great triumph E'en before
it was displayed.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
With four armies bearing on them King
Jehoshaphat would send First the band to
sing your praises, Thus Your glory to
extend.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
On that night before He died The Lord to You
would raise a hymn He would sing Your praise
and mercy E'en before the battle grim.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
And we lowly helpless few harassed and
fettered by our sin More than conquerors in
Christ for He did our salvation win.

title: You Parents Hear What Jesus Taught
author: Ludwig Helmbold (
source: 'Herr Jesu Christ, Dict Zu Uns Wend' from Cantionale Germanicum, Dresden, 1628

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
You parents, hear what Jesus taught When
little ones to him were brought:
Forbid them not, but heed my plea Permitting
them to come to me.

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Obey your Lord and let his truth Be taught
your children in their youth That they in
church and school may dwell And learn their
Savior's praise to tell.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
For if you love them as you ought,
To Christ your children will be brought.
If thus you place them in his care,
All in your family well shall fare.

title: You People Who Now Are Baptized
author: Paul Gerhardt
source: 'Es ist Gewisslich an der Zeit' from Klug's Geistliche Lieder, Wittenberg, 1533

sections.label: Verse 1
sections.text:
You people who now are baptized God's
gracious love sur rounds you.
By Christ's Name you're now recognized;
Pon der what happened to you:
Whose work was it which fashioned you,
Whose inborn nature that He slew,
When you first gained His promise?

sections.label: Verse 2
sections.text:
Before held in your mother's arm,
From your time of con ception,
Quite hostile to the Law's alarmsLet there
be no deception. A sinner born of sinner's
seed; Still God Himself for you would bleed,
He took on flesh to save you.

sections.label: Verse 3
sections.text:
Your soul and body turned within,
Sin filled you like a poison.
Concern for neighbor paperthin;
God's love was simply foreign.
Then raised by God the Lord of Life To glow
in His eternal Light Your robe of white is
gleaming.

sections.label: Verse 4
sections.text:
The majesty that terrifies Was all God's
presence brought you. Your fault you could
not rectify; An xiety consumed you.
A slave of sin and Satan held Trapped in a
prison bound for hell Death was your only
future.

sections.label: Verse 5
sections.text:
Then washed clean in this holy flood,
The water of Bap tism;
Instilled faith in Christ's holy blood
Brought to the Father's Kingdom,
Your heart rebuilt within your breast,
New nature filled with righteousness,
Your every sin forgiven!
